Chan Master Zhiguang of Fenghuang Mountain in Xijianzhou, successor to Chan Master Linxi Tuo of Yingzhou, was asked: "The myriad dharmas are fundamentally at rest; it is people themselves who create the clamor.
What are the myriad dharmas? The Master said: "Every land, every speck of dust. He was further asked: "When the numinous pine has no distinct color, what then? The Master—
He said, "This reveals the mind in the midst of the cold of winter. A monk asked, "What is the one volume of scripture for a student? The Master said, "Explaining causes and explaining effects.
He ascended the hall and said: "The autumn mountains are layered upon layer; the autumn waters are clear and still; the autumn wind is piercingly cold; the autumn moon stands tall and bright."
At this moment, leaning alone against the high tower, he clapped his hands and laughed several times in the breeze.
Chan Master Tong of Touzi in Shuzhou asked, "How was it before Bodhidharma had come? The Master said, "Fishermen’s songs resound on both banks.
The monk asked, "How is it after he has come? The Master said, "The great ocean surges with wind and waves. [A monk] asked, "Prajñā is a sūtra."
"Vajra" is a metaphor. A student came forward and requested, "I pray that the Master will grant me an instruction. The Master said, "A single blow accomplishes two things;

it covers and conceals what comes before. The monk said, "Thank you for the Master’s instruction. The Master asked, "How do you understand this? The monk replied, "A single blow accomplishes two things;
it covers and conceals what comes before. The Master said, "You are merely one who parrots words. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of 'the joint atop the solitary peak'?"
Cao Changsong asked, "The Master said: 'He can be the lord of the myriad phenomena, yet he does not wither with the four seasons.
Question: What is the Buddha-dharma here at your monastery? The Master said, "The eastern wall strikes the western wall. The Master added, "That was already the heart of an old woman."
Even so, it is not easy to realize. Consider this: before Bodhidharma had yet arrived, tell me, did [the Dharma] already exist here in this land?
If it did exist, what need was there for him to come here at all? Monk, how can you attempt to debate whether it exists or not?
Tell me, when did Bodhidharma come? And where has he gone now? If there were someone here who could attain awakening, I would grant that you have one eye of the patriarchs.
If you have not yet understood, you shall stand for long. He ascended the hall and said: "Morning after morning it is the same;
day after day it is identical. Even something new and marvelous cannot be brought forth. As for the emergence of the various sages..."
Come. Furthermore, I dare not deceive those seated above me. Why is this so? It is because you, who are seated above me, are a traveling monk (a *xingjiao ren*).
Now that we are gathered here together for a short while, it would already be an act of injustice toward all people.
Furthermore, if you continue to fluctuate between right and wrong, disputes will arise like a rising storm; it would be better to simply rest for now. Take care.
Nanyue Poyuan addressed Chan Master Zhen of Lantian County, who was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Rou.
[The student] asked: "What is the mind of the Great Sage of the Land of Chu? The Master said: "By whom was it transmitted?"
A visitor asked, "What is the white ox on the open ground? The Master said, "Do not let it eat the people's crops. The visitor asked, "What is the Dharma-preaching of the insentient?
The Master said, "Do you see the incense altar? The visitor asked, "What is the Gate of Non-duality? The Master said, [as before].
The Master said, "Even one is not it. Question: "What is the gate of Great Samādhi? The Master said, "Gathering firewood and selecting vegetables. Question:
"What are the traces of the ancients upon thousand-year-old rocks? The Master said, "They cannot be moved or altered.
Question: "What is it like when a stone contains jade? The Master said, "It ought to be so. Question: "What is it like when one seeks it but cannot find it? The Master said, "Use it."
“What do you seek? the Master asked. The monk said, “How can one attain it? The Master said, “When did you lose it? A monk asked, “What is it like before all Buddhas have appeared in the world?
The Master said, “I ask and you answer. The monk said, “What is it like after they have appeared in the world?
The Master said, “I ask and you answer. A monk asked, “What is the pivotal mechanism of the higher realm? The Master said, “It cannot be stepped upon. The monk said, “Not yet...”

[The Master asked: "Once you have stepped upon it, what then? The Teacher said: "It deceives people. The Teacher said: "A mountain is formed by relying on the first basketful of earth; a long journey depends upon the first step.
Upādhyāya, you just now came from the side of the hearth—is this the same as the first step, or is it different?
If you say they are the same, you do not understand 'non-transmigration. If you say they are different, you likewise do not understand 'non-transmigration. Upādhyāya.
How do you understand this? Do you understand yet? This place is not that place; that place is not this place.
Tell me, are they one place or two places? Are they shifting or non-shifting? Is it coming and going, or is it not coming and going?
If you can clarify this, then past and present will be as one; from beginning to end, it is naturally so. Moment by moment there is impermanence; mind after mind is eternally [empty].
Extinction. Thus it is said: "By observing the direction one knows where that which has departed has gone; yet that which departs does not arrive at a direction.
Upasaka, you have just now come in such a manner; now, please depart in such a manner. *Chan*.
Chan Master Kaixian Zhao of Mount Lu, a successor of Chan Master Piyun Zhiji of Shaoyou, asked:
"Regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school, I beg the Master to grant me an instruction. The Master said:
"When the white clouds are severed, one sees the bright moon. The monk said: "This is still a point of doubt for this student. The Master said: "When the yellow leaves fall, one hears [the wind]."
[The Master] was pounding clothes. A monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "Nine out of ten words may hit the mark, yet they are not as good as one silence.

The monk said, "If that is so, then at Shaolin he once sat facing a wall, and for a thousand ages his illustrious conduct has been spread abroad. The Master said, "As for your own portion, what do you make of it?
The monk said, "Facing each other in silence is a good news; there is no need to go further and ask Nanquan. The Master said, "Do not."
[The Master] disrupted the lineage. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "A single cold mountain stream; those who gain its strength surpass their descendants.
The monk asked, "How is it used? The Master said, "In pieces. He ascended the hall and said, "This is the regulation of the monastic community."
This is the ancestral style of the Buddhas of old: one inquiry, one request; one gruel, one meal. But tell me, what matter have you understood?

It is simply because the minds of all people do not rest and their thoughts do not abide. If you can rest where there is no resting, and be without thought where there is thought, you will naturally accord with the principle of non-arising.
To speak in such a manner would break the mouths of others. *Chan* (Investigate)!
Chan Master Tianbao of Jinling asked: "When the opportunity arises and one does not realize it, what then? The Master said: "Dull. The monk asked:
"After one has realized it, what then? The Master said: "Swift. A monk asked: "What is it like when white clouds embrace a secluded rock?
The Master said: "Not your realm. A monk asked: "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "Tearing it in half and making three. The monk said: "The student..."
[The monk] did not understand. The Master said, "A nose and a needle-case.

Chan Master Zongsheng of Liaoshan in Qianzhou, successor to Chan Master Xieqian of Letan Mountain in Hongzhou, asked: "What was the intent behind the ancients' 'wall-facing'? The Master said, "It was for..."
"You wish to ask? Ask. "How is it with the bright pearl within the robe? The Master said, "Take care to preserve it.
"How is it with the fundamental matter of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "Do not ask others. "How is it with the gate of liberation?"

The Master said, "Enter from this very place. He ascended the hall and said: "The sound of the bell is clear; the sound of the drum is resonant. Hearing them morning and evening, do not let your thoughts wander.
If you can realize this, it is a vain labor to seek another path. Do not say that this mountain monk has no skill—*tu!* (a shout of realization)."

The Tenth Generation from Chan Master Xing Si of Mount Qingyuan in Lilong, a Gate of Responding to Capacities;
Dharma Heir of Chan Master Guangzu of Zhimen in Suizhou.
Chan Master Mingjue of Zisheng Monastery on Xuedou Mountain in Mingzhou was named Chongxian. His surname was Li, and he was the ninth-generation descendant of Da Ji of Suizhou.
He was born on the eighth day of the fourth month in the fifth year of the Xingguo era. From the moment of his birth, he would close his eyes and appear as if asleep both morning and evening.
Even as a child, he was extraordinary; he took no pleasure in play, and whenever he saw a śramaṇa, he would pull at his robes with great joy.

He followed the Venerable Renxian of Puan Monastery for many years and entered the monastic order. After receiving full ordination, he took up his scroll at the lecture hall to investigate principles and exhaust the profound mysteries.
His interrogations were as swift as charging blades, and his eloquence was peerless; all recognized him as a vessel of the Dharma, and everyone pointed him toward a journey south.
Upon first arriving at Zhimen, he immediately posed this question: "If not a single thought arises, how can there be transgression? Zhimen called him forward, and the Master stepped near.
He immediately stepped forward. Baizhang struck him with his whisk and asked, "Do you understand? As the Master was about to respond, Baizhang struck him again. He attained sudden enlightenment;

his conceptual mind and intellectual calculations were cast off like a husk. Subsequently, he traveled through Jiang and Xiang, where his spiritual practice became even more prominent, and he was held in high esteem by the masters of the school.

The assembly of monastics was struck with awe and submission. He expounded the Dharma at Mount Dongting, where students gathered like clouds. The scholar-official Lord Zeng, admiring his virtue and reputation, summoned him to reside at Xuedou.

There he grandly opened the gate of the patriarchs and revealed the profound mysteries. Lord Li Zunxū, the Commandant of the Capital, specifically memorialized the throne for the bestowal of ceremonial robes upon him.
Soon thereafter, Lord Jia Changchao, the Palace Attendant, requested an honorific title for him. Consequently, the most eminent talents from all quarters [flocked to him].
He attended the Dharma assemblies; ascending the hall and entering the inner chamber, he was universally renowned for his mastery of the Way.

As his period of transformative influence drew to a close, one day while wandering the mountains and surveying the surroundings, he said to his attendant, "When shall we return here again? The attendant pleaded for a verse on the Path. The Master said:

Throughout his life, he had only been concerned that his speech was too much. On the following day, he took out his staff, sandals, robes, and alms bowl, distributing them among his disciples, and said, "On the seventh day of the seventh month, we shall meet again.
Having washed himself and adjusted his robes, he passed away with his head pointing north.
Yunmen’s prophecy stated, "Two hundred years hence, my Way shall be manifested once more"; this refers to the Master’s name. How could it have been in vain?

On the day of opening the hall, he looked toward the assembly from before the Dharma seat and said, "If we speak of seeing one another according to the fundamental portion, there is no necessity for ascending the high Dharma seat.
He then pointed with his hand and said, "The immeasurable Buddha-lands appear all at once;
each of you should observe them closely. Should you fail to know their limits, you will inevitably be muddying the waters. Thereupon, he ascended the seat.
After the presiding monk had struck the gavel, a monk was just coming out. The Master called him back and said: "The Tathāgata’s Treasury of the True Dharma Eye rests entirely upon this day.
If it is let loose, even tiles and pebbles will emit light; if it is held fast, even genuine gold loses its luster. The authority is in my hands;
killing or giving life is decided as the occasion demands. If there is anyone who is a true adept, let us bear witness together. He then asked: "Having left the ancestral seat of Cuifeng..."
Having arrived at the Snow Peak (Xuedou) Dharma site, [the monk] asked, "Is it one? Is it two? The Master said, "If a horse does not have the thousand-li stride, its wind-chasing is in vain.
The monk said, "In that case, the clouds disperse and every house has the moon. The Master said, "A dragon's head and a snake's tail.
The monk asked, "Deshan and Linji have already manifested their staffs and shouts; how do you, Master, benefit people? The Master said, "I let one move pass by. As the monk hesitated, the Master—

[The Master] gave a shout. The monk said, “If that is so, then there must be something else. The Master said, “If you do not truly strike the tiger, your efforts will be in vain and your arrows will only exhaust themselves.
A monk asked, “When the great Dharma conch is blown and the great Dharma drum is struck, and the high officials of the court attend the assembly—what is it like then?
The Master said, “The pure breeze has not yet ceased. The monk said, “If that is so, then I have met the Master. The Master said, “Once a word has been spoken, it cannot be recalled.”
"Four horses are hard to overtake.
The Master again looked toward the great assembly and said, "With humans and devas gathered here in such numbers, what matter should we together clarify?

How can one merely engage in the reciprocal roles of host and guest, racing back and forth with questions and answers, and take that to be the vehicle of our school? This gate is vast and expansive; its majestic power is sovereign and its brilliance soars aloft."

A monk asked, "What is the primary truth (paramārtha-satya)? The Master said, "A barbarian reading the Han Annals. He ascended the hall [to give a formal discourse].
It is said: Whenever there is an occasion for teaching, one must understand its fundamental principle. If one understands its fundamental principle, there is neither "is" nor "is not.
When it is applied, waves surge and the sea boils; the true essence is fully utilized in its operation. When it is embodied, the mirror is still and the water is clear;
every action follows conditions while returning to quiescence. Now tell me: in the Tuṣita Heaven palace, how many people walk? How many people sit? If you can discern this point—

Clear and turbid. You people of the four quarters—east, west, south, and north—are like clouds or cranes; if you do not understand this, you will never have the day when you have worn through your straw sandals.
*Chan.* Entering the hall, he said: "Yunmen drew back his gaze; the patch-robed monks were at a loss. The moon has set and the stars have sunk;
vast and boundless it is. Śākyamuni guards the pass; Dīpaṃkara returns the way. Wind and clouds pervade the earth—*Sili*."
"Su-lu. He ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said: "Where the precipice is wiped away, ghosts and spirits wail; as clouds emerge, he points directly to Mount Gao.

Resting it crosswise upon his knee, it is like a strange whetting-stone for the sword—dare we wait for those from all quarters to don their woolen robes? With a single strike, he descended from the seat.
Zen Master Wenyu of Dayang Mountain in Yingzhou, successor to Zen Master Kefa Xian of Jiangling Prefecture, was asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master replied: "The forehead is broad and level."
The monk said, "In that case, there is a share in gazing upon and paying homage. The Master said, "His nose is upturned, round, and long.
Upāsaka Rìfāng asked, "What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth? The Master raised his staff. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that cuts off all streams?
The Master held his staff horizontally across his body. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that follows the waves and drifts with the current? The Master...
"A phrase of waves. The Master threw down his staff. The monk said, "Beyond the three phrases, please speak, Master. The Master then rose and praised Zen Master Xianzhen:
"His pure deportment was lean, yet worthy of being gazed upon and revered; yet to look up at it is not to see the person. His wondrous brushwork depicted him, yet it can be compared and imaged;
yet to image him is not to see the true person. Neither the person nor the true form—like the full autumn moon in its orb. To have words is to lack flavor."
Within the midst of it, as before, one seeks and yet seeks. In the immediate response, whether hidden or manifest, there is the slightest deviation, like a hair’s breadth.
The golden crow and the white ox are like a swift wind and a clap of thunder.

Compiled by the Dharma-transmitting Chan Master Foguo, Abbot of Fayun Chan Temple in Dongjing (Subject) Weibai, during the Song Dynasty.
The Gate of Responding to Capacities:
Chan Master Huairang of Mount Nanyue,
the eleventh-generation successor of Chan Master Shanzhao of the Imperial Prince’s Chan Monastery in Fenzhou.
Chan Master Ciming of Xinghua Chan Monastery in Tanzhou was named Chuyuan. His secular surname was Li, and he was a native of Quanzhou.

From his childhood, he possessed divine insight that far surpassed that of others. He left home to become a monk and received full ordination at Yinjing Temple; thereafter, he gathered his robes and traveled to various regions.
Having traveled extensively to consult various spiritual friends, he finally visited Chan Master Fenyang Shanzhao.
Shanzhao had previously said to his head seat, "Before long, a monk of extraordinary character will arrive to uphold my Way. One day, Shanzhao led the head seat on a mountain excursion.
The head seat asked, "Where are you going? Shanzhao replied, "To receive the attendant. The head seat remarked, "Why do you act so perversely, Old Monk? Shanzhao said, "Just..."

He went out to wander in the mountains. As he was walking through the woods, he encountered the Master arriving. [The Master] said, "This is truly my attendant. He immediately returned with him and had a chamber built for him.
With a single word, they reached profound spiritual resonance, and [the disciple] penetrated the very source of the mind. He served the Master, holding his towel and pitcher, for twelve years.
Later, when he wished to take his leave, Huizhao said to him, "I have long known that you are a vessel for the Dharma. I—"
At the place of my late master at Shoushan, I personally realized the King of Samādhis and thoroughly investigated its essential core; I now entrust this to you.

You must maintain it well and proceed to the south, where you shall greatly propagate my Way. Having received these instructions, the Master went directly to the Dharma seat of Chan Master Baoshou at Dongshan in Junzhou, Jiangxi.
He sat facing a wall all day long, which caused Baoshou to regard him with wonder. Descending from his seat, Baoshou asked:
"How was the intent behind Bodhidharma’s nine years of facing the wall? The Master replied, "An empty stomach and a haughty mind.
The following day, Bao ascended the seat and appointed the Master as his head attendant. The Master spent forty years in the world, presiding over five monasteries.
Li Hou Zunxu, the Commandery Governor, memorialized to the throne and was granted robes of honor and a posthumous title for the Master.
On the day of opening the hall, after the head monk had finished striking the mallet, the Master said: "Do you understand?

In the past, at the assembly on Vulture Peak, before a multitude of one hundred thousand, the Great Being Mañjuśrī took that final strike of the mallet as the phrase of the primary meaning (*paramārtha*).
Today, the head monk has inverted this command. Tell me, is it the same as before, or is it different? If you can decide this, there is no need for further elaboration."

Meyi: If you have not yet attained clarity and harbor doubts, please ask your questions. Question: The Prefect respectfully and repeatedly invited you; Your Reverence crossed the Xiang River in a ceremonial carriage.

Regarding the event at the Peak of the Thrown Almsbowl, we request that you, Master, proclaim its significance for us. The Master said: "The wind does not come; the tree does not move. The monk asked: "Why?"
Suddenly encountering a master, [the monk] asked, "Is it just like this, or is it not? The Master then shouted. The monk said, "This is killing me with your breath!
The Master said, "Come back thirty years from now, and I will give you twenty blows. He then asked, "What is the inconceivable Dharma?"

The Master said, "Today this mountain monk has failed. The monk said, "In that case, the five thousand [monks] of the past were of overweening pride, while today the great assembly has had their doubts stilled.
The Master said, "By this single question, I have been reduced to a state where even ice melts and walls crumble.
The monk said, "It is my fault. The Master said, "One who recognizes a fault must surely reform it. [The monk] asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'?"
The Master said, "Shenhui once polished the stele for Puji. The monk asked, "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'?
The Master said, "One must believe that there is another heaven within the alchemical vessel. The monk asked, "What is 'seizing both the person and the environment'? The Master said:
"The Son of Heaven within the realm; the General beyond the passes. The monk asked, "What is it like when both man and environment are not usurped?
The Master said, "The bright moon and clear wind come and go as they please. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "His face is like the full moon;
his eyes are like lotuses. In heaven and on earth, all pay him reverence. The monk asked, "When the ancients sat facing the wall, what was their intention? The Master said, "There is."
[Nian] Wude asked: "Master, you have ascended the Flower-King Throne in four places; as for the matter of your returning to the West with your single shoe, what is it like?
The Master said: "Empty space has no obstructions; north and south, one may ascend and soar at will. The monk said: "Thank you, Venerable, for your reply.

The Master said: "The idle are idle, and the busy are busy. [Another monk] asked: "I do not ask about the three gates being left unbarred, but as for the matter before the Hall of the Withered Tree, what is it like?"

"What? The Master said, "This is good news. The monk said, "When one person has cause for celebration, the myriad people depend upon it. The Master said, "For a thousand ages there have been those who understand.
The monk bowed, and the Master then gave a shout. The monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said:
[The Master] held a staff that could subdue dragons and tigers. A monk asked, "What if a person of the highest caliber were suddenly to encounter you?
The Master said, "Without a mind, one subdues ghosts and spirits. A monk asked, "How is it when traveling as a cloud over the sea? The Master said, "Suffering.

The Master continued, "The five peaks stand toweringly, alone revealed within the great void. The spreading waters flow on, coldly pouring down from the edge of the emerald sky cliff. The dragon pool is deep and hidden."
Secluded: the leaping fish finds no gate to pass through; Mount Tianzhu is high, and the water-clouds advance with no path.
Casting the hook across the four seas, one rarely encounters a fierce dragon; when a single phrase meets the point, a true friend is seldom found.

Therefore, the Three Mysteries were provisionally established to apply remedies according to the ailment, and the Four Selections of inclusion and exclusion were opened to guide and entice according to the capacity of the roots. The compassionate vows of the Buddhas of the past are inexhaustible. To the West...

The Patriarch flowed eastward, never forgetting his entrustment. Countless *jñānis* (teachers) have employed skillful means in myriad ways; though ten thousand streams arise from a single source, they all return to the great ocean.
But tell me, how do you explain the phrase, "Water does not wash water"? Is there anyone who can say it? Come forward and speak!
Even if you could speak with such boldness and discernment, you would still not have seen even a dream of a patch-robed monk (*bhikṣu*).
[The Master] stepped down from his seat, stood with his staff upright, and descended from the platform.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas emit radiance to assist in the realization of the meaning of the true nature (*dharmatā*).
[He held up his staff and said: 'This here is Nan-yuan’s staff; which one is the meaning of the true nature? If you perceive it as such, you are caught by seeing and hearing.'"
[The Master] turns [the whisk]. "If you do not see it, where are the eyes of one who travels on foot?

He lets out a shout and descends from his seat. Ascending the hall, after a long silence, he says: "Sometimes illumination comes first and function follows; sometimes function comes first and illumination follows;

sometimes illumination and function occur simultaneously; sometimes illumination and function do not occur simultaneously. Therefore it is said: there is light and there is darkness; there is arising and..."
[The Master] turns over and shouts, saying: "Tell me, is this illumination or is it function? Is there anyone who can distinguish between them?
If there is, please come forward and show your clumsy performance. If there is not, then today the mountain monk has suffered a defeat."
He ascended the hall and said: "In the kingdom of Magadha, not even water could leak through; before the peak of Shaoshi, he personally issued this decree.
What is this decree? Is there anyone who can state it? Bring it forth, mixing mud and water together—is there such a one?"
After a long silence, he said: "The traveler, hearing it for the first time, finds his travel-sleeve damp; the beautiful woman, as soon as she sings, lowers her azure brows.

With a shout, he ascended the hall and said: "Speaking of Buddhas and speaking of Patriarchs is merely mixing mud with water. 'Upward' and 'downward' are but worn-out straw sandals for the patch-robed monk."
It is not like that at all. To be bound by what is not a rope is self-imposed bondage. Now tell me: how do you express the single phrase of solitary liberation?
Is there anyone who can say it? Try bringing forth a phrase for the assembly. Is there one? Is there one? After a long silence, he said:
"Adding mud upon a tomb. He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have a single word that cuts off deliberation and forgets conditions; it cannot be obtained through clever speech—it requires only mind-to-mind transmission.
Furthermore, there is another phrase: nothing surpasses a direct presentation. But tell me, what is this one phrase of direct presentation?
After a long silence, he struck the ground with his staff once and let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he said: "At the single assembly on Vulture Peak, a thousand sages gathered together. When the Lord of Śākyas blinked his eyes, Kāśyapa smiled.
Yet, within the gate of the patch-robed monks, this is still but halfway there. Now tell me: how do you express that one phrase of total upholding? After a long silence, he said:
"Cherishing one's child, one does not perceive their ugliness. [Zhaozhou] struck his staff once. He then ascended the hall and said:
"Yesterday I was an infant; today my years are already old. Without yet understanding three, eight, and nine, it is difficult to tread the path of the Ancient Sovereign.
With hands, he covers the Yellow River until it dries up; with feet, he kicks Mount Sumeru until it falls over. This floating life is a dream-like, illusory body; human life—"
The evening cannot be guaranteed. Both heaven and hell are created by the mind. The pines on the southern mountains and northern ridges;
the grasses on the northern ridges and southern mountains—moistened by a single rain, they are boundless. Their roots and sprouts, some flourishing and some withered, stand as a bridge.

You practitioners of Zen from the five lakes should go ask the void. To die is to cast off one's summer shirt; to live is to don one’s winter robe. Clearly, there is nothing to do; yet, for no reason at all, [one acts].
Arousing afflictions, he let out a shout and ascended the hall, saying:
"The myriad functions move like a blade; all day long he propagates the Way. When it comes to 'pressing down a pig's head,' how do you speak of this?"
"Is there anyone who can speak? If you can, speak back a single phrase. After a long silence, he said:
"A golden chain with linked rings; a blade cannot pick it out. He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Last night, the sky was covered entirely in snow; the great earth was all at once bright and pure.
This morning, there is no one in the courtyard—do not say that this mountain monk has nothing to say."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The alms bowl is coarse; the ladle is fine. The spoons and chopsticks are neither too short nor too long—there is not a single one missing.
Sometimes when responding to offerings, with whom does one discuss them? One sighs for Mañjuśrī and Maitreya. The assembly of holy ones has stood for a long time. Be careful."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The great sun rises; north and south they run. The night moon is full; the sky has not yet dawned.
Setting aside for now the phrase of 'hiding one's body within the nostrils,' how do you all express the phrase beneath your own feet? Is there anyone who can say it?
After a long silence, he said: "Familiarity fills the world; how many truly know the heart? He let out a shout.
In the master’s room, a sword was planted upright. A pair of straw sandals and a basin of water were placed beside the sword.
Whenever someone entered the room, the master would say, "Look! Look! If anyone approached the sword and hesitated, the master would say, "Danger!
You have lost your body and forfeited your life," and would immediately shout and drive them out.
Chan Master Shouzhi of Xingjiao on Mount Taiyu in Junzhou asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, “The weather is cold and the days are short. [The monk] asked, “How was it before Mazu saw Baizhang?
The Master said, “Tight. The monk said, “And after he saw him? The Master said, “Crisp. [The monk] asked, “What is the realm of Hongzhou? The Master said, “The Tengwang Pavilion.”
The scenery of a thousand rivers flows below; a thin mist rises before the courtyard of the young child. A monk asked, “What is it like to be a person within this realm?

The Master said, “Entering and exiting, they strike the golden stirrups; in crimson robes, they face the brocade screens. A monk asked, “All conditioned phenomena are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows.
Please, Master, cite for me a matter of ultimate reality. The Master said, “Two parts are distinct; the rest of the text follows below. A monk asked, “Full...”
"The body is the eye. Where is the mouth? The Master said, "Three leaps and you have not passed. The monk said, "I do not understand; I specifically request your instruction.
The Master said, "The lyrics of the chapter have ended; the melody of the song arises in spring."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The path at Cuiyan is steep and treacherous; every step crosses a thousand streams. There is yet more—the waters of the great source flow on and on to the west of the ridge.
He struck the meditation seat once and said: "I have stood here for a long time. Take care. Ascending the hall again, he said: "The bell is struck and the drum beaten."
He gathered his assembly of Chan practitioners. "Coming up and going down, you sons inherit your fathers' trade; how many people have you deceived?
He struck the meditation seat once and ascended the hall, saying: "Sitting upright and squatting, crossing your legs to buy boots; looking left and right, not worth a single coin."
Striking the meditation seat, he said, "Take care. Ascending the hall, he said: "Fire arises from wood; it does not come from itself or from another.
Green comes from blue; they do not share the same dye. Every person eats the same stalk of mustard greens together. If you seek to eat another stalk, you will enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow.
Ascending the hall again, he said: "As soon as the Dharma drum beats, the great assembly gathers like clouds. The Buddhas of the three periods..."
"Will the Eighteenth Patriarch return to inquire after me? If there is even one person who does not come, I shall give each of you twenty blows.

Why is this so? 'To receive a bull from one man, yet return a horse to another. He ascended the hall. When the assembly had gathered and settled, the Master said, "The manifest reality is already established;
it is like beating a drum that cannot be distinguished. He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall. He ascended the hall again. Holding up an incense box, he showed it to them.
The assembly said, "Whether in the light or in the dark, if you can speak, you may walk as you please; if you cannot speak, then simply close your mouths.
He then descended from his seat. Entering the hall, he said: "To find no oil in the sand is a pitiable matter; Cuiyan is chewing up food to feed an infant."
At another time, he said, "One must wait for the right moment and the true essence of wisdom. Only then will one realize that from the beginning, one's face has been covered in ashes. "Be careful!

He then ascended the hall and said, "The clouds have cleared and the mist has rolled away; the mountains and rivers are bright under the sun. If you try to speak of the many paths, you cannot bring them forth. [He struck the meditation seat] and descended from the hall."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The Ten Grounds are startled; the followers of the Two Vehicles cannot fathom it. Within the gate of the patch-robed monks, there are those with copper heads and iron brows.

He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall. Ascending the hall again, he said: "In the depths of the great ocean, they stand in ranks. From the beginning, the second in line has gray hair at his temples.
Why does the first not have gray hair at his temples? Do you wish to understand? Golden stamens and silver filaments form the jade dew."
A high monk does not sit upon the Phoenix Terrace. [He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it. Entering the hall, he said: "Deshan would strike immediately upon entering the gate;
Linji would shout immediately upon entering the gate. I, Cuoyan, am not like this: I would give you thirty blows right at the main gate."
What does this mean? To apply both the staff and the shout at once is already too late. Throughout past and present, all have praised it as being beyond all elaboration.

Since it does not involve either of the two paths, by what means could it be explained? When the King of Persia from the South Sea presented ivory, [Baizhang] struck the meditation seat and said, "Take care."
The Chan Master Kuaihua Guangzhao of Mount Langya in Chuzhou was named Huijue. He was a native of Western Luoyang.
His father served as the Governor of Hengyang and passed away due to illness; the Master carried his coffin back to Luoyang. On the way, he passed through the ancient monastery of Yaoshan in Liyang.
It was as if he had resided there from time immemorial; on this account, he left the household life. Wandering to consult various masters, he attained the Dharma at Fenyang.
Responding to conditions at Chushi, he proclaimed the Way simultaneously with Xuedou Mingjue; those from all quarters regarded them as two gates of ambrosia.

To this day, the traces of his transformation remain as if present in Huainan. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Copper heads and iron jaws. The monk asked, "What is the meaning [of this]?"
"What is the meaning? The Master said, "The beak of a bird; the gills of a fish. A monk asked, "I do not ask about Ānanda’s compilation of the teachings, but what about Kāśyapa’s smile?
The Master said, "Precise as to time and precise as to measure. The monk said, "Since the lamp was divided at Vulture Peak, it has shone through ancient and modern times right up to China.
The Master said, "Dotting the cinnabar; dotting the lacquer. A monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said—
[The monk] said, “I carry my book and sword in hand to pay court to the enlightened sovereign. The Master asked, “What is the host within the guest?
The Master replied, “Rolling up the pearl curtain, there is nothing to be seen. The monk asked, “What is the guest within the host? The Master replied, “Passing Mengjin at the third watch.”
The monk asked, "What is the master among masters? The Master said, "Sitting alone, he presides over the entire universe. The monk asked, "How is it before the lotus has emerged from the water?
The Master said, "A cat and a mouse wearing paper hats. The monk asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the water? The Master said:
The dog wears boots and walks. A monk asked, "What is the seamless stupa? The Master said, "It eternally anchors the crimson mists. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the stupa?
The Master said, "He constantly sleeps with the white clouds. A monk asked, "When a single speck of dust arises and the entire earth is fully contained within it, what then?
The Master said, "Li Guang shoots down a wild goose from the midst of the clouds. The monk said, "The dragon roars and the mist rises."

[The Master] rose. As the tiger roared, the wind arose. The Master said, "It startles the barbarian boy so that he flees like smoke. [A monk] asked, "I do not ask about raising the mallet or brandishing the whisk;
what about the matter of blinking an eye and raising an eyebrow? The Master said, "Zhaozhou once met Nanquan. The monk said: [He did].
The student did not understand. The Master said, "This winter there will be much snow and rain; how can poor families endure it? The student asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa?
The Master said, "With the left hand draw a square; with the right hand draw a circle. The monk said, "The Stone Bridge at Tiantai is narrow."
The sitting mat at Mount Nanyue was wide. The Master said, "On his back he bears the Seven Stars; in his mouth he recites mantras.

Entering the hall, he said, "If you wish to know the eternally abiding body, you should observe this decaying physical form. If you wish to know the eternally abiding nature, you should observe this staff.
This staff swallows up Mount Sumeru; Mount Sumeru swallows up the staff. When a patch-robed monk arrives..."
If you hesitate or deliberate here, your sword will fall from your shoulder and you will surrender; your iron breastplate will reach the furthest reaches of the sea.
(He struck the meditation seat once.)

Ascending the hall, he said: "How marvelous! The Buddhas of the ten directions are originally but flowers in the eye. If you wish to know the flowers in the eye, they are originally the Buddhas of the ten directions.
If you wish to know the Buddhas of the ten directions, they are not the flowers in the eye. If you wish to know the flowers in the eye, they are not the Buddhas of the ten directions.
If you can understand this clearly, the fault lies with the Buddhas of the ten directions. If you have not yet understood this, the Śrāvakas will rise up and dance."
The Pratyekabuddha prepares for his toilette.
Take care. He ascends the hall and says: "Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are all causes of birth and death; yet seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are precisely the root of liberation.
It is like a lion turning back upon itself; whether south, north, east, or west, it has no fixed destination. You all..."
"If you do not understand, do not fail the Old Śākyamuni. Tsk!
He then ascended the hall and said: "Today I have explained it through for all of you. O clear-eyed monks, do not sit in meditation in the mud. Take care."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The heavens are so high they cannot be measured; the earth is so vast it can never be known. Flakes of white clouds fly over the mountain peaks; clear waters murmur swiftly down the mountain ravines.
I shall not ask you about the single phrase of 'rising in the east and sinking in the west. But as for the single phrase of 'before birth and after death'—how do you speak of it?
After a long silence, he said: "The weather is cold. Go have some tea."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The birds call in the forest; the monkeys cry on the peaks. All phenomena are utterly still—how can they be revealed?
After a long silence, he said: "If you hesitate or try to deliberate further, the arrow has already passed beyond the kingdom of Silla."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "The Buddhas of the three periods turn the Great Dharma Wheel within the flames;
the old monks of the world turn the Great Dharma Wheel upon the tips of the hundred grasses; I, this mountain monk, turn the Great Dharma Wheel upon the tip of this staff.
Do you understand? If you do not yet understand, let this staff recite a verse once more. He struck it.
Descending from the meditation seat, he ascended the hall and said:
"A-he-he! What is this? When the mouth opens, it is so; when the mouth closes, it has passed. A light boat with a short oar floats upon the heart of the waves;
the raincoat and straw hat let others wear them until they are worn out. Heh!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas of the ten directions are nothing but rotten wooden stakes; the Three Sages and Ten Holy Ones are nothing but tally-sticks from a public latrine.
When you all have come here, what are you doing? After a long silence, he said:
"If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata."
Chan Master Qijū of Fahu Chan Monastery in Shūzhou asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed?

The Master said: "The head of the storehouse is white; the head of the sea is black. The monk said: "The true son of Fenyang. The Master said: "Do not confuse the needle and the awl. He asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master said:

"Reeds sprout through his knees. He asked: "What is the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "The head of the storehouse is white; the head of the sea is black. The monk said: "The true son of Fenyang. The Master said: "Do not confuse the needle and the awl."
The Master said, "Red lips and white teeth. The monk asked, "What is 'taking away the person but not the environment'?
The Master said, "White chrysanthemums bloom as the red sun warms; the centenarian does not encounter spring. The monk asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not the person'?
The Master said, "The great earth is cut off from all news; one wanders freely, alone, embodying the Real. The monk asked, "What is 'the person'?"
"Both object and subject are stripped away. The Master said, "The weeds overgrow and people’s complexions change; both ordinary and sage are equally empty.
A monk asked, "What is it like when neither person nor object is stripped away? The Master said, "The clear breeze and the bright moon—the rustic elder smiles as they draw near."
Chan Master Faying of Chongsheng Monastery in Tanzhou asked: "When the six states have not yet been pacified, what is it like?

The Master said, "The bronze pillars stand forever marking the land of the Manzi. The monk asked, "What is it like after they are pacified? The Master said, "The iron banners have blown out their smoke, yet the heart has not turned to ash.
A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Tearing open the fragrant pouch to perfume the great kingdom."
He pierced open the aperture of heaven and roared the true wind. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The sleeves of the robe are short while the arms are long.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The knees of the cloth trousers are worn through."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Upon the Terrace of Frost-Flowers, emerald hues swirl; before the Hall of Withered Trees, monkeys cry and tigers roar.
You all, arriving here, must stand still and behold it; then you may well rest and cease. Should your doubts not yet be extinguished,"
A wild understanding, towering and imposing! Let us further observe this mountain monk’s "one interpretation. [The monk] strikes once with his staff.
Chan Master Hao Tai of Tiansheng in Huzhou asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A black-lacquered holy monk. The monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Look at the wall; it is the color of earth. [Another] asked, "Before the precious sword has emerged..."

Introduction:
Chan Master Daguan of Mount Jinshan in Runzhou was named Tanying. He was a native of Qiantang and surnamed Qiu.

He entered the monastic life and received full ordination at Longxing Temple; there he mastered the Buddhist scriptures and extensively studied the Confucian classics. He subsequently visited various spiritual teachers.
He investigated the true vehicle (*bhūta-yāna*) and subsequently attended the Dharma seat of Chan Master Cizhao, where he secretly realized the essential tenets of the school.
For over thirty years, he presided over five major monasteries; his reputation for the Way grew ever more eminent, and both the clergy and the laity looked up to him with joy and reverence.
The State Councilors Wang Shu and Xia Song, as well as the Military Governors Li Duanyi and Li Duan, all knocked upon the gate of the profound mystery and respectfully took him as their teacher.
The rites were performed, and his words were recorded at the time; this collection was titled the *Dengmen ji* (Collection of the Entrance to the Gate).
On the first day of the first month in the fifth year of the Jiayou era, he ascended the hall to take leave of the assembly, returned to his quarters, sat in the lotus posture, and passed away.

Question: "If you block the throat, lips, and mouth, I ask the Master to speak. The Master said, "These are my own throat, lips, and mouth;
how could you possibly block them? The monk said, "In that case, it is the student’s fault.
The Master shouted, "Had it not been for Master Zangyuan being here, I would have given you a sound beating with a mallet! Question: "What are the first two characters of the sutra text?"
The Master said, "The character 'yi' (以). The monk asked, "What connection is there? The Master said, "The character 'ba' (八). The monk said, "How you deceive people!
The Master said, "Because of slandering this sutra, one incurs such guilt. Question: "Who do you teach to carry the iron cangue weighing one hundred and twenty catties?
The Master said, "The old monk. The monk said, "One reaps what one sows. The Master said, "Suffering! Suffering! Question: "Does the Master still... [text fragment]
"Have you ever recited the Buddha's name? The Master said, "I have never recited the Buddha's name. The monk asked, "Why have you never recited it?
The Master said, "I fear it would defile people's mouths. A monk asked, "When the Great Master Mazu gave a shout and Baizhang was deaf for three days, what was the meaning of this?
The Master said, "In my entire life, I have never been shouted at by anyone; thus, my ears have been deaf for my whole life. The monk asked, "How do you understand this?"
The Master said, "Lately my eyes have grown dim. The monk bowed, and the Master said, "When the eyes grow dim, one writes with large characters; when the ears grow dull, one speaks in a loud voice.
A monk asked, "I do not ask about the dead on the pure ground; but what of it after passing through the thicket of thorns?"
The Master said, "A Persian composes a Sanskrit hymn. The monk said, "Even before the Hall of Good Dharma, one must still pass through the interrogation.
The Master said, "A Khitan performs a foreign melody. The monk said, "Wait until I take Dahui’s words from this day and present them for the great masters of all quarters to behold."
The Master said, "In this place there are no attendants; you must ultimately ask those from the great community. The monk came forward and bowed.

The Master said, "This monk has indeed been a fellow practitioner in the past. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "If one does not sleep on the same bed, how can one know what is pierced within the covers?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "As soon as one involves the lips and tongue, one falls into the realm of conceptual thought;
all such are dead ends, not the living path. Even if one manages to break through, one still remains mired in delusion. Do not let your lifelong efforts go to waste, nor let this life pass in vain.
If you wish not to let your life go to waste—take up the staff and say: 'You must not be deceived by this staff. Look, look!"
"The staff has pierced through the skulls of you all and leaped into the nostrils. *He strikes once.* The Master ascends the hall.
When the assembly has gathered, the Head Seat comes forward to prostrate. The Master says, "Ask well! The Head Seat lowers his head.
During a question-and-answer session, the Master said, "Today I shall not answer questions," and immediately returned to his quarters.
He then ascended the hall and said: "The mountain monk’s approach is unique; I have already altered the tracks of all other quarters.
To extract Mañjuśrī’s wedge from his eyes, I bid Samantabhadra cease chewing the iron in his mouth. I urge you to let go of the hand that grasps the slithering snake, and I grant it to you."
"Chop down the hitching stake for the donkey. [The Master] pauses, intending to reflect, and shouts, "Squeeze!
Squeeze! Investigate! Ascending the hall, he said: "In my life, this mountain monk has always loved sumo wrestling, yet there was no one to match me.
Today, I shall wrestle with the Head Seat. Roll up your *kāṣāya* and come down from the seat! He challenged the Head Seat to wrestle. As soon as the Head Seat stepped out...
The Master said, "Tumbling on level ground," and then returned to his quarters.
Entering the hall for formal discourse, he said, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time are my servants; the entire Great Canon of teachings is my spittle. After a long silence, he said:
"Tell me, who are the servants of the Buddhas of the three periods? He then drew a line with his whisk and said, "The Buddhas of the three periods have gone over this side.
"Tell me, whose spittle is the Great Canon of Teachings? The Master then spat once himself.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The scale-weight suddenly floats to the bottom of the well; the old rat has been transformed into an ox for many years.
When Huikong saw this, he clapped his hands and laughed: 'A three-legged monkey—how different from a common ape!'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The five thousand scriptures are the constant discourse of all Buddhas; the eighty thousand afflictions are the wondrous functioning of sentient beings.
Yet even these are not yet the adamantine eye. What is the adamantine eye? After a long silence, he said: "Blind!"

Ascending the hall, when the assembly had gathered and settled, a monk just as he stepped forward to prostrate, the Master said, "If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season.
The monk then asked, "What are the conditions of time and season? The Master immediately descended from his seat.
At Longhua Monastery in Hangzhou, Chan Master Yue Baojue of the Qi Dynasty asked: "Whose song does the Master sing?
Whom does the lineage of his school follow? The Master replied: "The phoenix perches upon the *bing* table; the waters of the Han River flow toward the east. The monk said: "A true son of Guyin."
Regarding the descendants of Linji, the Master said: "White clouds span the mouth of the valley; the woodcutter asks for their origin. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "A prominent nose and a broad forehead. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Willow eyes and willow brows."
Chan Master Huiyue of Mount Dongting in Suzhou was asked, "What is the realm of Cui峰 (Cui Peak)? The Master said, "The mountain is high; the moon shines upon it first.
The lake is near; the water reflects the light. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Leaning on the railing, he watches the distant oars;
leaning his staff, he points toward the front peak. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of Zhizhi’s single finger? The Master said, "The moon has set."
At the third watch, he passed through the marketplace.
Zen Master Xiujǐ of Míngzhōu, holding his staff, asked: "What is the seamless stupa? The Master said: "Its four corners rest firmly on the ground.
The monk asked: "Who is the person within the stupa? The Master said: "High upon the pillow, there is no worry. [The monk] asked: "What is the Patriarch?"
[The monk asked about] the Master’s intent in coming from the West. The Master said: "A merchant ship crosses the sea; barefoot, he returns to his hometown.
Chan Master Yishi of Shuanglin Temple in Hongzhou asked: "Whose song do you sing? Whose ancestral style do you succeed? The Master said:
"One may deliberate well beneath the phoenix grove. The monk said: "In that case, the waters of Ruzhou flow eastward—the Linji lineage!"
[The Master] said: "A mere foot's distance separates one from the ends of the earth. Question: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said: "Two green pines stand facing each other as a mournful wind arises. Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "When people are equal, they do not speak."
The water flows level, yet does not flow. A monk asked, "What is the realm of the Twin Trees? The Master said, "Red clouds arise over the blue peaks;
green bamboos draw in the clear breeze. The monk asked, "Who is the person within this realm? The Master said, "Three times three before, three times three after. The monk asked again.
"How is it when one enters directly with a single blade? The Master said, "Act according to the command. The monk responded, "Yes. The Master then struck him.
Chan Master Kecong of Guyin Mountain in Xiangzhou asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed?"
The Master said: "The mountains connect with the beauty of Mount Song; the waters join the flow of the Han River. A question was asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master said:

"Stacking firewood and setting it ablaze. A question was asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "The sun rises in the east; its light reaches the western door."
Cen Shenxiu, the Ancient Chan Master of Shushan in Fuzhou, asked: "Master, as you now ascend this precious seat, whose dharma lineage do you succeed?
The Master replied: "Mount Duxiu is high; Fenghuang Ridge is steep. The monk said: "In that case, you are the legitimate son of Shimen and a descendant of Linji.
The Master said: "A single hand cannot clap alone."
Chan Master Xianqin of Yunmen Mountain in Yuezhou ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said, "What a fine phrase!
If you go to other places, do not misrepresent it. He then descended from his seat.
A newly ordained Chan Master from Shangfang in Anji, Huzhou, asked: "Form and mind are not two; self and other are without distinction.

Apart from these two paths, what is your intention, Master? The Master said: "Vast and empty, with nothing to rely upon, beyond the green cliffs. The monk said: "I do not yet understand the essential point. The Master said:
"White clouds do not reach the Purple Cloud Peak. The monk said: "If that is so, then when seeing the moon, one should cease looking at the finger."
The Master said, "What is the moon? The monk hesitated, and the Master gave a shout.
Chan Master Shenzen of Renshou in Chuzhou asked, "I know you have already attained the essential meaning of Chan; for whose sake do you proclaim that single phrase on the spot?
The Master said, "Clay chickens and tile dogs. The monk asked, "How should one understand this? The Master said, "It is not before the gate."
[The Master] swept with a mountain boy; at his will, clumsy hairpins filled the paths and forks. [A monk] asked, "What is the realm of Nanming?

The Master said, "Pavilions and terraces reflect the moon across a thousand worlds; flowers and trees bear spring in all four seasons. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said:
Clad in tattered robes and carrying a lute with broken strings on his back, he ascended the hall and said: "Clearly there is no awakening; to have a dharma is delusion.
When the sun rises without clouds, it shines radiantly upon the heavens. When there is no film before the eyes, the sky is fundamentally free of flowers.
Before those who lack wisdom, one must not speak erroneously. After a long silence, he said: "Just let it be so."
Chan Master Bianyuan of Chengtian Temple in Hangzhou asked: "How is it when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?

The Master said: "It is not seen at the bottom of the water. The monk asked: "How is it after it has emerged? The Master said: "Its fragrance fills the road. He ascended the hall and said: "The spring wind and the dews have cleared;
the Qingming Festival of Cold Food is serene and pure. If you speak of the meaning of the Westward Transmission, it is a journey of ten thousand miles."
Chan Master Puchan of Mount Cuifeng in Suzhou asked: "In the past, the Brahma King invited the Buddha for the sake of all living beings;
today, the king and his ministers invite you, Master. How will you act for the sake of the assembly? The Master said: "Before words are spoken, the Way is cut off—there is no realm beyond;

outside of the mind, the whole is raised up—there is that which precedes all forms. The monk said: "The great assembly bears witness; we students have cause for reliance. The Master said: "Do not say so."

Zen Master Ziran of Qizhenyuan in Quanzhou asked: "When the Old Barbarian appeared in the world, he looked around in the four directions.
When you, Master, appear in the world, how do you manifest it? The Master said: "The clear essence becomes heaven; the turbid essence becomes earth. The monk said: "If that is so..."
"Then it is just like picking up weeds with one's own hands. The Master said, "What connection is there?

Chan Master Daolong Yuanming of Huayan Monastery in Dongjing, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Julian Zhenhui of Guanghui Monastery in Ruizhou, asked: "The root of sentient beings relies upon the ocean of wisdom."
[The Master] said: "It is the source. The stream of sentient beings takes the Dharmakāya as its essence. Apart from these two paths, I request the Master to provide another way.
The Master said: "A wooden horse neighs by day; a clay ox bellows by night. The monk said: "If that is so, then as soon as a single word is uttered, the fourfold assembly receives its grace.
The Master said: "Do not obscure the great assembly. [The monk] asked: "What is the Way? The Master said: "High and low."
The monk asked, "What is it like for one on the Way? The Master said, "The feet are thin, yet the straw sandals are wide. The Master further said: "If you speak, you are met with a critique;
if you remain silent, you are rebuked. To convey the message once more: the moon and its reflection in the cassia trees sway and flourish. This is because sentient beings are vast and turbulent;
in pursuing the root and the branch, where can they find their return? They dwell in this world in a state of confusion; regarding birth and death, upon what can they rely?"

Liaotui asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Large head, small tail. The monk said, "I do not yet understand.

"The whole world hears of the ape carrying its young; who has ever seen a bird holding a flower in its beak? The monk asked: "What is the realm within the realm?"

through the ages, the meaning is clear. The Master said, "What tune is that? He asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master said, "The sun rises over Mount Fú."
The mulberry trees illuminate the great chiliocosm. He ascended the hall and said: "In the rainy season of plum blossoms, the downpours persist through the deep gloom;

weariness makes it difficult to discern the crane’s form. Yet, with eyes open and the mind awakened, one does not differ [from others]; though hearing neither morning nor evening, one remains ever more alert.
"Great assembly, for those who sleep, there is the principle of sleeping; for those who do not sleep, there is the principle of not sleeping. Suppose someone were to suddenly step forward and ask..."
"What are the eyes that do not sleep? After a long silence, he said, "The sun and moon do not travel through the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven. He then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Lan of Shanguan in Suizhou asked, "Your profound mechanism has been heard of by all who have passed before you;

today, at this assembly, I pray you will provide us with guidance. The Master said, "An iron pillar stands across the sea gate. The monk said, "In that case, the divine blade does not even reveal its tip."
The Master said, "Fishing on dry land from a boat. The monk said, "First, let me pay three prostrations. The Master then struck him.

Chan Master Guangyun of Miaozhi Temple on Mount Tiantai asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said: "The yellow chrysanthemums by the eastern hedge. The monk said: "What is the intent behind this? The Master said: "The Double Ninth Festival in the ninth month.

"Please walk alone through the vermilion heavens. "If you cannot recommend [the Way], you will inevitably sit coldly at Shaolin.

The Master said: "The seas are calm and the rivers are clear. The monk said: "The profound gate has been opened; all people stand in awe. Transcending the mundane world, how lofty!"

"Tell me, how can one attain resonance? After a long silence, he said: 'A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them;
they follow the warbling orioles over the low wall. *Du!* (A shout)."

The monk asked, "Who are the people within the realm? The Master said, "Two tigers patrol the mountains."

Chan Master Yihuai of Tiantai Mountain in Yuezhou was surnamed Chen. He was a native of Leqing in Wenzhou.

His mother had previously dreamed that a star fell into her courtyard and an auspicious light filled the room; subsequently, the Master was born. In his youth, he spoke seldom and smiled rarely, yet his speech was extraordinary compared to that of others.
He surrendered himself to leave the household life. His preceptor had previously dreamed that a divine being announced, "Tomorrow, the Dharma King will arrive.

The following morning, when the master arrived, he treated him with extraordinary hospitality. After receiving full ordination, he heard the lecture on the sutra passage, "One should give rise to the mind without dwelling anywhere," and attained a slight degree of awakening.
He posed questions and raised difficult challenges, yet none among the assembly were able to respond. Subsequently, he traveled through various regions.
He visited various masters; although he received many seals of approval, he had not yet fully exhausted the essential tenets.
Later, while in the capital, he encountered Yan Fahua, who patted his master’s back and said, "This is Yunmen and Linji. He then proceeded to the Dharma seat of Chan Master Mingjue of Cui峰 in Suzhou.
While drawing water, his carrying pole fell to the ground, and he attained sudden, great enlightenment. Xian immediately granted him formal approval (*kanna*).

Ascending the hall, he said: "The Great has no fixed direction; the Small has no location. Half-closed, half-open—this cannot yet be granted.
On the ridge the plum blossoms first burst open, and the myriad flowers flourish; with light rain and light sun, the power of spring is universal. The power of spring is universal."
"In the end, do not inquire after the Patriarch of Caoxi. He ascended the hall and said: "The Dharma has no 'you'; principle is not constant.

The Ultimate Way has no fixed point; it responds to things like motes of dust in a world-system. It reaches the point where the wind blows and the grass bends, where echoes follow sounds and harmonize.

There is not even a grain of anything with which to compare it—this is like setting up a sign in a bustling marketplace. If you wish to avoid harming the harmony of the atmosphere, you may as well idly consult with a pillar. If you can...
He nodded his head in agreement. "Do not say that this mountain monk is talkative," he said, and then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Shouchen of Chengxin in Yuezhou asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "What are you saying? The monk said:

Chan Master Zizhi of Xiangji in Zhenzhou asked: "I do not ask about the four mountains pressing in from all sides;

The Master said, "A three-legged frog leaps up into the sky. A monk asked, "What is a monk who sits in meditation?

The Master said, "He is utterly incapable of anything. The monk asked, "What is a monk who enters meditative absorption? The Master said, "The four seas are originally limpid and still. The monk said...
"What is a monk who practices the Way? The Master said, "The six realms of existence are surging with vital energy. The monk asked, "What is a monk who receives offerings?
The Master said, "The three spheres are equal in their emptiness of nature. He then ascended the hall and said, "The Way of the Bodhisattva cannot be schemed or measured.

The myriad dharmas are fundamentally non-existent; how could the four voids possibly exist? Taking non-action as the宗 (zong, or primary principle) and formlessness as the root, its measure encompasses the entire realm of sand-grains [the universe]."

His virtue permeates heaven and earth. Sometimes he expounds the One Vehicle; sometimes he transmits the Three Phrases; sometimes he causes others to awaken to their fundamental nature, leading them all to return to the source.
Yet, within ultimate reality, such things do not exist at all. Once the original mind is fully realized, the mind is perfectly clear;

mountains, rivers, and the great earth are likewise tranquil. He ascended the hall and said: "The originally possessed mind is not separated by so much as a hair’s breadth. Because of erroneous thoughts, one consequently falls into deviation."
No. When defilements are exhausted, one encounters people and enables them to clarify their own vision. What is this "own vision"? The vast waves of the four seas are stilled;
a single orb illuminates heaven and earth.
Chan Master Qianmingze of Xinyang Army asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed? The Master said: "A single cloud rises over the sea peak;
a lone wild goose passes through the cold sky. The monk said: "If that is so, then you are the true heir of Xuedou. The Master said: "On every ridge it is magnificent;
the six-flakes of snow are bright and pure. [Another] asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said, "A pure breeze arises in the azure void. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The bright moon reflects upon the long river.
The monk asked, "What is the Ocean-Seal Samādhi? The Master said, "Simply seek it within yourself. The monk said, "I do not understand."
The Master said, "Do not seek it from others. A monk asked, "What is the Way of daily life? The Master said, "A single arrow reaches Western Heaven.
The monk asked, "After it has reached there, what then? The Master said, "Pervading the entire Dharma-realm."
A monk from Numineng in Chuzhou asked Master Ming of Shendu, “How is it before the lion has emerged from its cave?

The Master said, “A pure breeze fills the earth. The monk said, “How is it after it has emerged from the cave? The Master said, “The brains of the foxes are split open. The monk asked, “Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master said, “The reflections of water and sky merge into azure. The monk said, “Ultimately, are they the same or different? The Master said, “They are the same.”
"Separate. The Master said, "The sounds of pines and bamboo are mutually cold.

The Master continued, "Even if one were to ask in a manner that overturns the ravines and topples the mountains—treading upon the earth in the east and west, knowing the directions in the south and north, unconstrained by either contrariness or compliance, appearing and disappearing with sovereign ease, such that all the grasses, trees, and forests of the entire world become the blade of wisdom—even so, within the gate of building and transforming, there is still a slight margin of difference. As for the fundamental state,"
[The Master] said, "It can be said to be one hundred and eight thousand.
Layman Li Linzong, the Head Seat Yuanyi of Yunfeng on Mount Nanyue, asked: "I desire to transcend the mundane world but have not yet done so;

Zuo said, "Do you understand? The scholar suddenly attained awakening and offered this verse: "The mirror of the mind has always been lucid; The great river was deep from the start.
It was only after the Master’s question That sand and stone were transformed into gold. Zuo said, "You are heading straight for hell.
The scholar said, "If there is no mark of self or other, why speak of hell? Zuo said, "Where are you now? The scholar said, "I am here before you."
The respondent said, "This very thing is gold.
The Dharma Master Fanzong of Mount Touzi in Shuzhou asked, "What is the家风 (family style) of a practitioner? The Master replied, "A *kāṣāya* wrapped around straw sandals.

Chan Master Ziyuan of Mount Ganlu in Shaoyou, successor to Chan Master Baoyuan Ciji of Nanhua in Shaoyou, asked:

Jiuyun said: "The pupil in the eye blows the wooden flute.

Chan Master Baoshou Xingde of Shaoyang was invited to Nanhua. It happened to be the beginning of winter. The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "It is a new winter for the new Baoshou;
these words are the same as those spoken in the past. If you understand the meaning of the Westward Journey, it is like a Persian merchant boarding a ship.

Chan Master Shoucheng of White Tiger Mountain in Shaoyang asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "He has eyes, but no nostrils.
Chan Master Zongqin of Fotuo Mountain in Shaoyang asked, "How do you directly point people to their nature? The Master replied, [as above].

"How was it that you were assigned first? The Master said, "What do you say? The monk said, "If that is so, then I thank the Master for his instruction.

Chan Master Haeyun of Baolin Mountain in Lechang County, Shaoyang, asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master replied:

The monk asked, "What is it like when one neither advances nor retreats? The Master said, "Lost. The monk asked, "How is it then?
The Master said, "Sulu sulu."

Chan Master Zutian Yuanzhong (also known as Ciyun Zuyin) of Lushan, whose Dharma lineage descended from Chan Master Pule Zizhong of Dongshan in Xiangzhou, was named Juna. He was the son of the Jian family of Hanzhou. At thirteen, he received full ordination;
at fifteen, he began lecturing. With a single sweep of his whisk, a thousand people would sit in attendance. His bearing was as pure as ice, and the source of his mind was like the ocean.
Zhan was preeminent in his quick wit and wisdom; his practice and understanding far surpassed those of his peers. His speech emerged as refined compositions, and his brushwork filled entire scrolls.

Suddenly abandoning what he had studied, he traveled afar to study under the Chan school, meeting Chan Master Rong, through whom he attained sudden enlightenment into the meaning of the Patriarchs. Later, he appeared in the world to reside at Guizong;
before long, he moved to Shangyuan Tongci, and subsequently transferred to Sijuzu. Afterward, he returned to Yuan Tongci. [This was recorded by] Wen Zhonggong Xiu of Ouyang.

[The Emperor] saw him and deeply admired his character and conduct. He frequently asked scholars coming from the south, "Have you ever seen Master Nǜ? Consequently, the Master’s reputation grew weighty among both the court and the common people.
During the Rénzōng era of the Huángyù period, Emperor Rénzōng issued an imperial decree for him to reside at Jìngyīn Monastery in the capital;

he firmly declined and did not go. Thereupon, the Emperor bestowed upon him ceremonial robes and a posthumous title. In the third year of the Xīníng period, one day, he took his leave of Liu Gōngshù, the Governor of Jiāng.

Together with his various officials and subordinates, he returned to the monastery to bathe, sat upright, and manifested his passing. Lord Liu led several thousand monastics and laypeople to escort him to the cremation pyre.
Amidst the flames, white vapor rose up piercing the sun; the assembly all looked on in wonder and reverence. They asked, "What is the Master’s family style?
The Master said, "At Guizong Temple, by the side of Mount Zixiao. A monk asked, "If a guest suddenly arrives, what will you do?"
[The monk] waited respectfully. The Master said, "To roam the mountains and play with the waters. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when an ancestral monastery is restored?
The Master said, "The man is on Mount Pòtóu. The monk said, "When power is once in one's hand... The Master struck him.
The Master said, "Have the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings ever spoken of this? After a long silence, he said, "Go and drink tea."
Chan Master Xiang of Huiyin in Hangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Zhijing Baoyue of Mount Baiyang in Hongzhou, asked:
"Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed? The Master said:
"Heaven is round and earth is square. The monk said, "I ask the Master for a word on this point. The Master said, "If you go to other places, explain it clearly to them.
The Master continued, "The southern mountain is high; the northern mountain is low. The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. The white ox climbs the tree and cannot be found;
the black rooster enters the water, and everyone knows it. But tell me, what is it like after it has been found? Liang.
[The Master] said, "For a long time. [A monk] asked, "What can it do?
Chan Master Huiyin Yining of Hangzhou was asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said, "Lady Māyā.
The monk asked, "How was it after he appeared in the world? The Master said, "Prince Siddhārtha. He ascended the hall and said, "The consciousness is stilled and brought to clarity."
Waves. When the water is clear, reflections appear; when one awakens to the essence of non-thought, quiescent extinction manifests before one.
Whether in Pūrvavideha to the east or Aparagoyānī to the west, I grant you this understanding. Yet, thirty years from now, do not be negligent. Investigate!
Chan Master Tan of Zhongshan Ba’en Chan Monastery in Zhuji, Yue State, a successor of Chan Master Jipeng of Yungai Mountain in Tanzhou, asked:
"Regarding the lion’s roar in the Hall of Good Dharma, how is the single phrase that benefits people? The Master said: "Layer upon layer, mountain pass and road. The monk said: "If it is so, then..."
A thousand flowers flourish by the side of the Purple Neighbor Rock; ten thousand people sing before the White Jade Hall.
The Master said, "This is reciting the lines of Du Fu. A monk asked, "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes picking and choosing. What is non-picking and choosing?

The Master said, "Yesterday was the third; today is the fourth. The monk said, "This is still picking and choosing. The Master said, "It is easy to distinguish dragons from snakes, but for a patch-robed monk..."

"Difficult to satisfy. [The monk] asked: "A question and an answer still fall within the gateway of manifesting transformations. I do not yet know how to raise and proclaim [the Dharma] within the primary meaning (paramārtha).
The Master said: "Raindrops before the eaves; snow fills the vast sky. The monk said:
"If that is so, then at the end, the frosty night moon falls naturally into the stream ahead. The Master said: "An adept Chan guest. The monk said: "Master, do not deceive me."
