Chan Master Yuanzhao, whose name was Zongben, was the abbot of Huilin Chan Monastery at Daxiangguosi in Tokyo. He was surnamed Guan and was a native of Wuxi in Changzhou.
Having left home under Master Sheng of Yong’an Chan Monastery in Suzhou and received the full precepts of a bhikṣu, he immediately aspired to travel for study.
He went to the Dharma seat of Chan Master Huai of Jingde Monastery in Chizhou and entered the inner quarters to seek instruction.
He was shown [the teaching] regarding what Dharma Maitreya’s inner palace expounds. It was said: "It expounds this very Dharma.

Day and night, he contemplated it without interruption, yet though he investigated its essence, he did not yet understand. By chance, while in his environment, he saw a yellow plum on a tall tree. The Wise One (Zhishi) had previously said:
"When the plums ripen in the fifth month, there shall be an awakening such as this. Suddenly, he attained sudden enlightenment of the Mind Seal.
He penetrated the subtle and profound depths, serving with diligent devotion for over ten years while daily investigating the esoteric principles.

Later, he emerged into the world at Suzhou Ruiguang Monastery, and subsequently moved to Jingci Monastery, where his assembly of students constantly numbered more than five hundred. Soon thereafter, he was summoned by imperial decree to reside at HuiLin Monastery.
Emperor Shen-zong received him in private audience and bestowed upon him the Chan title "Cuanzhao. Not long after, he requested to return to Lingyan Monastery. In the second year of the Yuanfu era—
On the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month, he bathed, changed his robes, summoned his disciples, gave them his final instructions, and passed away.
His disciples said, "Since you will no longer remain in this world, why not leave behind a verse? The Master replied, "For forty years, there has been no time when I have not spoken;
why must I repeat my verses on this very day? He then sat upright and entered parinirvāṇa. On the last day of the first month of the following year, his entire body [was enshrined].
His stupa was enshrined at his native mountain. His secular age was eighty, and his monastic seniority (śrāmaṇerī-vaṣa) was fifty-three.

For forty years he extended his hand [in teaching], and thrice presided over great monasteries. Those who inherited the Dharma and transmitted the Way are beyond counting; those whose names were renowned in their time numbered more than one hundred.
On the day of opening the hall, Emperor Shenzong dispatched an imperial messenger to bestow incense. After the Master had finished expressing his gratitude, he ascended the seat and offered incense.
Having completed the prayers for the Emperor’s long life, he spread his sitting mat. Once the Chan Master Jingyin Jingzhao had struck the wooden mallet, the Master said:

"Are there any gentlemen from the five lakes, eminent streams of those who have realized the Dharma? Come forth before the assembly and together propagate the Buddhist service. He then asked: [Question]...

In the past, at the sublime assembly on Vulture Peak, the Great Dharma Wheel was turned according to capacities; this morning, as the Field for Selecting Buddhas opens, I extend my hand, wishing to propagate the Buddha-work.
The Master said: "Where the incense smoke rises, let the great assembly behold it together. A monk said: "The Dharma rain falls everywhere, moistening the realms of sand;
all living beings rely upon the grace of the One Person. The Master said: "Henceforth, you must not speak erroneously. The monk said: [Silent].
This may be called "hearing what has not been heard before. The Master asked, "What is this matter that you have heard?

The monk said, "Relying on a single drop of Caoxi’s water from the Master, I shall bring rain to the four seas to repay our Sovereign. The Master said, "A clever monk! [The monk] asked: [Note: The original text contains a fragmentary question at the end, which is translated here as a concluding inquiry.]
The Sage Emperor, with hands folded in ease upon the imperial dais, recalls the time when the Buddha gave his entrustment at Vulture Peak. Today he issues an edict for the Master to propagate Prajñā;
may you open the gate of skillful means to resolve the multitude of doubts. The Master said: "The phrase that cuts off the flow is simply handed over as it is.
The monk said: "A single word transcends beyond the limit of *Avīci*; to stand on tiptoe and praise *Tiṣya* in vain is mere labor. The Master said: "Thirty years..."

Do not misunderstand this later. A monk asked, "In the past you were a guest beneath the forest trees; now you are a man of the imperial capital. I do not know if these two states are the same or different.

The Master said, "The single moon is in the sky, yet its reflections are contained within all the waters. The monk said, "Without leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he has already descended into the royal palace;
without emerging from his mother’s womb, his work of saving beings is already complete. The Master said, "The true does not conceal the false; the crooked does not hide the straight."
Question: Within the nine-layered city, there is nothing that is not the awakening of every touch; before the Hall of the Bright Moon, the signs of the Dragon Flower have already appeared.

Since this was not obscured at that time, I request the Master to grant me an encounter. The Master said: "The bells and drums of the six streets resonate with a deep *dong-dong* sound; this very place is a world spread in gold. The monk said:
"I am no longer aware of when, starting from the eastern side of the city, I first gave rise to the original resolve. The Master said: "The incense burner..."
Where the smoke penetrates, a wind arises that sweeps across the earth. A monk said, “One might say: ‘The Sage’s grace moistens ten thousand li;

joyful qi stirs at a thousand gates. The Master said, “Having prostrated, withdraw. The monk said, “I know that flowers in the Imperial Garden are difficult to pluck, yet one will not cease until the fragrance is secured.
The Master said, “You have already spoken. [A monk] asked, “The lush, auspicious qi of the Golden Palace; the sweeping frost—”
The wind, jade dew, and autumn—precisely at such a time, how shall we discuss this when Zen practitioners meet?

The Master said, "The lion yawns; the elephant king roars. The monk said, "The dragon pavilion and phoenix hall radiate brilliance at every glance; the jeweled chimes and golden bells all sing of the Emperor’s virtue.
The Master said, "The Great Gate of Giving is open; enter and investigate all at once. The monk said, "Your kindness is great."
"I do not know how to repay [this favor]. With a single incense burner and its coiling smoke, I pray for the longevity of the Yao Dynasty. The Master said, "Listen and see.

The Master continued, "I have presumptuously received the Imperial decree and come to occupy Huilin Temple. Having traveled a long distance of over three thousand li, now that I have arrived at the Imperial Capital, my spirit is wide open and clear.
Why is this? The pavilions and terraces rise in emerald green; the halls and stupas interlace their light; the broad avenues and thoroughfares..."
The crimson gates and magnificent halls were no different from Sudhana’s ascent of Maitreya’s pavilion; everywhere was sublime, and all was adorned.

The Flower Treasury world was perfectly luminous, with principal and attendant elements interlacing; countless dharma-gates were suddenly realized within a single hair-pore, encompassing the realms of infinite lands.
The verification is right before your eyes. I venture to ask you, venerable practitioners of dhyāna: what is this matter before your eyes?

He then looked at the assembly and said, "Do you understand? If you can realize it here, let us verify it together. If you do not yet know its limits, I shall hand over the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye face-to-face.
After a long silence, he said, "The path ahead of Mount Kukkuṭapāda is not far; Kāśyapa has attained it."
The essence lies in this very moment.
As the hall is opened and the Dharma is expounded, we offer our highest prayers for the Emperor’s person to live ten thousand years.

We humbly wish that the sky of Yao may forever cover all, and the sun of Shun may eternally shine with clarity. May the ocean of blessings be equal to the vast deep seas, and the mountain of longevity be loftier than Mount Song and Mount Hua. May you be protected and sustained.

The Three Jewels govern the myriad regions, further increasing the prosperity of the imperial lineage and expanding the flourishing of the sovereign’s domain. May you long establish universal compassion;
I humbly pray that you will take care of yourself. Question: Before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring flowers in their beaks to offer him?
The Master said: "Six times six is thirty-six. The monk asked: "After he had seen him, why did they no longer bring flowers? The Master—
[The Master] said, "Six times six is thirty-six. The monk said, "It would not be understood without you, Master. The Master said, "In India and here in this land.
[The monk] asked, "An ancient said, 'Rolling up the curtain removes the obstruction; closing the door gives rise to hindrance. I do not know what the meaning of this is. The Master said:
[The Master] stepped on the sounding hammer, which was as hard as iron. A monk asked, "What is it like when one goes forth in this very manner?

The Master said, "Wrong. The monk then shouted; the Master struck him. A monk asked, "The ancients said: 'Words do not unfold the matter; speech does not meet the occasion. He who receives the words perishes;
he who lingers in the phrases is deluded. How do you, Reverend, benefit people? The Master said, "The golden crow is swift; the jade hare is fast. The monk...
[The student] asked, "What is it like when one simply goes thus? The Master said, "Look after five days. The Master continued, "Words do not unfold the reality;
speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded.
When a patch-robed monk reaches this point, what more is there to do? How would it be to wear a bamboo hat, don a straw raincoat, cast a straight line, and drift in a light boat?"
Seeking out wise companions, I have not yet been able to rest. Since the monkey returned to the green peaks, I cast aside my hook and overturned my boat;
let the Xiang River flow through as many clear autumns as it may. *Du!* (A cry of realization)
Ascending the hall, he said: "A single stroke of the great sound encompasses the eight directions; a single edict put into practice brings a clear breeze across ten thousand miles.
The essential point of the school is laid bare, and the tradition of the lineage is extensively expounded. Cast forth before our eyes, its light flows into the great ocean;

its majesty encompasses the three realms, and its virtue covers the four quarters. Lofty and towering above humans and devas, it responds to things with an empty mind—neither within nor without, penetrating the ten directions, perfectly round."

Pervading all that appears before us, the Buddha-activities extend both vertically and horizontally. A drop of water from the eaves is the wondrous gateway of Avalokiteśvara; rain falling across the vast sky is the realm of Mañjuśrī.

Do not ask whether Potalaka is near or far; at the eastern edge of the City of Awakening, the gates of the multi-storied pavilion stand open. Look with eyes wide awake! *Tu!* (A sharp exclamation of realization).

Ascending the hall, he said: "Excellent, all you venerable Chan practitioners! One question, one answer—how brilliant! How exhilarating! The place of questioning is like a spark bursting forth from within a stone;
the place of answering is like a thunderclap in the azure sky. It appears suddenly and vanishes in an instant.
Unless one is a patch-robed monk who possesses the *śakrābhilagna* eye at the crown of his head, reaching this point, one cannot help but mistake the head for the tail. Therefore..."
"O, you are born and I am born; you kill and I also kill. The mechanism of birth and killing in the Wheel-Turning King races back and forth like a flash of lightning.
He ascended the hall and said: "The head is round like heaven; the feet are square like earth. His ancient countenance is rugged and imposing—this is the spirit of a true man. He kicked [the seat].
He overturns Mount Sumeru and tramples the waters of the ocean; even Śakra and the Dragon Kings have no place to hide their bodies.

Then he picks up his staff and says, "Come here and try to evade me on this staff! *Du!* No matter what supernatural powers or transformations you employ, in the end, you must come to this very spot."
He struck the ground once with his staff and ascended the hall, saying:
"Beside the Gusu Terrace, one does not speak of spring and autumn; before the eyes of a monk, how could one discuss the profound and the subtle?
One can only wear clothes and eat food, enjoy the water and look at the mountains, see the stars at night and the sun by day, and with both hands hold the plow in the water."
Reaching down past the knees—such was the prediction on Vulture Peak. How could it have ever been different from this day throughout kalpas as numerous as dust motes?
Entering the hall, he said: "A single phrase cuts off the flow; ten thousand functions are instantly pared away. Gain and loss, right and wrong—let them all go at once.
If you can understand it thus, then please return to your quarters."

Ascending the hall, he said: "Look! Look! A brilliant, auspicious light shines, illuminating the great trichiliocosm—ten billion lands as numerous as motes of dust, ten billion great oceans, ten billion Mount Sumerus, ten billion suns and moons, and ten billion sets of four continents.
Even down to lands as minute as motes of dust, they all manifest simultaneously within this light. Do you see it, worthy ones? If you do see it..."
"I grant it. I allow you that your kinsman is at Rui-guang. If you do not see him, do not say that Rui-guang does not shine.

[He] concluded with "Chán" (Investigation). Ascending the hall, he said: "Within the tip of a single hair, one manifests a jeweled royal land; sitting within a mote of dust, one turns the Great Dharma Wheel.
Holding up his staff, he said: "This staff is a mote of dust. How can you speak of the principle of turning the Dharma Wheel?"
Today, this mountain monk, not sparing a single hair on his brow, shall explain it through for all of you. When he lifts it up, the waters of the ocean surge into waves and Mount Sumeru trembles;
when he lets it down, the four seas are calm and clear, and heaven and earth are serene and still. I dare ask you all: [what is it?]
Now tell me: is it when you pick it up? Or is it when you let it go? To hesitate between severing and not severing—this is a double-layered public case.
(He strikes the meditation seat once with his staff.)
Ascending the hall, he said: "A thousand different forms all come down to this: they reside upon the tip of a single thread. He then lifted up his staff and asked, "Do you understand?
One becomes the infinite; the infinite becomes one. The Tathāgatas of the ten directions all transcend together in this very way.
If you can grasp this, your studies as a practitioner are complete. If you still do not understand, why need you suppress yourself? He struck the meditation seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A cool breeze blows; the red sun shines. This realm is serene—whom would it not please? Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva proclaims it for us:
in the nine thoroughfares, buyers and sellers vie with one another in their cries. Feet do not stop; hands do not rest. Within the realm of Vairocana, its function is clear and distinct.
Since time immemorial, all the sages have been nothing other than this. Do not give rise to despondency or disparage yourselves. Study!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "It is the coldest season of late winter; coming and going are no different. A thousand mountains, ten thousand peaks, are covered only in lingering snow.
When Zen practitioners meet, what can they possibly explain? Each of you, please return to your quarters and rest as circumstances allow.
If you treat this as meeting Bodhidharma while lost, it is much like adding grit to your eyes."
The Chan Master Juehai of Huilin Chan Monastery at Da Xiangguo Temple in Tokyo was named Rujiong. His secular surname was Zhong, and he was a native of Jurong in Jiangning Prefecture.
When his mother first became pregnant with him, she repeatedly dreamed of a monk sitting upright in her bedchamber; she consequently abstained from meat and strong flavors.
When her husband questioned her persistently, she told him of her dreams. Her father said, "If you truly give birth to a son, you should renounce him [to the monastic order]."
When the Master was still a child, his mother took him to Mount Zhong to pay homage to the image of Master Zhi. The Master immediately wept and refused to return home.
His mother, realizing this was due to past events, permitted him to leave the household life under the venerable monk Huaiyi of that monastery.

Later, he received full ordination under Chan Master Baoxin and proceeded to the Dharma seat of Chan Master Huai of Chiyang, where he was instructed to contemplate the cause of the state before mental conditions had arisen.
Through these conditions, he attained awakening. He served as an attendant for several years and deeply penetrated the profound essence of the teachings.

Initially, he resided at Jianfu Monastery in Changzhou; next, he resided at Shanguan Monastery in Yixing; then he returned to Jianfu. Later, he resided at Fusheng Monastery in Beijing and Falong Monastery (the Dharma King) in Xijing.

The Chancellor, Duke Han Jiong, and the Grand Preceptor, Duke Wen Yanbo, both held him in high esteem and veneration. In his later years, he received an imperial decree to reside at Hui... [Monastery].
On the day Lin opened the hall, Emperor Zhezong dispatched an imperial messenger to bestow incense. After the Master had finished expressing his gratitude, he ascended the seat and offered incense.
Having completed the prayers for the longevity of the Emperor’s reign, he spread his sitting mat. Once the Chan Master Fayun Yuan Tong had struck the gavel, the proceedings concluded.
The Master said: "Each person faces every other face-to-face; this is much like those at Shaolin gazing at the wall. Each pair of eyes looks directly into the other;
how is this any different from the entrustment at Vulture Peak? O worthy ones, it is truly profound and majestic, manifest and revealed all alone.
Is there among you any monk who can provide verification? At that time, a monk stepped forward and asked: "For the sake of the nation, [please] open..."
[The monk] entered the hall and said, "I pray to hear the essentials of the Dharma. The Master said, "The light of the Three Vehicles illuminates the Buddhas and Patriarchs;

a single phrase settles heaven and earth. The monk said, "The brilliant sun of heaven shines before the window; the pure wind pervades the seat. The Master said, "There is no different grass before one's eyes; it does not obstruct the view of coming and going.
The monk said, "Were it not for the eye opened at the crown of the head, who would know that this kindness is difficult to repay? The Master said, "A draught."

[The Master] said, "Indeed. The monk asked, "The fragrance was transmitted from Vulture Peak to the Eastern Land; the Yunmen lineage is established in the Imperial Capital. Today, the site of enlightenment is grandly opened;

I pray that the Master will again bestow upon us a skillful means. The Master said, "Those of superior capacity awaken at the moment of hearing the words; the Great Way is perceived before one's eyes.
The monk said, "If this is so, then Yuanzhao has now departed the Golden Realm, and in the monastery of Xianglan, the flowers of awakening bloom once more. The Master said, "..."
"Do not look askance. A monk asked, "What is the realm of the imperial capital? The Master said, "Majestic are the twin towers piercing the Milky Way;
drifting are the auspicious clouds covering the ninefold palace. The monk asked, "Who are the people within this realm? The Master said, "The two palaces are at peace, as secure as solid rock;
the myriad nations turn their hearts toward home, for there is an old minister. A monk asked, "The ancestral gate has opened wide, gathering the multitude of the wise."
The decree having been issued, he requested the Master to give a single shake [of the staff]. The Master said, "A green serpent roars from within its case.
The monk said, "This student’s stepping back is precisely it. The Master said, "A white rainbow soars high across the heavens. The Master further said:

"By imperial command, I, a subject-monk, am to open the hall for the sake of the nation, to circulate the Ultimate Way and awaken both humans and devas. Now, as for the Ultimate Way, it cannot be conceived through thought..."

It is unfathomable; it cannot be sought through conceptual thought. Those who apply themselves with diligence have yet to see it; those possessed of eloquence and wisdom remain utterly ignorant of it.
If one were to understand it clearly, only then would one know that the Way of every Buddha is the same, and that past and present do not differ.

What is right and what is wrong? What is heterodox and what is orthodox? It manifests existence where there is no existence, as remote as a dream; it achieves what is unachievable, appearing as if accomplished, yet vanishing like an illusion.

Abiding thus, they arise and cease from the source of emptiness; in every dharma there is no knowing. They manifest diverse forms according to the ocean of transformations, while conditions and objects remain free from dependence.
Those who realize this can repay the unrequitable debt of grace and assist in the transformation of non-action. O virtuous ones!
The transformation of the Unconditioned has been heard by the entire nation. Furthermore, what is the phrase for repaying this kindness? After a long silence, he said:

"The intent of the Three Vehicles is difficult to manifest; with a single impartial word, we celebrate Great Peace. On this day, the *Prajñāpāramitā* is circulated and wondrous goodness is universally gathered.
We offer our highest prayers for the Imperial Majesty’s person: may the precious throne remain eternally firm, and may the phoenix calendar [prosper].

Ever new and enduring, like the sun and moon illuminating all, and like heaven and earth encompassing and supporting all; your station exalted as the North Pole, your longevity equal to the Southern Mountain.
We humbly pray that you will cherish yourself and remain in good health.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The azure sky is pure and cloudless; the autumn heavens are bright with the moon. The long river is as clear as a silken ribbon; the pure breeze comes without ceasing.
The man of the Way beneath the trees is profound; as we gaze upon one another, our hearts are mutually delighted.

O worthy ones, what was just spoken of—the pure breeze and the bright moon—is still a matter within the gate of provisional transformation. What, then, is the matter from the standpoint of the man of the Way?"
After a long silence, he said: "Leisurely coming to the stone, I gaze at the flowing stream; wishing to wash my Zen robes, yet there is no dust. *Chan.* He ascended the hall and said:
"The boundless ocean of meaning all returns within a single glance; the forms and appearances of the ten thousand phenomena are entirely contained within the sphere of his illumination.
When you all encounter them and strike against them, why do you not recognize it? After a long silence, he said: "Do not—*chan*."
"What a strange mountain monk, making such a fuss! Time passes as swiftly as a flying arrow, pressing us on from all sides. Take care! He ascended the hall and said:
"The sun rises over the connected mountains; the full moon faces the door. It is not that there are no words, but I do not wish to reveal everything at once.
He then asked, "Is there anyone here who can fully reveal it? After a long pause, the assembly remained silent. He then took up his staff and said, "If you try to..."
[The Master] deliberated, then pierced [the air] through his cheek and struck the incense stand.

He descended from his seat and ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said: "When the myriad functions have all ceased, what is the nature of the body? A single point of numinous light merges with the Great Void.
Through kalpas as numerous as dust motes, it has never undergone change. Monks, do not labor in vain. He then called to the assembly, saying: "To save effort."
"Bring me a phrase from the Way! The assembly was silent. The Master said, "Return to the hall and drink tea. He ascended the hall.
After a long silence, he said, "On pure ground, one must strictly avoid scattering sand or dirt. Although gold dust is precious, alas, it cannot be placed in the eye.
Do you understand? Even if one’s realization were equal to that of Nāgārjuna, one’s eloquence like that of Aśvaghoṣa, and one’s wisdom surpassed [all others]..."
Śāriputra, when you arrive here, not even a single point will be of use. Why is this so? "The jade of Bian was originally without flaw;
Zhang Yi deceived the King of Qin. *Chan*.
Ascending the hall, he held his staff horizontally across his chest and said, "In the kingdom of Magadha, Kāśyapa personally carried out this command.
Today, this mountain monk must not add further mud upon the existing earth. He struck the incense stand and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The eyes are as pure as the blue lotus; the radiance contains white jade.

If you can penetrate this point, it will be no different from a divine pearl shining in all four directions, penetrating through the ten directions. The precious mirror is impartial; the beautiful and the ugly are naturally distinguished.
Even so, though it may be thus, dragons and snakes are easy to distinguish, but it is difficult to deceive a patch-robed monk."

Ascending the hall, he remained silent for a long while, then said: "Do you understand? When the auspicious rain comes in season, the summer heat subsides; sitting in meditation in the Zen hall is just like autumn.
When will the fires of the weary mind be extinguished? Simply by resting in non-mind, one may find peace."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The divine mechanism flashes forth; it is presented face-to-face. A flash of lightning is hard to catch; a spark from flint cannot be stayed.
Even if you can realize it in this way, you are not yet truly brilliant. He struck the floor with his staff, drew a line, and said:
"All the monks under heaven retreat eight hundred paces. Those who hesitate will find their faces scorched by the fire. He struck the incense stand once.
The Chan Master Guangzhao of Changlu Chongfu Chan Monastery in Zhenzhou was named Yingfu. His secular surname was Jiang, and he was a native of Qingliu in Chuzhou.
He left the household life and received full ordination under Chan Master Chengtai of Baoning Chan Monastery in Jiangning Prefecture.
He traveled far to attend the Dharma assembly of Master Huai at Mount Tianyi, where he entered the inner chamber for instruction and attained awakening, profoundly mastering the essential tenets.

Initially, he resided at Gānlù in Rùnzhōu; subsequently, he moved to Chánglú. Later, he was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Zhìhǎi Chan Monastery, but he firmly declined and would not accept.
[The questioner] asked: "I grant that you, Elder Brother, have understood the Tathāgata Chan; however, as for the Patriarchal Chan, you have not even dreamed of it. I wonder—"
"Is Tathāgata Chan the same as or different from Patriarchal Chan? The Master said, "A single arrow passes beyond Silla.
When the monk hesitated, the Master gave a shout. The monk asked, "What is it like when one recognizes the treasure within the robe? The Master said, "Try bringing it out and show me."
The monk extended one hand. The Master said, "There is no need to point east or draw west; where is the treasure?
The monk said, "How can it be that the student does not put it to use? The Master said, "Try using it then. The monk gave a single stroke with his sitting cloth.
The Master said, "The assembly will laugh at you. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "His face is like the full moon. The monk said, "What is the underlying meaning?"
"What? the Master said. "It shines everywhere throughout the world. The monk asked, "What is the place of practice (dōjō) wherever one is?
The Master said, "The nature is like white clouds unfolding and rolling back; though it responds to things in all directions, it cannot be bound.

The monk said, "If that is so, then the pine by the mountain stream is pure and cool, and the morning moon shines upon the long river. The Master said, "When the mind reaches stillness, a thousand anxieties cease; when the nature is clarified, it lies beyond the mundane world."
"Lamp-light. The monk hesitated. The Master said, "Ten myriad *yojanas* away. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Holding the dragon pearl in the palm of one's hand; encompassing the myriad phenomena within the breast; realizing the entire Dharma-realm before one's eyes;

pointing to the great trichiliocosm at the limit of one's own body. All is blended into a single essence, a perfect mirror without end. It encompasses the two polarities of heaven and earth and contains all things."
It accommodates all phenomena. Such a Dharma is wondrous when investigated to its depths and profound when explored to its limits.

When the principle of profundity and wondrousness manifests before one, the sentiments of both ordinary beings and sages are suddenly extinguished. It is perfectly integrated and unimpeded; it shines through with clarity and impartiality; it is distinct and resolute, leaving no gap between past and present.
Even were the former sage Dīpaṃkara or the Great Awakened One, Śākyamuni, to preach the Dharma for the benefit of sentient beings, they could not forget this.

The Essential Meaning: To engage in such discursive interpretations is to bury the ancestral style. Why is this so? One must simply have clouds rising on the southern mountain and rain falling on the northern mountain.
Entering the hall, he said: "Clouds roll away from the thousand mountains; dust clears across ten thousand miles. The vast sky is revealed alone; the Dharma-realm is transparently luminous. All.
Do people still see it? If you have not yet reached the reality as it is, do not be careless.
Only when the light is released from the crown of your head will you finally believe that the events of the "Ordinary Age" (Pǔtōng nián) were not transmitted from the Pamir Mountains. Take care.

Ascending the hall, he called to the assembly, saying: "The Ultimate Way is vast and open, neither partial nor biased. Sometimes it rolls up, sometimes it unfolds; sometimes it points, sometimes it palms.
Relaxed and expansive, it follows conditions; numinous and bright, it shines alone. It universally covers the sands of the Ganges, its light containing the myriad phenomena.
He then looked back at the assembly and said: "The spiritual traces of the thousand sages are but signposts for later generations."
Ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The rivers and mountains wind around the balustrade, appearing as if they were a screen of ink and water;
the halls and pavilions soar into the void, as magnificent as the grottoes of immortals. The myriad phenomena of the universe interpenetrate like the ocean-seal;

a single path of divine light is utterly without obstruction. Do you all understand? After a long silence, he said: 'In the vast and empty space between heaven and earth, standing alone, what limit can one gaze toward? "
[The Master] entered the hall. Looking at the assembly, he said: "Why is this [state] such that it cannot be gathered together, nor scattered apart;
the wind cannot enter it, water cannot wet it, fire cannot burn it, and a sword cannot cut it? What is this? [He asked] to the assembly: "Do not..."
"Is there a monk with a nail-like beak and an iron tongue who will try to settle this for me? Is there anyone?
After a long silence, he said, "If there is none, I have lost today. He remained standing for a long time.
Chan Master Zhiquan of Qixian on Mount Lu was surnamed Gao and was a native of Qiantang. By nature he was pure and his will was serene;

his mind was quick, yet his speech was reticent. He studied under Chan Master Huai of Tiantai. One day, upon seeing a craftsman pulling a log and hearing his shout, he attained awakening and subsequently received formal certification.
He emerged from seclusion at Fahua in Longshu and later moved to Qixian. This was in the first year of the Yuanyou era.
On the nineteenth day of the first month of that year, he took leave of the assembly. Having bathed and changed his robes, he sat in meditation and passed away. Five-colored śarīra were obtained.
A monk asked, "What is the one phrase by which you, the Master, benefit others? The Master said, "Excellent. The monk said, "I thank the Master for this instruction. The Master said, "..."

A monk asked, "What is the matter that transcends [this world]? The Master said, "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger.
The monk said, "In that case, when the dragon meets the water, his spirit increases; when the tiger encounters the mountain scenery, his ferocity intensifies.

The Master said, "But what about bringing forth clouds and causing rain? The monk immediately gave a shout. The Master said, "Is there anything more? As the monk hesitated, the Master rebuked him with a shout.
[The Master] said, "I am thinking of the Du family. A monk asked, "What is the original mind? The Master said, "Bending the eastern fence to patch the western wall.
The monk said, "If that is so, then today’s meal is finished. The Master said, "Step back and take care.

The Master said, "Puxian transforms the Jin River; Wenshu flourishes on Mount Wutai. The monk said, "Better not to have such good things at all. The Master said, "I will break the donkey’s waist."
Ascending the hall, he said: "This mountain monk has no Buddha-dharma; I simply let things take their course as time passes. Morning after morning the sun rises in the east;
night after night it turns behind the western mountains. When the clouds gather, the valleys are still; when the rain falls, the distant peaks appear low.
Once every three years we meet a spring; the rooster crows at the fifth watch. *Chan*."
Ascending the hall, he said: "To hear the two words 'Buddha-dharma' is already to defile one's ears and eyes.

Ascending the hall, he said: "To grasp the essential subtlety, the incense pillar frowns; to speak beyond the conventional, the tortoise turns toward the fire.
To be straightforward and free from affairs, how could praising or disparaging the ancients save one? O Zen practitioners, apart from this, is there anything else to deliberate upon?

"Yangma! Is it not that a large month has thirty days and a small month has twenty-nine? Is it not that when spring comes, the grass grows green of its own accord?

Ascending the hall, he said: "What kind of thing is this that is so stubborn, so dull-witted, so brazen, and so fickle? He clapped his hands and laughed loudly, saying:
"Today’s core reality—though the Yellow-Faced Gautama were to have a mouth all over his body, he could not even begin to explain it.
He stood for a long time.
Ascending the hall, he said: "For a long time, this mountain monk has not engaged in conversation with the assembly. Why is this?

Ascending the hall, he said: "Deshan said, 'I will strip you of your head-cage and unload your shoulder-yoke, so that you may become a true person—one whom the three realms do not contain and the six paths do not encompass.

Is there still blood beneath your skin? You have been thoroughly deceived by them.
Today, when I speak thus, it is as if I am increasing your delusion over a trivial matter. Take care."
Shuzhou Shanggu was Chan Master Sanzu Hui’s place of birth, being from Qiantang Lin’an.
Shanggu Baoshan was his residence. Chonghui was his Dharma name. Yuanzhi was his Zen title.
The Venerable Tiandi was his Dharma heir. Transcendent awakening and fierce acuity were his wondrous nature.
To speak plainly, he was one who brushed away worldly sentiments. As for the Master’s character, it was perfectly enlightened and perfectly penetrating; such were his spiritual companions.
From this, the Master’s Way may be known. Lord Jia Yi, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, honored him with the etiquette due to a teacher.
Though over seventy years of age, he lived as a true hermit, free and unburdened.

Entering the hall, he looks at the assembly and says: "When wisdom is all-pervasive, it does not reflect; how can the dust of worldly entanglements find a place?

Chan Master Faben of Baofu Temple in Huzhou was the son of Lu Shi, a prominent local family in Hangzhou. From birth, he was exceptionally bright and quick-witted.

He read widely across the various scriptures and was refined in his literary compositions. He took particular delight in the Ultimate Way (*tīdao*), and upon reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, he attained awakening to the nature of wisdom (*jìxìng*).
He immediately cast off worldly entanglements and entered the monastic order (*zīmén*). Admiring the tradition of the patriarchs, he traveled far to rely upon the seat of a great master.
Chan Master Tiānyī Huái deeply approved of him. He first resided at Shòuśèng Monastery in Wújiāng, Suzhou. [There,] he asked: "When one Buddha appears in the world, all Buddhas..."
"Praising. The Preceptor has appeared in the world. Who is it that praises him? The Master said, "The nine heavens shed rain and dew;

"Do not resent the power of the spring. The monk said, "The great assembly bears witness. The Master said, "The wind of spring continues to cause disturbance without ceasing.
A monk asked, "When a flavorless discourse blocks the mouths of men, what is the phrase that blocks the mouth?
The Master struck him with his staff. The monk said, "In that case, this one phrase circulates, and gods and humans raise their ears in awe. The Master said, "Only..."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The golden wind rustles; the jade dew is chilling. The chrysanthemums uncoil their fragrant buds; the rice stalks hang with fine ears."
The times are clear and things are at peace; the village elders sing songs of joy. Everywhere they ascend to high places; everyone is filled with delight. O virtuous practitioners of meditation:
how could those who wear the patched robes of the forest not know the seasons?

If you remain in silent stillness, forgetting your physical form, and remain oblivious to the passing of time, thinking that in the depths of the emerald peaks you need not follow the four seasons, then even a single stick of sandalwood incense would be an unrequited kindness. [He] strikes the meditation seat and descends.

The Master said, "One, two, three, four, five, six. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Counting the blue-eyed barbarian monks."

[The Master] was insufficient [in his previous response]. He ascended the hall and said: "If one discusses this matter, it is difficult to clarify directly. The Three Sages cannot fathom it; the Ten Saints do not know it.

It would straightaway cause Mount Sumeru to shatter and the great ocean to dry up. I shall now open a single thread of the Way for you all to deliberate upon."

Tai-uyak (Atractylodes), Beihai Tianma (Gastrodia elata), Xinluo Fuzi (Aconitum carmichaelii), and Shenjin Cinnabar. After a long pause, he asked, "Does the assembly understand?

Chan Master Zihong of Ruiyan in Taizhou was surnamed Wu and was a native of that province. He received his monastic training at Zisheng Monastery on Qingfeng Peak.

He planned to retire into seclusion. His virtue was solitary and lofty; from beginning to end, he remained as one. A monk asked, "What is the Way?

raising his staff to travel far to the center of heaven. The monk asked, "What is the essential meaning of this? The Master said, "Mount Xionger is steep and towering, its color unchanged for a thousand ages. [The text ends here.]

He also granted permission. Moving freely in every direction—seven ways and eight ways—the frogs and earthworms die and live together. Entering the hall, he said: "Frost blankets the four fields;

at the lowest depths, one stands solitary and towering. Wandering through the dust-motes of all lands, one never departs from beneath one's own feet."
The Universal Gate opens wide; it is right before one's eyes. On the plains, mountain peaks stand in clusters; through the winding streams, clear waters flow.

Chan Master Wenxi of Longhua in Hangzhou later resided at Lulian Hermitage. He asked: "What is the realm of Lulian?"
The Master said: "A single path with weeds before the steps; several pine trees after the frost. The monk asked: "What is it like to be a person within this realm? The Master said:
"Clear away the paths of ordinary and holy beings; tread through the painted gate and come forth. The monk asked: "As for the matter of the supreme vehicle above, what is it like?
The Master said: "A single staff of *jǐlì*; its majestic power extends ten thousand miles. The Master then said: "O virtuous ones, tell me now—"

Do you understand thoroughly? After a long silence, he said: 'From time to time clarify the Patriarch’s intent; day after day, the pure breeze rises. Take care!"'"
Chan Master Zizhen of Yongtai in Chuzhou asked: "What is the white ox on the open ground?

If you are a superior traveler on the path, a practitioner of the fundamental Chan stream—even if you were to scatter white clouds with a shout and burst through the azure void, such an enjoyment still belongs to the gate of expedient manifestation.

Question: "The frosty wind begins to stir; the Patriarch’s command is now in effect. At such a time, what matter should one discuss? The Master said:

The Master said, "The green mountains are dotted with green.

North and south are in turmoil; the flames continue and the fragrance links together through the present and the past. Today, this mountain monk has personally encountered a single ladleful [of this teaching].
Ascending this seat, though there is no door from which to escape, he shall raise the profound wind of a thousand ages and revitalize the contemporary model of this era.
After a long silence, he said: "Look! Look! This mountain monk is about to pour a ladle of foul water over your heads;

I report this with earnestness to those guests who have not yet returned: when the moon is full in autumn, the frost is cold."
[The Master] entered the hall and said: "Day after day, day after day, each day hastens one toward old age. When cold, simply sit around the brazier; when weary, collapse with your clothes on.
To those who come and go, I offer this report: the treasure has always been within the house, yet you have never sought it there. Instead, you lean upon your staff and search outside the gate.
No matter how many years you spend searching, you will only produce weariness and vexation. It would be better to turn back and return home. He then departed.
He cleared away the weeds before the gate and said again, "All you practitioners of Chan, the entire world of the ten directions is grass.

How will you proceed? Then he returned to the hall for tea. Ascending the hall, he said: "For many days the sky has been clear; this morning it rains. The great earth, the mountains, and the rivers—there is nothing that is not universally so.
The bell is struck at three times; the drum is struck at two times. It is distinct everywhere; realize it at every single point. Then he spoke again.
Holding up his staff, he said, "All you practitioners of Zen, do you understand? All Buddhas of the three periods of time are entirely contained within this.
He struck the meditation seat once.
[This was] Chan Master Lan of Baoben in Huzhou, a successor of the Dharma lineage.
Chan Master Zhongji Kezun of Fuzhou addressed the assembly, saying: "Heshan and Puhua suddenly went mad; Beating drums and shaking bells, they put on a show.
The kalpa-fire blazes fiercely—time to brew tea; The mountain wind blows violently—best to enjoy the cool.
Four snakes share one basket—watch them at play; Two mice gnaw the vine—how lacking in self-awareness! The moon shines bright over the vast ocean—where has it gone?"
"The Golden Hall of the Vast Cold, the Silver Bed. *Du!* [He] descended from his seat. Entering the hall, he said:
"Last night, amidst a hazy spring dream, I suddenly encountered Huik'e. My arm ached, my feet grew cold, and my two brows knitted.

He then descended from his seat. Entering the hall, he said: "Tsk! Tsk! Tsk! What thing is that chirping at the bottom of the well?
Even the three thousandfold world system is nothing but a ghost cave. Tsk! Entering the hall again, he said: "Last night I got up at the fourth watch and laughed out loud, unable to stop.
Fortunately, it was a good sleep; the frost-bell struck and split into two pieces."
Chan Master Guangji of Shanglan Monastery at Chengtian in Hongzhou, a successor of Chan Master Shouming of Chenshan in Yuezhou, asked:

"Sprout. The Master said, "You have seen enough of the sights. He ascended the hall and, holding his staff horizontally across his chest, said:

[He] struck the incense stand once. As the Master was approaching the time of his passing, he took leave of the assembly, saying: "For those of us who are patch-robed monks, the matter of birth and death is great;

(Long pause. Chan Master Shengyin Zhi of Linping, Hangzhou, asked: "I know that you have long harbored a treasure within your bag; today it should be revealed."
[The monk] briefly borrowed [the text] to look at it. The Master said, "Square and round, there is neither inside nor outside; whether it be ugly or clumsy, let the guest loathe it as he will.

If one relies on the authentic command of the Patriarchs, even if a thousand variations are proposed for deliberation, one must directly break through the profound pivot of the golden lock.

The Master said, "Scabies, sores, and carbuncles. The monk said, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "One must not say..."
The Three Bodies and Four Wisdoms. Question: Whose song does the Master sing? To whom does the lineage of this school trace its roots? Master:

If held fast, it is continuous and without leakage; if let loose, rain falls and clouds rush.

The assembly said, "Keep your eyes open!

is there anyone who does not observe the New Year's retreat? The Master said: "There is. The monk asked: "I do not know who that person is. The Master said: "Outside the gate."
Jingang asked, "What is the tradition of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "The bell tolls and the drum resounds. The monk said, "That is it.
The Master said, "Three thousand in the morning, eight hundred in the evening. [Jingang] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The nine apertures are constantly flowing."
The monk asked, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this; how is it? The Master said, "Form, fragrance, taste, and touch. The monk asked, "What is 'A Single Tune from the Zither Terrace'?
The Master said, "A wooden man stands by the terrace; 'Ra-li' has never been heard. The Master continued, "Five, four, three, two, one—the barbarian monk cannot count them out.

Red. White plum blossoms. The spring mountains are layered in chaotic greens; the spring waters reflect a vast azure. When you meet [a master], do not ask about Zhaozhou’s barrier.

The Buddhas, as numerous as the motes of dust in the three-thousandfold world system, each preach the Dharma. They do not speak of existence, nor do they speak of non-existence."
I do not say it is neither existent nor non-existent; I do not say it is both existent and non-existent. Why? Because it transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations.
Meeting face-to-face, few recognize it at a glance. Last night, the frosty wind leaked its secret: the plum blossoms still cling to their cold branches as before.

The Master asked, "Are you a novice with a master, or a novice without a master? Zhengyan replied, "Setting aside for a moment the question of having or not having [a master], are you, Preceptor, a Chan master with a master, or a Chan master without a master?
The Master said, "I have been circumambulated by a gourd that has grown over my vine. Zhengyan said, "What do you mean?"
"Ma! The Master hesitated. The Master struck his sleeves and departed, saying, "Seeing the person is not as good as hearing of their reputation.

The Master laughed heartily. That evening, he entered the room for private instruction, but the Master did not grant him permission. The Master then offered this verse: "With a golden blade, he shaves off the black hair;

Chan Master Yuanming Zhengtong of Mount Lingyin in Hangzhou, successor to Chan Master Yunzhi Cijue of Lingyin in Hangzhou, asked:
"The imperial wind sweeps vast and wide; the Emperor’s Way is level and even."
When the Master was inaugurating the hall for the sake of the state, he asked, "With what shall I offer prayers for the Emperor? The monk said, "There is no answer beyond this question.
The monk said, "The student joins his palms at his chest and steps back three paces. The Master said, "I do not know where you will thank me for my impartiality. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Those who know gratitude are few. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "When walking at night, do not step on white [snow].

Chan Master Yongming of Baolin in Wuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Xianzhu of Baolin in Wuzhou, asked:
"The World-Honored One’s samādhi was not known by Kāśyapa; who knows the Master’s samādhi? The Master said:

To those who behold it with their own eyes, it is as if they have ascended to heaven. Facing the city walls before them and backed by forests and springs, everywhere one hears songs of imperial transformation.

What need is there to expound the subtle or discuss the profound? That single aperture pointing toward the Ultimate has not been transmitted by the thousand sages. I venture to ask you all: [Where is it?]

Chan Master Shousheng Liyuan of Mount Zhizhe in Wuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Chengtian Weijian of Wuzhou, asked:

The Big Dipper is hidden away; one finger points upward, striking the nostrils of Śakra; one finger points downward, piercing through the adamantine waters.
One finger before everyone’s eyes—what kind of business does it accomplish? After a long silence, he strikes the ground once and says:

On the thirteenth day of the ninth month in the tenth year of the Xining era, the Master bathed, changed his robes, and left behind this verse: *The numinous sword leaning against the void is cold.*
The light floated upward. "The Buddhas, Patriarchs, and demonic hordes are gathered by a single blade; with the moon upon his belt, he roars through the wind back to the precious casket.

The Iron Ox is startled and scattered at the head of the Qujiang River. Having finished speaking, he sat in the lotus position and passed away. When his body was cremated and the bones collected, five-colored śarīra were obtained.

he memorialized the throne for the master to be granted purple robes and a formal name. On the day of the opening of the hall, he was asked: "Universal knowledge is already complete; you have now attained Buddhahood."
The virtuous minister earnestly requested that the Abbot remain. The Abbot did not inquire, "How are your affairs? The Master said, "Lifted up, it is clear.
The monk said, "If so, then the ancestral lamp shall not be begrudged its long-night illumination; we offer this in gratitude during the peaceful times of our enlightened sovereign.
The Master said, "Thieves are but petty men. The monk said, "A true lion cub lets out a lion’s roar. The Master [nodded].
[The Master] said: "Two layers of public cases. A monk asked: "In the assembly on Vulture Peak in the past and today at Baima— are they the same or different?
The Master said: "It is perfectly clear; let me raise it again. The monk gave a clap. The Master said: "What are you doing? The monk said: "I do not yet understand the underlying meaning.
The Master then struck him. The monk asked: "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "You still speak with your mouth..."
[The student] murmured. The Master said: "The Ultimate Way has no location; does it not have no location? The Ultimate Word is inexhaustible; is it not inexhaustible?
To attain it, it is as clear as something before one's eyes; to lose it, there is a separation by the breadth of a hair.

Therefore, although the entire Tripitaka is not considered many words, how could the single silence at Vaiśālī be called speechlessness? You must know that Buddhas, patriarchs, humans, and devas are distinct."
It is not originally existent; yet neither is beauty, ugliness, length, or shortness originally non-existent. To realize this directly is still to be halfway there.
This matter must encounter a person of clear eyes for verification. Today, it may be said that my efforts have not been in vain;
by raising this up, I offer prayers for the imperial wind, so that both the sentient and the insentient may attain the patience of non-arising. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Spring..."
The mountain bamboo shoots and bracken are lush and thick. You should take the yellow millet and grind it through the night.
Do not say that this intention was not present in the West; the Patriarch is entirely within the alms bowl. *Chan*. Entering the hall, he said: "The Patriarchs did not understand Chan;
the Buddhas did not understand the Way. Studying the Way and studying Chan—everywhere there is such clamor. Some take jade for dust; some mistake stone for..."

"Treasure! Having attained 'one belly-full' through practice, you will needlessly give rise to affliction. If you do not give rise to affliction, understanding that [state] is like entering a field of wild grass.
I send word to those who study the Way through Zen: the white hair at the side of your head grows new year after year.

How much better it would be to come and work the fields with Damei to eat the rice we earn together—then the business of a lifetime of study is finished. Take care. He ascended the hall and said: "The end..."
The final phrase is like a vine leaning against a tree. As for the single opening toward the transcendent, it is as if Yan-ruo lost his illumination.
What is the essential point of this subtle and great Dharma-gate? For you, I shall sing a "Pusa Man" melody; it is but a leisurely tune for the human world. *Chan*. Entering the hall, he said:
"At the beginning of the thirty-six decades, at the start of the seventy-two seasonal signs—let us set aside the final phrase for now. Only...
"How do you speak the first phrase when it comes right down to it? [The Master] picks up his staff and says, "On the first day of the year, one grasps the brush;
all matters are auspicious. Swiftly, as by imperial decree! "Great assembly, when I, this mountain monk, proclaim it in this way, tell me:
does it still contain the intent of the Patriarchs? After a long silence, he says, "I remember Black Li of the Eastern Village; every year he personally writes it upon his gate."
[The Master] stepped forward, held up his staff, and descended from the seat.

Chan Master Xiaoxuan of Dingfeng in Jianzhou, a successor of Chan Master Shunzong of Guoqing on Mount Dongshan in Yuezhou, asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "Clouds."
[The Master] said, "It gathers the green of a thousand peaks. A monk asked, "How does one comprehend this? The Master said, "The rain washes the hundred flowers fresh.

A monk asked, "I, a student, have come before you; I beg the Master to grant me instruction. The Master said, "The river is clear as the autumn night moon; the wind sweeps away the dawn sky's rosy clouds. The monk said, [and remained silent].
"The moment a single phrase is heard, it shall circulate for ten thousand ages. The Master asked, "How do you understand this? The monk gave a shout;
the Master struck him.
[This concludes the record of] Chan Master Chenghao of Jingde Temple on Mount Yuyuan in Jingmen, successor to the Dharma lineage.
One day, Zen Master Wenqing of Linxi Xingjiao in Yingzhou said: "Six times six is thirty-six. In the east, the Jia-yi wood;
the Great Image of Jiazhou comes out of the pass; the Iron Ox of Shanfu enters Western Shu. *Pause.* "Study!"
Chan Master Xìn of Fuchang Temple in Jiangling, a successor of Chan Master Zūn of Jiaoshan in Lǐzhōu, asked: "Regarding the saying, 'One flower opens into five petals,' what is the first petal?"
The Master held up his sitting mat. The monk said, "Clouds arise in drifting flakes; raindrops fall in fine spray.
The Master said, "One does not feel pain, nor does one know injury. The monk said, "This is still the wind arising and the intent of rain.

What is the first leaf? The Master struck the sitting mat once. As he struck it once, the monk clapped his hands. The Master said, "Feel free to leap about as you please. A monk asked, "Before the lion has emerged from its cave..."
"How is it at that time? The Master said, "Ask further and see. The monk asked, "How is it after emerging from the cave? The Master said, "Grinding teeth and baring fangs.
The monk asked, "How was it before Bodhidharma had come? The Master said, "The great earth is entirely vast and boundless. The monk asked, "How is it after he came?
The Master said, "The clouds disperse, and every household has the moon. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The young man of the eastern house."
The monk asked about the Weaver Girl of the Western House. The Master said, "The student does not understand. The Master continued, "Casting aside the brush and tossing away the shuttle.
A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Heaven covers and earth bears. The monk said, "In that case, everything is contained within it. The Master said, "A-ye, A-ye.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "It is behind your head."
A monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "It is fortunate that you do not understand. If you were to understand, it would bring trouble upon this old monk.
He ascended the hall and said, "The weather is cold; I shall rouse the assembly. Otherwise, the Dharma seat will fall into neglect and the winds of our school will not be stirred.
The weeds at the triple gate grow deep and those coming and going have ceased their tracks. It is better, then, to prepare a simple feast for everyone. [He] slaughtered..."
In the open air, the white ox makes offerings to all people; the great assembly gathers around the hearth to sing the "Song of Non-arising.

After a long while, he says: "Listen attentively! Listen attentively! He ascends the hall and says: "Great Assembly! Great Assembly, lift up your heads! The Master says: "The wind and weather on South Mountain are brisk."
He then descended from his seat and ascended the hall, saying: "I have ascended this lion throne this morning merely to seek medical treatment.

All you practitioners who have come here have already been swallowed up by the sound of the drum. Is there anyone here who recognizes the illness? After a long silence, he said: "Is it not a case of deafness?
Now, each of you return to your quarters; once the sound has faded, the illness will be cured."
Chan Master Jingwu of Qingshan Monastery at Baizhang Mountain in Hangzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Foyin Liaoyuan of Yunju Mountain, asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Ask who?
The monk said, "I am specifically asking the Master. The Master said, "A hawk flies over Silla. [The monk] asked, "What is the New Year?"
The Master was paying homage to the Buddha-dharma. He said, "If you ask, you will know. The monk said, "The 'Shang Daren' (The Great Man Shang) begins from the very beginning.
The Master said, "When the Yang energy arises, there is no hard ground. The monk said, "With faith, it comes and goes; without partiality, it reaches from antiquity to the present.
The Master said, "Everyone turns their head to thank the Lord of Spring. A monk asked, "The ancient Buddha intersecting with the pillar—what stage of the teaching is this?"
The Master said, "The old man of Shaoyang has also spoken of this. The monk said, "Today I have my share.
The Master said, "It is very much like laboring in vain without merit. Ascending the hall, he said: "To speak is to move the lips; to act is to move the feet.
Even if you neither speak nor act—at such a time, it is still 'wrong, wrong. He struck the meditation seat once. Ascending the hall again, he said: "The single word of cause and effect reaches..."
Abiding according to conditions. If one were to calculate and speculate, there are one hundred and eight thousand [distinctions]. "Participate!

Chan Master Huìtài of Guǎngjiào on Shànquán Mountain in Chángzhōu asked: "It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making offerings to a single mindless person (wúxīn dàorén).
What fault do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have, and what virtue does the mindless person possess?"
Fú. The Master said, "Flowers fall because of attachment; weeds grow because of disdain. A monk asked, "I do not know whether this is one or two.
The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment the question of one or two, why are your nostrils in my hands? The monk hesitated.
The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master continued, "The Buddhas appeared in the world to extensively expound the Three Vehicles;

Bodhidharma came from the West to secretly transmit the Great Matter. Those of superior capacity transcend immediately upon hearing a single word; those of middling or inferior capacity must gradually clarify the ground of their own minds.
Whether by singing the Way in a single phrase, or unfolding it in three sentences, or responding skillfully to the capacities of others, [the truth is thus revealed]."

To establish many meanings and yet grasp only their essential pivot is to treat them all as flowers in the sky. To exhaustively investigate the source with a single phrase is to bury the ancestral Way.
I dare ask you all: what is the phrase that accords with the time and season? After a long silence, he said: "A faint cloud hovers over the Milky Way;
sparse raindrops fall upon the paulownia trees. *Chan*.
Cen Master Huikong of Guanghua at Cuiyan in Western Mountain, Hongzhou, was asked: "What is the Way? The Master said:
"One does not select the weeds in a field. The monk said: "Is this not where you, the Master, benefit people? The Master said: "Appointing according to one's capacity."
The Master said: "Yesterday the rain fell in torrents; this morning the sun shines brightly. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra—entirely enter the wild weeds.
Fortunately, it was thanks to Old Teacher Wáng who sent them out early last night. He raised his staff and said: "They are coming! They are coming! Have you not heard it said:
'In spring, there are no three days of clear weather'? He then descended from his seat.
Chan Master De Pu of Jingtu on Mount Miyen in Ruzhou asked, "What is the realm of Miyen?
The Master said, "A pure breeze rises atop the peaks of the hibiscus. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "An old villager sings before the altar of rain and dew.
[The monk] asked, "Regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage, how do you point it out? The Master said, "A new melody for an ancient tune."
"Who is the one who knows?
Chan Master Deqi of Chongfu Temple in Ruzhou asked, "Please, Master, proclaim the supreme vehicle of our school. The Master said, "How very clear it is!
The monk said, "Please grant us further expedient means. The Master said, "The wind that comes is deeply discerned. The monk said, "I, this student, prostrate."

"Thank you," [the student] said. The Master said, "You must not misunderstand. The Master continued, "If you can understand it right here, you will be able to enter a Buddha-land and sit within a site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
There, waterfowl and forest trees will together discourse upon this essential point, and towers, pavilions, and halls will jointly expound the True Vehicle.
You shall continue the lamp of the thousand sages that never ends, and illuminate the impartial flame that shines in all eight directions. Therefore, it is said: 'In heaven...'"

Heaven is the same; among humans, they are the same as humans. Is there anyone here who truly understands? After a long silence, he said: "The golden crow at the bottom of the water and the sun in the sky;
the pupils in one's eyes and the person standing before one."
Chan Master Zhonghe of Zhenru Monastery on Yunju Mountain asked: "What is the Buddha? The master said, "The place where you ask is clear.
The monk said, "Last night the pines and bamboos stirred up a pure breeze, blowing away two or three fragments of white clouds.
The master said, "Do not bump into the pillar. The monk bowed and returned to the assembly; the master sighed repeatedly.
Chan Master Chongsheng Youzong of Tong’an on Mount Lu ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he called to the assembly, saying, “This staff is the essence.
Striking the meditation seat, he said, “This is function. It reaches such a point that high and low are seen everywhere, and far and near all hear it.
At this very moment, tell me: is it divided or undivided? After a long silence, he said: “The oar is held horizontally across.”
The Flower Treasury World is not as vast as the palm of Vimalakīrti’s hand.
Chan Master Huaiji Zhenjue of Baolin Monastery in Wuzhou asked: "Regarding the staff of Deshan and the shout of Linji, I wonder whether they are the same or different.
The Master said, "Bring forth those who are true monks. The monk said, "I do not yet understand; I specifically request your instruction."
The Master said, "He is indeed sharp. A monk asked, "What is the Master’s phrase for benefiting others? The Master said, "There is a question and there is an answer.
The monk said, "I have heard what I had not heard before. The Master said, "As for that which was heard, how is it? The monk said, "Six ears do not share a secret. The Master said, "That too is so.
The Master further said, "The legacy of the wind of Shanhui has endured for five hundred years at Mount Yunhuang."
The form remains as it was; now the Patriarchal Command is being put into practice once more. A single phrase circulates throughout the great thousandfold world-system.
Tell me, O Great Assembly, what phrase is this? Is it the one that encompasses heaven and earth, cuts off all streams, and follows the waves?
*Hūṃ*. What connection is there? Since the time of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, it has never been moved. Today—
"One must not leak the true mechanism. Looking toward the assembly, he said, "If you go to other places, do not speak of this mistakenly.
Chan Master Deyan Renshou of Goose Lake Mountain in Xingzhou asked, "What is the environment of Goose Lake? The Master said:
A single pool of lake water turns emerald with the coming spring; several immortal geese return from beyond the heavens. A monk asked, "What is it like for one within this realm?
The Master said, "The sound of pines comes to my seat; mountain greens rise upon my robe.

The Master continued, "When many mouths all come forward to pose questions, that single point in the void makes it difficult to respond. Now, the Great Meaning is proclaimed once more: raise your eyebrows!"
Mao looked directly at him.

After standing for a long time, Chan Master Wanshan Zizhang of Mount Lu asked, "The Way prevails, so the Emperor’s edict is not transmitted; the times are peaceful, so all sing the Song of Great Peace.
What is this Song of Great Peace? The Master said, "The clouds have vanished and the sun and moon are bright; the snow has melted and heaven and earth [are clear]."
Spring. A monk said, "If that is so, then rain sprinkles the thousand peaks in their splendor, and the wind moves the ten-thousand-year-old branches.
The Master said, "The waters of the Xingjiang River are vast, merging with the azure sky; Mount Wulao stretches across the universe, its expanse wide.

The monk asked, "How was it before teacher and disciple had met? The Master said, "Dingguang beckoned from afar at Jinci; Zhiyi nodded his head in secret at Jiangling. The monk said, "Once they have met..."
"What then? The Master said, "Father and son share their intimacy; the honorable and the humble differ in their positions.
Zen Master Zongyou of Zifu in Hongzhou ascended the hall and said: "The more lofty the chant, the fewer those who can harmonize with it.
For nine years at Shaolin, one was as if mute. To even raise a brow is to have missed it. Today, this mountain monk releases [the sound] from the void."

[The Master] descended from his seat. Why was this so? Because when the Dharma is exhausted, there are no people. He ascended the hall and said, "Today at Longquan, I shall speak some entangling vines with you all.
After a long silence, he said, "From the vines and branches, even more vines and branches grow."
Chan Master Yue of Longxing Mountain in Yuanzhou asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed? The Master said:
"Since the time Bodhidharma divided the stream, all ten thousand branches have returned to one family. The monk said: "I do not yet understand;
I pray the Master will point directly. The Master said: "The four willow switches beneath Jiyun Peak."
Chan Master Zhiyin of Huangbo Mountain in Junzhou, a successor of Chan Master Zhengjue Benyi of Dongjing Zhikai, asked:
"It is not as good as a person practicing seated meditation who, in a single thought-moment, transcends the stage of Buddhahood."
"What is the Buddha-ground? The Master said, "The land of Śrāvastī. The monk asked, "I do not understand the meaning of this.
The Master said, "Gold spread out on all sides. Question: "What is the phrase for attaining power? The Master said, "The feet. The monk said, "I do not understand, Master.
The Master said, "One step forward, one step further. The Master said, "Before Vulture Peak, the pines and cedars drip with emerald green; the clouds and mists..."
Within the shadows, the water and rocks are pure and empty; these are entirely the gatehouses and courtyards of antiquity, the old family style of former days.

Why, then, do you say there is no place to avoid the cold or the heat? After a long silence, he said: "How can one blame others? Ascending the hall, he said: "To return to the root is to attain the essential meaning;

to follow after illumination is to lose the source. To the east is the kitchen and storehouse; to the west is the monks' hall—all of these are following after illumination. Returning to the root and attaining the essential meaning is [one thing]."
"How do you express this? After a long silence, he said, "Investigate! Ascending the hall, he said: "For forty-nine years he preached, bestowing grace upon birds and fish;
having traveled a hundred thousand leagues, he has awakened humans and devas. To each of these two old fellows, I would gladly give thirty blows of the staff.
Why? One speaks of the long and the short; the other utters gibberish. Nevertheless, for now—"
Letting this one move pass.
Chan Master De-long of Da-zhong Temple in Fuzhou, having received full ordination, traveled to study under Chan Master Yi, where he profoundly realized the essential meaning of the school.

When Prime Minister Wen personally and earnestly invited him to take charge of a monastery, he entered the inner quarters and attended upon the master; his disciples numbered eight hundred, and he ascended the hall to preach.
One day, he addressed the assembly, saying: "In the kingdom of Magadha, not even a drop of water could leak through; in the city of Vaiśālī, this decree was personally enforced.

Vertically it exhausts the three periods of time; horizontally it spans the ten directions. It sits and cuts off the heads of the Reward-Buddhas and Transformation-Buddhas; it draws a line that severs the worlds of self and other."
Therefore, more than two thousand years ago, the Great Teacher, the Tathāgata, by the power of his compassionate vows, manifested birth and descended into a royal palace.
He practiced on the Snowy Peaks and attained Perfect Enlightenment. Turning the Great Wheel of Dharma, he transcended words and language;

the direct intent of the human mind remains consistent across past and present, for diverse paths lead to the same destination. Then, looking to his left and right, he said: "The realms of humans and devas meet."
The guest and host are clearly distinct. Again, he called to the great assembly: "What is it like? When [a monk] raised his hand, he did not look back; this was already a mistake.
If you try to deliberate upon it, when will you ever awaken? He stood for a long time. Take care.
On the day Chan Master Shenyu first opened the hall at White Deer Mountain in Fuzhou, the head monk struck the gavel and said:

"In this Dharma assembly of dragons and elephants, you should contemplate the primary principle. The Master said: "As for the three peaks of Mount Hua and the nine branches of the Yellow River—does anyone here perceive them?
If one can perceive them in this way, what need is there for the ten-thousand-character mark upon the chest or the auspicious patterns on the feet?"
Lotus. At the site of enlightenment, he first attained perfect awakening. Yet, regarding this matter, there were surely those who knew the way and who collectively provided testimony.
When beginners and those new to the path had doubts and sought instruction, a monk asked: "Master, you have ascended the high and broad seat; please reveal the pivotal teaching of Shaolin.
He replied: "The crimson clouds pierce the azure heavens; the bright sun circles Mount Sumeru. The monk pressed further: "If that is so, then people..."

The heavens listened intently from the sidelines. He replied, “It is merely a waste of effort to stand and contemplate. The monk pressed further, saying, “Who knows that beyond the distant mist and waves, there is yet another way of thinking?
He replied, “Idle words. A monk asked, “Since the Cloud-Rider has ascended the Dharma seat, I pray the Master proclaim a single phrase of the *tánhuā* (dew-flower).
He replied, “The golden wind spreads across the fields at dawn; the jade dew hangs like pearls at night. The monk pressed further, saying, “If it is thus...”
"Then the dragon roars and mist rises; the tiger howls and the wind is born. [The student] replied, "The heavens are so high it is difficult to lean one's ear toward them.

[The student] pressed further, "If one does not ascend the tower, how can one know the vastness of the sea? He replied, "When have you ever dreamed of it? The Master then said, "Let us cease this dialogue for a moment.

Even if one could discern the core within words and conceal the pivot within phrases, with thoughts racing against one another, it would all be nothing more than drifting along the current. Why? Because I—"
Is the Way of the Patriarchs truly like this? If one is a practitioner of the highest capacity, they walk alone across the crimson heavens;

when facing the great function of the moment, they can seize and hold fast so that not a single drop leaks away, yet when they let go, waves surge forth across a thousand rivers. They sit upon the ground with full majesty, standing as steep as a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.

Such a person attains their own heroic spirit and carries the burden of the ancestral school. Even if one achieves such a state, it still does not fully measure up to the requirements of a patch-robed monk.
"Monk," he said, "tell me, what is so extraordinary about a patch-robed monk? After a long silence, he continued: "In the deep autumn, a thousand tombs under the curtain of rain;
at sunset, towers and terraces with the wind of a single flute."
