Compiled by [Song] Ming, the Dharma-transmitting Chan Master Foguo, Abbot of Fayun Chan Monastery in Dongjing, (Subject) Weibai.
The Door of Responding to Capacities:
Chan Master Huairang of Mount Nanyue,
the thirteenth-generation successor of Chan Master Huinan of Huanglong Mountain in Hongzhou.
Chan Master Zhaojue (Zhaojue Chanshi), whose name was Changzong, resided at Xinglong Chan Temple in Donglin, Jiangzhou. His surname was Shi, and he was a native of Yanping.

His mother dreamed that a foreign monk bestowed upon her a white lotus flower, and she subsequently gave birth to him. When he grew up, he relied on Baoyun Temple to leave the household life and receive full ordination.
He traveled to visit the Dharma seat of Master Nan (Nanyuan Huiyong) and knocked three times at his door. Master Nan then asked: "Who is it?"
He attained great enlightenment regarding the fundamental purpose [of the teachings]. After serving with diligence for several years, he was promoted to the position of head instructor.
He first resided at Letan and subsequently moved to Donglin, fulfilling the prophetic prediction of Master Huiyuan. His assembly numbered over five hundred.

Emperor Shenzhong issued an imperial decree for him to reside at the Zhihai Chan Temple within the Great Xiangguo Monastery, but he firmly declined and did not go. Having obtained permission to remain in retirement among the forest trees, Daewang of Seoguk submitted a special memorial on his behalf.
He was granted the Zen title Chiao (Illumination-Awakening). When his life came to an end, he sat in meditation and passed away; his entire body was interred to the left of the Yantan Pagoda.

On the day he opened the hall for formal teaching, after the head monk had struck the gavel, the Master looked to the left and right, remained silent for a long while, and then said: "The sound of the gavel has not yet fallen."
The Patriarch’s command has already been carried out; how much more so when the *ghanṭā* is struck to summon the assembly and announce that they shall observe?

To do so early would already fall into the second [level]. Those of superior capacity are like the empty space within the pupil of the eye; those of middling and inferior capacity have doubts and ask questions. Question: On this day, you open the hall for the sake of the nation;
with what Dharma will the Master repay the sovereign’s kindness? Master: White clouds seal the mountain peaks; the bright moon—

[The Master] reflected upon the Emperor’s mind. The monk said, “The Master has already repaid the grace of the sovereign; as for the matter of the Patriarch’s intent coming from the West, what is it like?
The Master said, “Do not seek beneath words; do not look for it within the mind. The monk said, “Now I truly believe that the Tathāgata once had these words:
‘At Huangmei today, I have finally come to know the mind. The Master said, “Who does not receive the power of grace? [The monk] asked, “How does one transform customs and change social mores?”
The monk did not ask immediately: "In the lineage of our ancestors, what is taken as the ultimate principle? The Master said: "Holding the Mohe sword crosswise, the whole body is revealed.
The monk said: "This is still but a bold statement. Please, Master, speak quickly that one phrase which cuts right through. The Master said:
"Who among them is the one who emerges? The monk said, "A true spiritual friend. The Master said, "Elsewhere, I would not let you pass. The monk said, "What do you mean by that?
The Master said, "The direct command has already been issued. A monk asked, "I do not ask about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West;
but how is it that the Vinaya was changed into Chan? The Master said, "The sun and moon within the jar; the mountains and rivers beyond the mundane world. The monk said, [silently].
Master Yuan did not bestow his prediction in vain. The Master said, "If it were Tao Yuanming, he would have knit his brows and returned home.

The monk said, "I did not ask about the transgression. The Master said, "The bell after the midday meal. [The monk] asked, "When the treasure hall strikes the drum of Chengtian, I request that you sing the song of peace.
The Master said, "Where the incense smoke rises, the pure breeze leads the way. The monk said, "The fourfold assembly has heard it all."
"A lofty air. [The monk] asked, "I do not know who composed the song to this? The Master said, "It only serves to make the barbarians laugh even more.
The monk said, "That was still the second level of function. The Master said, "Which one is the first level of function? The monk said, "A mistake. The Master said, "The assembly has eyes.
The monk stepped forward from the group, lifted up his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*), and said, "I ask the Master for an answer to this statement. The Master said, "Put it down."
The monk again made a gesture of drawing a sword. The Master said, "Withdraw. The monk said, "A seeker of the sword in years past;
today he meets a master. The Master said, "What kind of place is this? The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "Shout at me, do you? The monk shouted again.

The Master said, "Even if I let you go, how could that be right? He then struck him. [Another monk] asked: "If one does not clarify the profound principle after the phrase, then cease [seeking it] toward—"
Regarding the words "the ancestors were settled before speech," what was the essential point of the nine years at Shaoshi? How did Shen Guang’s three prostrations pass through [this barrier]?

The Master said, "The great earth cannot bear it up. The monk asked, "If so, as for 'the fine springwater connects with the veins of the sea' and 'the tall cypress enters the layers of the clouds,' how about that?
The Master said, "It is a separate family spring. He asked, "What is the Immovable Honored One? The Master said:
"Going downhill, one does not run; such swift opportunity is hard to encounter. A monk asked, "I do not ask about the tune of non-arising. Please, Master, play the lute's melody without strings.
The Master said, "Fingers idle, the Xiang River flows far; the solitary moon, the night hall is deep.

The monk said, "In the hall, the wind is cold and still; through the ages, the meaning is clear. The Master said, "Once again, it has been blown by the wind into another tune. A monk asked, "Of heaven and earth—"
Within, amidst the universe, there is a treasure hidden within the mountain of form. What is this treasure? The Master said, "The white moon appears; the black moon hides.
The monk said, "I have not merely heard its name; today I have seen it directly. The Master said, "Tell me, where is the treasure?
The monk said, "The doors of the ancient hall open and the light is brilliant; by the side of the white lotus pond are those who dwell in the community."
The Master said, "Discerning the treasure belongs to the blue-eyed barbarian. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun. The monk said, "I shall prostrate three times. The Master said, "Do not move.

Not long after, he aspired to travel and study, eventually finding his spiritual resonance at the Dharma seat of Master Huanglong Nan. Thereupon, he attained enlightenment; his practice and understanding became firm and profound, and he maintained his inner cultivation with natural ease.
He propagated the Way during his time, and the fourfold assembly turned their hearts toward him. In the eleventh month of the fifth year of the Yuanfeng era, he bathed.
He shaved his head and wrote a verse: "The exposed essence floats in life; the concealed essence sinks in death.

At fifty-three years of age, in the sixth, seventh, and eighth months, at Mount Nanyue and Tiantai, amidst pine winds and mountain stream snows. Cherish this, O connoisseurs! A blue lotus in a red furnace.

"Can it be sought and attained? Can it be sought by sitting idly and waiting for it? Can it be sought through deliberate effort and contrived action?

Xiao: "The shadow of the Tai star disperses as it approaches the clear Bian River. The monk said: "The grace is so deep that words fail. The Master said:

Why is this? On the ground of the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), not even a speck of dust remains; in the gate of true subtlety, how can verbal expression be established?

Therefore, one spreads the clouds of compassion to moisten all things and raises the torch of wisdom to illuminate the obscure. One manifests words that transcend speech as a discourse that is beyond saying.

The Master said: "Neither square nor round; neither above nor below. The braying of donkeys and the barking of dogs—throughout the ten directions, they are priceless.

"The direct source has been made clear to people; how, then, should those of middling and inferior capacities be instructed? The Master said, "The spine of the stone man flows with sweat.
A monk asked, "What is the person who is at ease amidst the dust of the world? The Master said, "While walking, it does not hinder one from swinging one's arms.
The monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "In the boiling cauldron, there is no place that is cold."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Śākyamuni appeared in the world, playing with the false as if it were real; Bodhidharma came from the West, taking the long and making it short.
Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout are like mirages used to satisfy hunger or the plum trees that quench thirst. In a world of pure peace, there is no hindrance to traveling by night.
Now, is there anyone here who can swallow up the Buddhas and Patriarchs and shatter the provisional city? After a long silence, he said: "Today..."
Having been thoroughly exposed by the great assembly, he ascended the hall and said, "It comes! It comes! After a long silence, he said, "It goes! It goes!
Ascending the hall again, he said, "My mouth is full of tongues, yet none can speak. The old barbarian with the blue eyes has a missing tooth right in the middle.
Ascending the hall once more, he said, "Look, look! This mountain monk is entering the Hell of Plucked Tongues. He pulled out his tongue with his hand and cried, "A-ya! A-ya!"
[Ya]. He ascended the hall and said: "When scolding one another, there are no good words; when striking one another, there are no good fists. Great assembly, you must simply act in this way."

Only then did he begin to strike blow after blow with piercing force and punch after punch with solid impact. Suddenly, having struck this faceless fellow, he was filled with a sense of exhilarating liberation.
Upon ascending the hall, after the attendant had finished burning incense, the Master pointed to the attendant and said:
The attendant has already finished preaching the Dharma for everyone. He ascends the hall and says: "The hundred rivers flow in different directions, yet all return to the sea;
the myriad paths differ from one another, yet all enter this school. He plants his staff firmly on the ground and says: "To heal the sore beneath the eyes, he gouges out the flesh from the heart.
He ascends the hall again and says: "On the road to Caoxi, the village elders sing songs; before the hall of the ancient Buddha, the travelers..."
The sleeves of the dance flutter; his feet tread solid ground, known to all under heaven. His nostrils reach the vast heavens—how can one discern them? He then said:
"Blowing the unperforated flute, he plays a melody beyond the profound; where in the Five Lakes shall one find a true知音 (zhīyīn—'one who knows the sound')?

He then gave a single clap. Entering the hall, he said: "For over twenty years, this mountain monk has carried his bag and borne his bowl, traveling throughout the world to seek out virtuous spiritual friends."

There were ten or more people, none of whom had any personal realization; they were like stubborn stones. The venerable masters we consulted likewise possessed no superior qualities that could benefit us.
From then on, for the rest of my life, I was merely a person who understood nothing at all—a truly pitiful state of affairs.
Suddenly, however, driven by the winds of karma, I arrived in Jiangning Prefecture. Without any cause, I was...
A person of high station should be driven to the crossroads to dwell in a dilapidated courtyard as a master of gruel and rice, receiving guests from all quarters.
Having no other recourse, he provides salt and vinegar according to his means; with sufficient gruel and sufficient rice, he passes the time in this manner.
As for the Buddha-dharma, however, he has not even seen it in his dreams.
Chan Master Xianqiong of Changqing on Mount Mufu in Yuezhou was asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Clay niches and molded images.
The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "Yellow scrolls and red volumes. The monk asked, "What is the Sangha? The Master said, [The text ends here].
The Master said, "Ask someone else. The monk asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]? The Master said, "Mount Mufu is high.
The monk asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "Tying up my skirt with a cloth belt."
Chan Master Shun of Mount Jun in Yuezhou asked: "I do not ask about the high mountains and deep waters; what is the realm of Mount Jun?
The Master said, "The mountains are high and the waters are deep. The monk asked, "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "An old fisherman beats his oars.
The monk asked, "As for the matter of the ancestral vehicle (zongcheng), how is it? The Master said, "Gazing at Lake Dongting from the Yueyang Tower."
Chan Master Qinshan Qianming Zhiyin of Lizhou asked: "What is the Way? The Master said: "Step by step, one treads upon it.
The monk asked: "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said: "Eye meeting eye. The monk asked:
"What is the house style of the Master? The Master said: "Brocade and embroidery; a silver incense pouch. The monk asked: "How do you receive guests? The Master said: [He remained silent].
Hard *hūbǐng* (stiff buns); soft *bòtuō* (noodles). A monk asked, "What is the matter of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Human sentiments are thick, while the sentiment for the Way is thin.
Chan Master Shoushun of Mount Shishuang in Tanzhou asked, "You do not speak of life, nor do you speak of death. Why [is this]?"
“Do you not say so? The Master said, “Once a word has been uttered. The monk asked, “What about when one goes from east to west?

The Master said, “It is as difficult to turn back as it is for four horses to overtake their tracks. The monk said, “I, your student, do not act in this way at all. The Master said, “It is easy to open a mouth that can speak from beginning to end.”
"It is difficult to guarantee one's heart remains steadfast through the long winter. The Master said: "The autumn wind whistles; the autumn rain falls in fine drizzle.

Withered leaves fly about; mountain clouds coil and swirl. If you can realize this, you will understand how Sudhana entered Maitreya’s pavilion, where the Indra-net is layered upon layer, all interpenetrating one another.
If you have not yet realized this, do not mistake your head for its reflection. Stay and dwell in the thatched hut. To discuss it in such a manner—"

This is intended for those at the beginning stage of practice. Let those with clear eyes and high standing examine and verify it together. Alas! What kind of talk is this? After a long silence, he said:
"The clouds atop the ridge have no leisure; the water flowing down the ravine is far too busy. *Chan*.

On the day of the opening of the hall by Chan Master Liaojue of Qianyuan Temple in Fuzhou, the successor of Chan Master Qing sui of Mount Tiantong in Mingzhou, the head monk finished striking the gavel. After a long silence, the Master said:
"Even if Aniruddha’s divine eye were employed, it would not yet be able to discern clearly; even if the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands were used, how could he [perceive it]?"
"Seize upon it! Is there anyone among the assembly who does not feel this bitterness? Come forth and overturn the meditation seat, bringing the great assembly to their knees!
Even so, this is not yet the work of a master; for now, let us vent our spirit as monks within the second gate. He asked:
For nine years at Shaolin, [Bodhidharma] offered but a single word; it has continued to deceive people until the present day. If you wish not to be deceived, I ask the Master to speak.

The Master said, "Oṃ. The monk said, "Mādriga. Mādrīci—what about that? The Master said: *Note: The term "賺舉" (zuàn jǔ) refers to misleading or deceiving someone by raising a point or posing a question.*
"I grant you thirty blows. The monk asked: "Venerable Sir, you have realized the fruit and transcended the stream of the sages; you do not need to undergo further cultivation.
Please, Master, speak quickly. The Master said: "Falling blossoms cluster beyond the eaves; green willow branches hang before the railing. The monk said:

"A single rain pervades the entire dharma-realm; the hearts of all beings are revived through the long night. The Master said: "Water does not wash water—how do you say this? The monk said: [silence].
"One should know that the character of the pine and cypress does not change its heart through the cold of winter. The Master said, "For now, believe only half of it.
A monk asked, "Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he had already descended into the royal palace. I wonder, who was this person? The Master said, "The ox-head emerges; the horse-head returns.
The monk said, "I wonder, was this the Dharmakāya or the Saṃbhogakāya? The Master said, "Plowing the furrows and pulling the plow. The Master looked around at the assembly and said:
Do you understand this thoroughly? If you do not, then today this mountain monk has pointed to a deer and called it a horse, sung nine and made it ten, and deceived all of you.
The true mandate of Mahādeva was impermeable as water; the authentic rule of Śrīparvata could not be penetrated by the wind.

When the sentiments of sage and ordinary are exhausted, the true permanence is revealed in its essence. Transcending all views and knowledge, its brilliance surges through past and present. This is truly because...
The mind remains fixed on the measure of the sages, perceiving and knowing according to whatever is encountered. Thus, hearing does not transcend sound, and seeing does not surpass form.

Even if one were to extinguish all seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, and inwardly maintain a state of profound stillness, it would still be a matter of conceptual shadows regarding the objects of the Dharma (*dharmaviṣaya*).

One continues to create various karmas, transmigrating through different realms, going forth without returning—how truly pitiable! If one can turn the light back to reflect upon itself, [one will realize the source].
What Buddha-way is there to be accomplished? What sentient beings are there to be saved?
Then one can hide one’s body within a mass of flames, emerge from the east and submerge in the west, gallop horses upon motes of dust, and share in both death and birth.
If you can see through this point and penetrate it thoroughly, take care not to mistake the bridge of a donkey’s saddle for your father’s chin.
Chan Master Yingcheng of Nanyue Shengtian Wanshou first visited Chan Master Suizhi of Jingci.
Suizhi asked, "Where have you come from, Venerable Sir? The Master replied, "From Pilu. Suizhi said, "I have heard that Pilu produces fine grasshopper-patterned fans;
have you brought any with you? The Master drew a perfect circle and said, "Great *Kalyāṇamitra*, you require this further."
"What is the point of blocking this? He then said, "It is precisely this; it is also required here. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Entering the hall, he said:
"The mountain flowers are in disarray, betraying Śāriputra; the mountain grasses are scattered, yet I pick up Śrī."
Startled, the deity of Mount Yue prostrated; the local guardian bowed in greeting. The iron ox of Shanfu has no place to go;
the stone statue of Jiazhou reveals its entire body. Such talk as this—many misunderstand it. I dare ask you all: how do you speak that single phrase which does not involve the conditions of spring?
After a long silence, he said: "Without the spring breeze, the flowers will not bloom; yet once the flowers have bloomed, they are again [snatched away] by—"
The wind blows it down.
*Du!* Chan Master Zhongli of Fuzhou asked: "Holding the dragon pearl in the palm of one's hand, one discerns the ten directions before one's eyes.
As this student approaches, I request the Master to discern me. The Master said: "The grass-robbers are utterly defeated. The monk said: "This student now..."
The monk lost the point. The Master said, "To know for oneself is already half the battle. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "Pretending to be so clever.
A monk asked, "I have traveled from afar to your chamber, looking up with admiration at your school’s tradition. Now that this student has come before you, I pray the Master will receive me.

The Master said, "Hang up your alms-bowl bag high. The monk said, "Is there no way to benefit others? The Master said, "Like a blind man feeling his way along the ground. The monk said, "Do not disdain me."
"Truly base. The Master said, "A short-lived woodcutter merely boasts of his books and sword. The monk asked, "When Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang rolled up his mat.
I do not know what the intent of these ancients was. The Master said, "Official horses trampling one another.

The monk said, "Today this student has gone out for a small matter and encountered something great. The Master said, "I have not even yet lifted my staff. Ascending the hall, he said: "The howl of the ape, the cawing of the crow..."

On the slopes of the mountain, the various beasts hide away; clouds arise from amidst the conch-islands, and the peaks lose their luster. The precious sword Ta’a blazes, vying with the sun for brilliance.
The wood-gatherer loads his firewood onto the boat, while the King of Physicians appraises its value. Yet, is there not one who disregards the distinction between host and guest?
"Come forward and speak. After a long silence, he said: "The waters are frozen, so the fish find it hard to leap; the sky is cold, so the grass sprouts late.
He struck the incense altar once with his staff and ascended the hall, saying: "The Dharma does not see the Dharma; the Dharma does not practice the Dharma; the Dharma does not know the Dharma."
"Great assembly, this is a censer. How is it that you do not see, do not act upon, and do not know?
Within ten billion worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, all Buddhas are emitting light from atop this censer, shaking the earth, preaching the Dharma, and saving sentient beings.
Do you all see them? Even if you were to see them, it would still involve hesitation. *Du!* (A shout). This was spoken by the Master in the third month of the first year of the Shaosheng era."
On the eleventh day, he gathered the assembly. Having bathed and purified his hair, he wrote a verse:
"The Qilin breaks the golden chains; The Jade Hare bursts through the white jade pass. How wonderful, after the cloudless midnight: A single bright moon shines upon Zhongshan."
The verse concluded. He sat in the full lotus posture and passed away. His body was cremated, and śarīra relics were obtained.
They were enshrined in a stupa at his home mountain.

Zen Master Ya of Shimen Luohan Chan Monastery in Hengshan County, Quzhou—successor to Zen Master Zanyuan Juehai of Jiangshan in Jinling—asked: "When the thunderous sound resounds once, the dragons..."
The elephants all arrived. A student came forward and requested the Master to raise his shout. The Master said: "When the lotus eyes blink, the thousand worlds fall silent;
where the golden countenance smiles, a single flower blooms anew. The monk said: "Humans and devas have all entered the realm of Luofeng;
today we have personally heard the definitive sound. The Master said: "Amidst the vast and boundless millions, none know it. [A monk] asked: "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?"
The Master said, "In the Jade Palace of the Eastern Court, no shadow remains. The monk asked, "What is it like after entering the world?

The Master said, "Rain flowers fall by the side of the Veḷuvana Garden. The monk said, "If so, then you have surpassed the city of Spring on the eighth night and dwelt upon the Snowy Peak for six years.
The Master said, "How was it before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvara? The monk said, "Wait until another time. The Master then—
[The Master] struck [the monk]. He asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The pagoda at Xiongsi opens to reveal a void so profound;
only a single shoe remains, braving the light dust. He asked, "What is the house style of the Master?

The Master said, "A single staff of *qióngzhú* bamboo; three garments of patchwork robe. The monk said, "When guests arrive, how will you receive them? The Master said, "Draw the spring water and prepare a strong infusion."
The Patriarch’s Tea. Entering the hall, he said: "The *ju-yu* is fresh and the chrysanthemums are fragrant; How thoroughly satisfied is the drunken gentleman of the Tao family!
Though we have no share in such wine-sipping, It does not hinder us from idly enjoying the scene by the eastern fence.

"Great assembly, 'idly enjoying' is indeed not lacking, but tell me, where are the eyes? Those who know it have their eyebrows arched above their eyes; those who do not yet understand... [The text trails off].
Wandering aimlessly within the yellow [silk]. A-he-he! Today it turns out to be the Double Ninth. *Du!* [He] descends from his seat.
Chan Master Ziju Ruyong of Guifeng in Xinzhou asked, "What is the realm of Boshan? The Master said, "The mountain stream flows with clear water;
the path leads out through the pine gate. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "His body is clad in red."

[The monk wore] a garment of fine silk. [His] belly was as black as lacquer. The monk asked, "As for the matter of the supreme vehicle above, what is it like? The Master said, "The top of the pagoda pole points to heaven.
The monk asked, "The spring has already passed; the summer scene is warm and flourishing. Regarding these seasonal conditions, I beg the Master to explain them for me.
The Master said, "The twenty-fifth of the twelfth month is not yet the time for New Year's greetings. The monk said, "I, your student, do not yet understand. I beg the Master [to explain further]."
[The Master] pointed again. The Master said, "A stone person’s body does not grow hair.
Chan Master Kezheng of Jiangshan in Jinling asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Night travel is not permitted.
The monk asked, "What is one who is on the Way? The Master said, "One must arrive by dawn. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]?"
The Master said: "One person’s spring is at the highest peak.
Chan Master Weibing of Chenghui in Luzhou, a successor of Chan Master Shouyi of Kaifu in Tanzhou, asked:
"Regarding the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage, I request the Master to proclaim it. The Master said: "There is."

A monk asked a question. The Master said, "It is just as when Śāriputra questioned in the past; it is exactly like when the Sugata answered at the beginning. The Master continued, "No question, no answer.
The monk said, "I have received the pointing of a single phrase from the Master; three prostrations to thank for the Master's kindness. The Master said, "Svāhā in a place of stillness.
A monk asked, "Treading upon and shattering the moon in the clear pool, piercing through and opening the sky of the azure void—disregarding danger and ruin, I beg [for instruction]."
The Master gave him instruction, saying, "The bell after the midday meal. The monk said, "The green mountains have no divergent paths; discernment lies with the person themselves.
The Master said, "You must be thorough about this. The monk responded with an affirmative grunt. The Master said, "Jump! Jump!"

Chan Master Qixiao of Shouning Monastery in Guizhou, a successor of Chan Master Wenyue of Yunfeng on Mount Nanyue, asked: "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; what matter should we discuss together? The Master said:
"A Persian enters a bustling marketplace. The monk said: "In that case, the grass bows and the wind blows. The Master said: "Ten thousand miles away, gazing toward the home pass."
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Dressing and eating. The monk said, "With hands folded at the chest, I step back three paces.
The Master said, "A lacquer cup after drinking too much wine. Ascending the hall, he said: "If you do not realize the Way upon seeing before your eyes, you are still somewhat ahead of the mark.
To move your feet while asking about the path is to err in the use of names and phrases. You worthy ones, today this mountain monk shall follow the error with the error. You..."
When people like these see that there are eyes, hear that there are ears, smell that there is a nose, and taste that there is a tongue, why is it that they still do not understand?
After a long silence, he said: "Emperor Wu sought immortals but did not obtain immortality; Wang Qiao sat upright and ascended to heaven. *Du!* (A sharp rebuke.)
Chan Master Chenghui Xianxu of Luzhou asked, "Deshan’s 'staff upon entering the gate' is a patriarchal style for all ages;
Linji’s 'shout upon entering the gate' is a model for all time. Setting these two paths aside, I ask the Master to provide a comment. The Master said, "I do not act in either of those ways.
The monk said, "If one utters a single word, that is a different kind of family style. The Master said, "Fortunately, I have this staff to rely on."

"It is not in the hand. [The Master] asked: "There is questioning and there is answering; you have skillfully distributed [the teachings]. As for the ultimate vehicle (*zongcheng*), I ask the Master to speak of it separately.
The Master said: "Your question, *ācārya*, is most intimate. The monk said: "I understand, Master. The Master said: "Understand what?"
The monk lifted up his sitting mat. The Master said, "In the end, what is it? The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "A true adept. The monk bowed. The Master then gave a shout.
The Master said, "How could the secret intent of the Tathāgata involve the sharpness of verbal sparring? The mind-seal of the Patriarchs is merely a laborious exercise in intellectual dissection.
If one were to utter a single word of the Dharma-treasury, the waters of the ocean would flow backward and Mount Sumeru would stand upside down. If one speaks of the Buddha..."
When the Patriarchs are spoken of, the three realms sink into stillness; what existence can there be for the four modes of birth?

If one deliberates by descending [into the mundane], withered trees will bloom and cold ashes will flare into flame. Even so, within the gate of the patch-robed monks, white clouds stretch for thousands of miles.
Now tell me, what excellence do these patch-robed monks possess? After a long silence, he said: "There is yet another aspect worthy of admiration: the continuous [seating]..."
Sleeping with a knife on the bed.
Zen Master Chongsheng Yiran of Huayao Mountain in Hengzhou, successor to Zen Master Baizong of Fuyan on Mount Nanyue, asked: "The lineage of Linji—please, Master, speak directly."
The Master said, "Raising eyebrows in the void; nodding the head in silence. A monk said, "Is it not just this?
The Master said, "It is indeed so. How do you understand it? The monk then nodded his head. The Master said, "This thief deserves a good beating!
The monk repeatedly cried out, "Thief! Thief! and returned to the assembly. The Master said, "Even thirty blows would not suffice. He then ascended the hall and said, "Mind..."
Mind and mind. The green mountains and deep waters are profound. If a person can recognize these mountains and waters, then all phenomena facing them will sink away into stillness.
You all have recognized this; why then do the seventy-two peaks remain as they were? Try to explain it for me.
If you cannot speak it, it is very much as if you have never traveled on pilgrimage. *Chan*.
Chan Master Zhishu of Chengtian on Mount Nanyue was asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Long hair; the monk's appearance is ugly. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "Palms joined behind the crown of the head. He was further asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The Shilin Peak is high. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Few travelers reach it."
A question was asked: "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Paper curtains in the Zen grove. The monk asked, "How do you receive guests?
The Master said, "Stone ears from the mountains. In the fourth month of the eighth year of the Yuanfeng era, the Master bathed and shaved his hair, sat in the lotus position, and passed away.
Upon cremation, his teeth, tongue, eyes, and pupils remained unburnt.
Chan Master Hui-xian Wenhui of Changqing Temple in Fuzhou, a successor in the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Jingzhao Daozhen of the Ten Directions Pure Cause Monastery in Tokyo, asked:

"Having departed from the precious land of the Higher Birth and ascended to the sacred site of Yansheng, what is the Venerable One of Immovability? The Master said: "A solitary boat carrying the bright moon. The monk said: "Suddenly—"
"If the oars and the rowing poles both stop, what then? The Master said, "The fisherman especially loves to stay among the reeds. Question:
"Regarding the long-term advancement on the Path, in the West they take the waxing of the person as proof. I wonder, what serves as proof here in this land? The Master said:
[The Master] held up an iron ball. The monk asked, "I do not yet understand the meaning of this; how should I regard it? The Master said, "The large is large; the small is small.
The monk asked, "I do not ask about Deshan or Linji; what is the matter regarding the transmission of the robe and the conferral of the Dharma?
The Master said, "Where have you seen Deshan or Linji? The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "Have you ever even dreamed of them? The monk clapped his hands.
He entered the assembly. The Master said, "Indeed. Indeed. The Master continued, "When one cuts off the vital ford, the vision is as black as lacquer;
when one opens a single thread of the path, Maitreya is seen everywhere. Now, I have opened it—let go! But tell me, where is Maitreya?
Is there anyone among you who can see him? If so, please come forth and speak before the assembly."
He looked for a long while and said, "Is there anyone? Is there anyone? Not knowing where Sudhana had gone, the gate of the multi-storied pavilion opened and he went off alone.
[The Master] shouted, "Each of you, please return to the hall."

Chan Master Jichao of Qisheng in Fuzhou ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he remained silent for a long while and said, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time are all leaping about right here.
Does the assembly understand? The Buddhas of the past have already spoken;
the Buddhas of the future have not yet spoken; the Buddhas of the present are speaking now. I dare ask you all: what is this matter that is being spoken?"
*Claps his desk once.* He says: "Suru, suru.
Chan Master Huizhao of Xiangyan Mountain in Dengzhou was originally from Dongfu in Fuzhou. Born into the Fan clan, he possessed a clear and sensitive temperament from childhood.
As he grew, he admired the school of emptiness (*śūnyatā*) and relied upon Great Master Yuanming of Jingde Temple in the Eastern Capital as his teacher.
The Master passed the scriptural examinations and received the tonsure. Subsequently, he traveled extensively to study at the monastic centers of Jianghuai.

Eventually, upon meeting Chan Master Jingzhao Zhen of Jingyin, he attained sudden enlightenment through a single word, as direct as the point of an arrow. Furthermore, his scholarly discourse on ancient and modern matters caused his reputation to resound throughout the capital.
Thereupon, he received an imperial decree to reside at Xiangyan in Dengzhou for nearly ten years. Later, he returned to his hometown and received [the invitation].

He invited [the abbots of] Guishan, Shoushan, and Shenguang; he served in three monasteries in total, all of which were among the premier sites in Min. Thereafter, his legacy would have been immeasurable.
On the day the Master first opened the hall for formal teaching, a monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed?"
The Master said: "The mud ox roars at the bottom of the sea; the wooden horse neighs in the clouds. The monk said: "I do not yet understand;

I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said: "Every single sound penetrates the Nine Heavens. [The monk] asked: "Now that the imperial decree has arrived this day, with what Dharma will the Master repay the Sovereign’s grace?
The Master said: "The August Heaven shows no partiality; it assists only those who possess virtue. The monk said: "If so..."
"What is virtue? The Master said, "One person sings of the Way; ten thousand people rejoice in its lack of partiality. Question:
"Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "The Phoenix Palace brushes the sky; the Bian River pours forth azure."

The Master further said: "In the West, during the four and seven [generations], the Way was cut off from words and speech; in the East, during the two and three [generations], the Dharma was devoid of written characters.
Only one seal was transmitted, directly pointing to the human mind. When the mind is realized, heaven and earth are fully encompassed; when the seal is fixed, not even a hair’s breadth is leaked.

In every particle there is no dependence, and in every dharma there is harmonious emptiness. Only then does one accord with the source of the sages, and only then can it be called entering the Buddha-knowledge."
Seeing it thus, one realizes it; falling away from two, falling away from three—how can a monk of true color speak of this? Can you say it?
How can the message within this be transmitted? The phoenix palace and dragon towers stand steeply leaning against the heavens.
If you wish to understand the matter at the eastern boundary of the city of awakening, it remains as it was, vast and silent, through the ages.
A monk asked, "Having recently taken leave of Master Xiangyan’s chamber and now arriving at this Guishan monastery, what is the Immovable Honored One?
The Master said, "The Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot lift him up. The monk asked, "What is the Moving Honored One? The Master said, "He has traveled through the Jade Palace;
he has repeatedly passed in and out of the Golden Gate. The monk asked, "What is the realm of Guishan? The Master said, "A thousand peaks come..."
“There is a road; it extends to the eight poles, pure and free of dust. A monk asked, “What is one who is within the realm?

The Master said, “Sometimes the eyes are open; sometimes they are closed. He asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, “The mountains are cold, and the bones are exposed.”
"When the water is shallow, the sand is seen.

The Master said: "To exhaustively study the sutras and treatises is just like entering the ocean to count its sands; to seek the Dharma and seek the mind is much like feeling the empty air in search of an echo.
Therefore, when our Buddha appeared in the world, it was for the sake of the one great matter; likewise, when the various patriarchs transmitted the robe, it was also for this very reason."

Chan Master Xinghua Shaoying of Tanzhou asked, "When one does not touch the waves, how should one proceed?
The Master said, "When the time is right, you must raise the oars; do not wait for the headwind. The monk said, "That is still the ripples on calm water.

Answer: To depart [from the question] would only increase redundant words; it would distance one from the Way even further. Once the Patriarch’s command has been issued, the critical ford is cut off.
The Buddhas of the ten directions crumble like tiles and melt like ice; the vehicles of the Tripiṭaka teachings are swept away until not a trace remains. Upon reaching this point—
Who would dare look upon him with a direct gaze? Therefore, although Śākyamuni possessed the pivotal mastery that exhausts the world, he still remained silent in the kingdom of Magadha;

When dragons and elephants trample, it is not something donkeys and mules can endure. [He] ascended the hall and said: "The Patriarch..."
To the Undersecretariat: The Buddha-dharma does not persist; before the Hall of Good Dharma, benevolence and righteousness are no longer spoken of. Although this is so, matters are never absolute.

I have humbly heard that one’s parents are mourned with deep sorrow, for their toil in giving birth to me was great. Desiring to repay this profound kindness, it is as vast as heaven and beyond measure.

"One does not dare to damage or injure one's hair, skin, body, or person; this was the filial piety of the late Zhongni (Confucius). Yet, while transmigrating through the three realms, one cannot escape the bonds of affection.
To cast aside such affection and enter into non-action (*wuwei*) is the true way to repay one's debt of gratitude.

Therefore, our Great Awakened World-Honored One practiced austerities on the Snowy Mountains, attained the Way in Magadha, and ascended to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to preach the Dharma for his mother—this is the Śākya [Buddha]."

This was the filial piety of Maudgalyāyana. Having attained great liberation and exercised great supernormal powers, he held a golden staff in his hand and cradled a dragon-bowl in his palm as he went to the gates of hell.
Standing there resolutely, he sought out and found his compassionate mother; he wept with immeasurable sorrow. This was the filial piety of Maudgalyāyana.
But what is the filial piety of Xinghua? After a long silence, he said: "Today, Xinghua does not ascend to heaven."
He did not enter hell. Instead, he ascended the royal throne within the Hall of Good Dharma and preached the Dharma for his mother to repay her labors.
Now tell me, where is my mother right now? He then said: "In her lifetime, my mother possessed abundant roots of goodness."

There is no need to trouble yourself by asking the Buddha whether one will certainly be reborn in heaven; among humans, a long life has been rare from ancient times to the present. Ninety years of spring and autumn—already diminished by one year.

The Master said, "When Hanshan meets Shide, they clap their hands and laugh heartily. The monk asked, "As for the matter of the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage, what is it like?

The Master said, "The waters of Caoxi are swift."

Huā later resided at Yanfú Monastery. His speech did not discuss the abstruse mysteries; his conduct was neither refined nor pure; his person did not conform to formal decorum, and the assembly took no pleasure in seeing him.

He spoke in verse, saying: "This mountain monk dwells at Ruijun; never have I manifested words or phrases. Seventy-three years have come, and seventy-three years have gone.
Having finished speaking, he sat cross-legged and passed away. Three days later, his hair and beard grew back again.

Subsequently, śarīra relics appeared frequently from his body. During the Yuanfeng era, the prefecture suffered a great drought.

The Governor, Lord Sun, who admired the Master’s virtue and wisdom, invited him to pray for rain. The following day, sweet moisture poured down in great abundance. Lord Sun held him in profound reverence and moved him to reside at Wen... [Monastery].

[The Master’s] reputation was extraordinary. During successive years of severe drought in the surrounding prefectures and counties, the Prefect Xu Gong, Censor Wang Gong, and Vice-Director Ye Gong repeatedly requested him to pray for rain, and his responses were effective.
When Censor Wang Gong moved to reside at Shengquan Monastery, the Master took up residence in three different monasteries, renovating each as they fell into decay.

Five or six [claps]. "Eh! [The Master] claps once and descends from the seat.

All should be wiped away. To be enlightened by the tip of the staff is not the mark of a true adept; to take up the shout is not yet extraordinary. The school of this wild monk is not like that:

This is the true wondrous secret: the majestic self is truly pitiable. To directly accept it is like the "second moon"; a great man must utterly sever it.
An established case already has many complications; do not act like a fool who allows himself to be stroked and rubbed. Alas for the Dharma of the Final Age!

cutting off heaven and earth, sun and moon are ever new. The Master said, "Golden-maned lion. [Another monk] asked, "In years past, Yuanzhao’s light illuminated the universe;
today, the Buddha-sun again sheds its brilliance. As a student who has come before you, I request the Master’s discerning gaze. The Master drew a circle. The monk said:
Ten-thousand-fathom white clouds cannot conceal it; a single orb of light shines through, illuminating all without partiality.

The Master said, "This too is entirely dependent on the lingering radiance beneath the gate of the sun. The monk asked, "If Māyā, the Buddha-mother, gave birth [to the Buddha] in Tuṣita, where is the Great Empress Dowager?
The Master said, "Flowers distinguish day and night; water encircles the beams and pillars. The monk said, "The Hall of the Ancient Buddhas..."
The former has already been realized; the Palace of Lapis Lazuli expounds the Ultimate Emptiness (*śūnyatā*). The Master said: "This is merely repeating a verse. Question:
"In the past, Empress Dowager Cisheng was like the moon that never leaves the heavens; Jingzhao personally received her imperial grace.
Today, for the late Empress Dowager Daxing, it is as water flowing back to its source in the sea. I wonder, what is the meaning of this? The Master said: "The vast expanse of the great ocean."
A solitary sail drifts far away; how much wind from the vast heavens can it withstand? The monk said, "Though there be a thousand ways of understanding, one ultimately cannot reach the goal;
in a single thought of no-mind, one is the same wherever one is. The Master said, "It is easy to distinguish dragons from snakes, but difficult to deceive a patch-robed monk.
The monk said, "If that is so, then we may cease the field-clearing of Xiyun and laugh at the alms-bowl carrying of Subhūti. The Master said, "Who says there is not even an inch of grass?"

[The Master said: "The mind receives the radiance of three springs as its retribution. The monk asked, "Tell me, when you perform this memorial service for the Empress Dowager today, in which realm of retribution does she ultimately dwell?
The Master replied: "Clouds gather and clouds disperse; the heavens are eternally pure. Bubbles vanish and bubbles arise; the water is fundamentally clear."
The monk said, “I have already received the good news of the True Man; there is no further doubt regarding the human realm or the heavens.

The Master said, “Not bad—how sharp you are! The monk asked, “I do not ask about the Buddhas handing down the transmission from hand to hand, but what is the matter of the succession from generation to generation?
The Master said, “A dragon begets a dragon-child; a dragon grows into a dragon-grandchild. The monk said, “If that is so, then the thousand sons will always surround the Golden Wheel.”
[The Master] pervades the great trichiliocosm. The Master said, "The fisherman dances for joy; the village elder sings his song. The monk said, "Auspicious clouds soar and harmonious qi flows;
magical mushrooms grow and fine grain flourishes. The Master said, "It is precisely right to offer praise."
The Master said: "The one who preached the Dharma at the beginning did not know the final phrase; the one who preached the Dharma at the end did not know the initial phrase.
Regarding these initial and final phrases, Master Huilin has already explained them for you all. But how were they explained?
If we rely on the three vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings—whether partial or complete, sudden or gradual, half or full—"

As for sound, one cannot avoid mistaking the pointing finger for the moon or counting grains of sand while entering the sea; it is merely like the reflection of the moon in a clear pool or the sound of a bell at night.
The sound issues forth according to the striking, and though it follows the waves, it does not disperse—yet this remains a matter belonging to the shore of birth and death.
Therefore, Bodhidharma observed that there were those with the capacity for the Mahāyāna in the Divine Land (China);

thus, he floated his cup across waves a thousand *qīng* wide and ascended peaks ten thousand mountains high. He first visited the Liang court, where the King of Liang questioned him regarding the dharmas of causality and conditioned phenomena.
Bodhidharma responded by revealing the supreme truth of the noble truths (*āryasatya*). As the King of Liang did not yet realize the meaning, he subsequently departed for Mount Song and Shaoshi.
For nine years he faced the wall, eschewing all reliance on written words. Transcending the three vehicles, he directly pointed to the human mind, so that by seeing one's nature one becomes a Buddha.

At that time, the Second Patriarch, Shen Guang, stood in the snow and severed his arm; thus he attained the marrow and clarified the mind. With "one flower and five petals," the fruit ripened naturally.
Through the transmission of the robe for six generations, later followers attained the Way. From this point onward, those in the Eastern Land finally believed that the True Dharma Eye existed.

The treasury of the wondrous mind of *nirvāṇa*—among those of middling and inferior capacities, delusion and awakening are equally divided. Thus, did not the Emperor Zhenzong of our Great Song dynasty state in his verse:
"The First Patriarch sat in meditation at Shaolin; he did not transmit the teachings, but transmitted only the mind"?
If those of later generations wish to awaken to the nature of True Suchness (*tathatā*), they must realize that the profound principle of the Secret Seal has been thus from the beginning.
How vast it is! The wondrous principle of True Suchness is most subtle and profound; none but those of great capacity and great vessels can comprehend it. Why is this?

To perceive, hear, sense, or know is itself a dharma, yet the Dharma is free from perceiving, hearing, sensing, and knowing. To do otherwise is to encounter a mass of fire at a fork in the road or to find an iron mountain blocking one's path. By oneself—
Yet, before the peak of Shaoshi, cliffs rise sheer for thousands of fathoms; along the path of Caoxi, not even a drop of water can pass.

Amidst this, the ancestral wind has not failed to decline, and the collapsing discipline is on the verge of falling to the ground. Nevertheless, though it be so, the Dharma has no fixed form, and the Way manifests according to the times.
To erect the great banner of the Dharma, to expound the great meaning of the Dharma, and to give rise to this great cause and condition—this is the work that must be done.
To bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings is not a matter of another time;

it is what is known as the "convergence" when a Great Sage appears in the world, causing [the Dharma] to spread extensively and pervade the entire realm of *sāhasra-lokadhātu*. Truly, this is an encounter once in a thousand years!
As for those such as Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang—who sat upright with robes trailing behind them, their transformation through non-action was such that nothing failed to reach them. If one were to...
He opens the gate of skillful means and reveals the mark of ultimate reality. A magnificent assembly from the ten directions gathers, with the fourfold congregation seated together on one mat.
He revives the ancestral style of the Buddhas of antiquity and awakens the fundamental source of all living beings. How could this be discussed as being the same as our present day? Why is this so?
Śakra-devānām-indra and Subhūti elucidated the Prajñāpāramitā, yet they stopped at mere emptiness; King Prasenajit offered his congratulations... [text continues]
Joy specifically refers to non-transmigration; it still exists within the conventional truth (*saṃvṛti-satya*).

This is precisely the separate transmission outside the teachings, the supreme point above [the ordinary], manifested for the present age—is this not a rare opportunity that accords with what is clearly manifest? Yet, while streams and mountains differ, clouds and moon are the same.
Like sounds responding to one another and vapors seeking out their kin, one then knows that this matter is neither of the past nor of the present.
Now, there is neither "that" nor "this. It is lofty yet without superior; vast and beyond limit. It is profound yet without inferior; deep and unfathomable.
A single hair swallows the great ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. When among the heavens, it is identical with the heavens; when among humans, it is identical with humanity.
Among the heavens, it becomes the sun and the moon, providing illumination and clarity. Among humans, it becomes the ruler and the minister, embodying loyalty and filial piety.

Inferring from this, the ten billion suns and moons, the ten trillion Mount Sumerus, and the ten billion great oceans—the fundamental bodies and the environmental world, the sentient and the insentient—all share a single ontological nature. It is not that the benevolent do not see them as benevolent, nor that the wise do not perceive them as wisdom;
yet the common people use them daily without realizing it. Only one who can integrate all phenomena as themselves is capable of such realization.
Is it not only the Sage? From this, lamp follows lamp as the flame continues, and leaf succeeds leaf in mutual succession.

For hundreds of thousands of generations, the moon has illuminated the true lamp, its light merging with the three realms; for hundreds of thousands of miles, the stars have aligned along the ancestral trunk, their cool shade sheltering the four modes of birth.
Thus we know that the Wheel of Dharma has turned once again in China, and the Sun of the Emperor radiates its long-lasting brilliance over Zhendan.
If this is so, then regardless of the magnitude of things or the distance of phenomena, all are enveloped by its light and all receive its bounty. This extends even to plants, trees, birds, and fish;
there is nothing far away that it does not reach. It is just as when the King of Śrāvastī wished to go to Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain to see the Buddha and issued an edict to all...

"Ministers, officials, mountains, rivers, the great earth, grasses, trees, and forests—all must go together to see the Buddha. If even a single blade of grass or a single tree does not go, I shall not be able to see the Buddha.
Great Assembly, right now, within the realm of heaven and earth and amidst the universe, the mountains, rivers, the great earth, grasses, trees, and forests neither go nor do they not go;
they neither come nor do they not come. They are profoundly still and without..."

I am majestic and immovable. Whether in civil or military arts, whether in Chan or Vinaya, we are all together in the ninth heaven before the Hall of Compassionate Virtue, seeing the Buddha at one and the same time.
Good sirs, it is not that you do not see him; but how do you see him? After a long silence, he said:
"His double pupils shine with the inexhaustible light of the sun and moon; his prominent nose is as magnificent as the beauty of the mountains and rivers."—The Monk Wei Yue.

I have humbly received the Imperial Decree. Today, as I ascend the seat to proclaim the Prajñāpāramitā, I do so on behalf of the Late Empress Dowager, whose karmic conditions in this world have reached their end and who has attained supreme retribution in another realm.
As the fifth seven-day period concludes, I offer this for her posthumous advancement to the Immortal Abode.
I reverently acknowledge that the Empress Dowager’s pure wisdom was innate and her supreme spirit moved with singular mastery; she manifested the traces of maternal virtue and her merit—
Praise to the Three Courts. Having departed to repay the causes within the Dharma-realm, may your fruition be perfected through the Ten Stages.

We humbly pray that you shall enjoy leisurely wandering alongside the Buddha-mother Māyā in the Tuṣita Heaven Palace, and together with the Naga-daughter Sāgaramati, attain Perfect Enlightenment in the Stainless World (Vimala-loka).
May your returning radiance and auspicious light cause the imperial house and the state to flourish and shine brightly. We humbly observe that when Śākyamuni Tathāgata approached his Parinirvāṇa...
Nirvana. Entrusting the Buddha-Dharma to the Sage Sovereign of Ten Thousand Chariots, may you illuminate it with the radiance of the sun and moon, providing eternal external protection;

may you encompass it as heaven and earth cover and sustain all, granting its long-term circulation. We, the śramaṇas, rejoice in having the fortune to draw near to the steps of the auspicious calendar.
The Prajñāpāramitā is proclaimed, adorning the national destiny. We respectfully venerate Your Majesty, the Current Emperor:

having inherited the ancestral throne from seven successive sagacious predecessors, the world rejoices as in the eras of Yao and Shun; manifesting the Way amidst the myriad affairs of state, your teachings spread abroad like those of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
This is surely because Your Majesty has long since embarked upon the divine vessel of Prajñā and is well-accustomed to its voyage.
Juehai now unveils the precious mirror of the Yellow Emperor and, within the assembly of Chan monks, gathers this vast merit to offer prayers for the long life—
ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years— of His Majesty the Present Emperor.

We humbly pray that his blessings may equal those of the Great Brahmā King, his longevity that of Śakra Devendra, and that he may govern the world of the three-thousandfold great thousand-fold universe with the Golden Wheel.
The Realm: The Jade Calendar records hundreds of billions of years of flourishing splendor. May the rains be timely and the winds harmonious; may the people be at peace and the state be prosperous.

We, the Imperial Grand Dowager, the Empress, and the Crown Prince, humbly pray that your ocean of merit and mountain of longevity increase for a thousand thousand years, and that the golden branches and jade leaves of your lineage flourish forever through ten million ten-thousand springs. May the royal princes and the imperial clan receive the favor of Heaven.

The palace ladies: may all virtues support you and a thousand auspicious signs gather upon you. We dare not trouble Your Majesty’s sacred hearing for long; we humbly pray that you will cherish yourself.
On the day of opening the hall, the Master ascends the seat and offers incense. Having finished the prayers for the Emperor’s longevity, he spreads his cushion. [He pays homage to] Zhihai Buddha.

After Master Yin struck the wooden mallet, the Master said: "Under the sky of Yao and the sun of Shun, within the Phoenix Pavilion and Dragon Tower, atop the solitary peak of Wondrous Height amidst the fragrant seas of floating banners—there is no duality and no division;
there is no distinction and no interruption. Lord and retinue appear simultaneously; one and many are without obstruction.
You monks with eyes of wisdom, come forth and behold! A question was asked: "For the sake of the nation, you have opened this hall; we pray that the Master will offer a blessing."

The Master said, "Clouds part to reveal the Tortoise Peak; the moon rises over the Whale Sea. The monk said, "The pivot of the celestial sphere turns upon its axis throughout the three thousand worlds;

may your sagely calculations extend the life of the great phoenix for a hundred thousand springs. The Master said, "You have spoken only half of it. The monk said, "To grind flour, one must use the wheat of that specific land;
to sing the song, one must be a person from the imperial capital. The Master said, "A golden-maned lion. [The monk] asked, "World-Honored One..."
[The Master] went out. [The monk asked: "For what great cause and condition have you come? What matter will the Preceptor attend to this morning? The Master said, "Auspicious snow fills Chang'an.
The monk said, "One person’s years of life increase; ten thousand miles of songs and chants resound. The Master said, "The wind blows and the grass bends."

The monk said, "To cut through nails and sever iron—this must still return to the essential tongs and hammer. The Master said, "That too is unnecessary. A monk asked, "How is it when the lotus has not yet emerged from the water?
The Master said, "In the clear waves, there is no path to penetrate. The monk said, "How is it after it has emerged from the water?
The Master said, "Before one's eyes, there is no different grass. The monk said, "If that is so, then its fragrance fills the Great Tang. The Master said, "..."
"This is not the realm of the public," the Master said.
"This Dharma-gate does not reside in the trap or the snare; how could it be concerned with questions and answers?
Even if all the lands of the ten directions were reduced to fine dust, and each grain of dust were a monk—each as learned as Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra or Śāriputra—to exhaustively [investigate it]..."
Tianxuan’s eloquence exhausted the pivotal mechanisms of the world. Yet, upon reaching this point, not even a single atom has any utility. Why is this?
Because birth and Buddhahood are perfectly interfused, and self and other are equal. Each person’s nostrils reach toward the heavens; each stands like a cliff rising ten thousand fathoms.

It is simply that they do not realize that reality follows the turning of delusion and phenomena shift with conditions; they obscure their own numinous light and perversely cast themselves into different realms of existence. Therefore, [this teaching] is used to shatter [their ignorance].
There was a Dharma King who, wielding unconditional compassion (*anālambana-maitrī*), steered the oars of the Three Vehicles to ferry across the waves of the five natures.

Yet he turned his affection toward the moon’s reflection in a clear pool and the sound of bells at night; thus, he allowed the ox of Huai Prefecture to eat the grain while the price of rice in Luling rose ever higher.

Furthermore, he could not avoid the labor of making the First Patriarch Bodhidharma visit China to find those of suitable capacity, and instead of polishing a mirror from a rhombus-shaped flower outside the teachings, he failed to polish the tile.
Within the robes, the black jaws [of the dragon] are not counted among other treasures; before the ancient sail is hoisted, one sees the established case.

From this, one awakens to the face that has no awakening, and becomes lost in the homeland that is never deluded. Impartial throughout the three periods of time, it flows forth equally throughout the ten directions.
In one's own fields, withered trees bloom with flowers; in the incense burner of the ancient temple, cold ashes flare up again.
There is not a single word or letter, nor any means of livelihood or industry, that does not accord with the true nature (*dharmatā*).
If this is so, then beneath the shadowless tree, the old fisherman dances upon his boat; within lies a kingdom of gold, where the rustic elder sings and rejoices together.

Rejoicing in peace and prosperity, may we all ascend together to the realm of longevity. Great assembly, may we all ascend together to the realm of longevity. From this day forth, may earth endure as long as heaven.
But tell me, how does one rejoice in shared peace and prosperity? After a long silence, he said: "Drums beat at Luofu, and the dance begins in Shaogzhou.
He stood for a long time. "Take care."
Chan Master Zhenji of Sizhou Puzhao Temple, whose name was Chuhui, was a native of Qingliu County in Chuzhou. His surname was Zhao.

He left the household life and received full ordination under Chan Master Yong of Baoning Temple in Jiangning Prefecture. In the fourth year of the Shaosheng era, by imperial decree, he was appointed as abbot.

On the day he ascended the Dharma hall, [the Emperor] asked: "When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, golden lotuses sprang up from the earth. When you, Master, appear in the world, what do you have?"
"What is an auspicious omen? The Master said, "Sweep away the snow before the gate.
Chan Master Yan of Puhui Temple on Mount Yinjing in Taiping Prefecture asked, "When Kāśyapa Mātanga entered the Han, the treasury of the teachings was made clear.
When Bodhidharma came from the West, what was his underlying intent? The Master said, "My Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive; dragons and devas all take refuge in it."

He asked the Master, “I do not yet know whether the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings are the same or different. The Master said, “Two colors, one prize. The monk said, “A single word returns to the Way;
the myriad phenomena are naturally mindless. The Master said, “There is still a slight gap. Another asked, “When a man of realization meets another, how do they communicate?
The Master said, “Rarely does one encounter a true adept. The monk said, “Were it not for a high official who understands this, [this truth would remain hidden].”
"How would the Master ever be willing to bring this forth? The Teacher said, "The golden hammer moves its shadow; the precious sword’s light is cold.

The Teacher said, "If not one dharma is penetrated, then ten thousand conditions will pass through. "If you can understand it here," he continued, "then your eyes have pierced through the Iron Ring Mountains, and you have swallowed the waters of the great ocean in a single gulp.
He then sang: "The waters of the great ocean have already been swallowed up; fish and dragons [turn toward]..."

Where shall one find a place to settle one’s body and establish one’s life? If there is among the assembly a monk who can give rise to compassion and exercise pity, let him come forth and save the Dragon King;
if he cannot, it will be enough to kill him with indignation. Nevertheless, though this is so, matters are never absolute.

This mountain monk cannot help but explain the principle for you all. Have you not seen what the former sages said? "Ultimate nirvana is the mark of eternal quiescence; it ultimately returns to emptiness.
When there is a single film over the eye, illusory flowers fill the entire world. If the film does not clear away, one knows the affairs of the world even without stepping out the door.
If the film is completely cleared away, only then does one know that the person within the hermitage does not see what lies outside the hermitage.
If you can act in this way, only then will you understand how to sit securely; throughout the twelve periods of the day, you may enjoy it as you please.
If you do not yet know this, I shall stand for a long while. Take care. He ascended the hall and said: "Spring clouds and spring rain cause all things to flourish; warm days and gentle breezes."

Rock flowers vie for beauty; green mountains layer upon layer; mountain stream waters are crystal clear. As for Bodhidharma’s lost path, one must by all means avoid revealing it. He spoke again, saying:
"If anyone can examine this thoroughly, I, this mountain monk, have today fallen into a verbal slip. With his staff, he struck the meditation seat.
He descended from his seat.
Chan Master Yuanyi of Dinghui Monastery in Suzhou, whose dharma name was Zunshe and whose secular surname was Gu, was a native of Gusu.

From his childhood, he was extraordinary compared to his peers; admiring the Way, he left the household life and received full ordination. Not long after, he first studied the *vinaya*, and subsequently practiced the Mahayana sutras, penetrating their depths.

He clarified what was profound and abstruse; his conditions for enlightenment accorded with perfect illumination. He transmitted the Way and sealed the mind; his practice and understanding were as clear as ice and frost.

He provided for both the religious and the secular, moving through three monastic seats. The fourfold assembly took refuge in him; he established rules as a teacher and model, never wearying in his instruction and study.

Duke Zhang Dunli, the Regional Commander, submitted a memorial to grant him a title of honor. A monk asked, "Regarding Nanquan’s killing of the cat—what was the underlying meaning? The Master struck him immediately. The monk said:
This was still a point of doubt for the student. The Master said, "One hundred and eight thousand.
The monk asked, "What if one suddenly encounters Zhaozhou? The Master said, "To sell gold, one must meet the buyer of gold. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Ten thousand rivers and ten thousand mountains. The monk asked, "What if one goes forth in this very manner? The Master said, "Ten thousand mountains and ten thousand waters."
The monk said, “I am doing this solely for the sake of its circulation. The Master said, “The mouths of those who travel between the north and south are like stone monuments.
The monk asked, “What is the eye of a patch-robed monk? The Master said, “A needle cannot pierce it. The monk asked, “Why is it so? The Master said, “I told you: it is the eye of a patch-robed monk.”
The Master said: "As for the fundamental principle (zongzhi), how could it reside in verbal expression? Furthermore, there are towering, lofty peaks and steep, precipitous cliffs;

the lake reflects the clear water, and the wind sweeps away the white clouds. The pines and bamboos rustle—yet this is not as good as the summit of Wuaofeng Peak, where mist and clouds are profound and vast, no different from the front of Kukkutapada Rock.
Upon reaching this point, each must reflect back upon their own light; there is no need for further pointing or instruction. Excessive words lead to ruin."

The Way has many paths, and one loses the sheep on them. If you are a person of this fundamental capacity, you will simply rest your shoulders and lean upon your staff, transcending sages and surpassing ordinary beings.
You will enter and exit birth and death, moving freely through sounds and forms. If you can truly act in this way, only then can you prolong the life of the Buddha and repay his profound kindness.
The inexhaustible Dharma-gate is to be encountered right before your eyes. Take care.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have a true mechanism that transcends even the finest hair or its tip. It is beyond light and darkness, above and below, north, south, east, and west.
It cannot be reached by words; it cannot be known through thought. Do you understand? East is Pūrvavideha; West is Aparagoyānī."
Ascending the hall, he said: "At the first month, the moon is full; the reflections of the hundred rivers subside. A single lamp emits its brilliance; ten thousand wicks flow with radiance.
The moon has no intention to retain its reflections; the lamp has no thought to transmit its light.

If you can attain such a state, you may dwell amidst clamor and enter into the secular world, wielding the light of great compassion throughout the lands of the sands, and opening the eye of the Universal Gate for all living beings. How could this not be so?"
Only the Great Being Avalokiteśvara possesses thirty-two kinds of wondrous and unimpeded responses;

he is able to open the eye of the True Dharma for every single ordinary person bound by all fetters. Nevertheless, even so, one must be a man who can "sever the nails and cut through the iron" before this is possible.
Otherwise, *svāhā* in a quiet place!
Ascending the hall, he said: "The green mountains are lush and the waters flow on; ten thousand waves and a thousand ripples join the ocean tide.

Grasping the fishing line, one rows out upon the boat; at the tip of the hook, one must catch the whale and the tortoise. He took up his staff and said: "Those who can bear their lives, come to the hook! "Examine! (Chán).
Ascending the hall, he said: "When sleepy, I close my eyes; when food comes, I eat. Let the Buddhas and Patriarchs say it is easy or difficult as they please.
If you ask what dharma there is for settling the mind, Lake Tai constantly submerges Mount Dongting.

Every monk says, "I am all-pervasive in the eight directions and four quarters, moving freely without obstruction. Why, then, did Longji say: "Rolling up the curtain removes the barrier; closing the door..."
"Birth-attainment is obstructive. If a person can discern this, I grant you a place to sit securely beneath your robes and bowl.
Entering the hall, he said: "How high is heaven! How thick is earth! The sound of the ocean tide; the roar of the lion.
Looking up, one cannot see its front; meeting it, one cannot glimpse its head. Do you understand? Seven times seven is forty-nine."
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have a single phrase; I bestow it upon you right now. The jade-axled scrolls and lapis lazuli cases are all fully present at once.
There is no need for deliberation; it is revealed layer upon layer. The udumbara flower blooms and awakens within the fire. Examine!"
Chan Master Puchong of Shouzhou Toudi Mountain Shengyin Chan Monastery ascended the hall and said: "Atop the Peak of Abiding in Stillness, leaves fall and return to their root;
before the Hall of the Bright Moon, there is the golden wind and jade dew. Tell me, what is the single phrase for this deep autumn?
After a long silence, he said: 'In antiquity, we know not where they went; tonight, as before, the moon shines through the window.'"
Chan Master Fazhen of Benjue in Xiuzhou was named Shouyi. His surname was Shen, and he was a native of Jiangyin.

From birth, he displayed auspicious and extraordinary signs; he was naturally quick-witted and possessed outstanding talent. Before reaching the age of twenty, he suddenly developed a deep aspiration for the monastic community. He took leave of his family to join Rui Guang Temple and entered the service of Master Yuanzhao.

Attending upon him and inquiring after the Way, he never traveled elsewhere. The assembly recognized his profound realization as he propagated the Path in Xiecheng. [The text here records] a question by Xuan...
The Buddha selected officials; they ought to have been me. As for the matter of ascending the imperial examination hall in the ancestral seat—what was it like?

The Master said: "The great phoenix spreads its wings as the celestial path is vast; the giant turtle turns its body as the seawater is narrow. The monk said: "The Master’s family reputation preserves the ancient legacy;
the Dharma King’s foundation finds its restoration. The Master said: "Look after five days. The monk said: "Tell me, then, what is the difference between 'yesterday' and 'now'?"
"Same yet different. The Master said, "Once a word has been uttered. A question was asked: "The spring air has already dispersed with the red rain;

the fragrant breeze first passes through the cool green shade. I, a student, ask about the meaning of the Westward Journey; I beg the Master to employ skillful means to expound it for me. The Master said:
[The Master] clearly brought this up for the assembly. A monk said, "It can truly be called 'one phrase cutting off the stream, ten thousand functions suddenly eliminated.
The Master said, "When you strike it and bump into it, how will you speak? The monk said, "The grand and pure regulations are the same from ancient times to the present;

when we meet, there will surely be those who can express them. The Master said, "Not unsharp-witted indeed. A monk asked, "A lion that has left the herd crouches on the ground with full majesty. Not..."
"Baring your claws and fangs; I wish to hear your roar. The Master said, "Everyone, exert your strength! The monk said, "In years past, Old Lu was already loquacious;
today I have personally heard the primary pivot. The Master said, "What about the matter beneath your heels? The monk said, [silence].
With the precious staff, he parts the eyes of a thousand sages; on the spot, he discerns the lotus within the fire. The Master said, "Truly a master.
The Master said, "This Dharma-seal is not something transmitted. Worn for kalpas, it is not obtained from others.
It encompasses the six voids without exterior and blends the ten ages into a single moment. When fully raised, the traces of Buddhas and Patriarchs sink away; when let go..."
The distinction between the sage and the ordinary arises from words; yet it is vividly manifest in daily life. The myriad phenomena suddenly appear within the numinous light;

vast and open before one’s eyes, self and other are undivided within the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). Though all traces are obliterated in this expansive clarity, the infinite gates of meaning flow forth.

In its silent state of non-reliance, it transcends far beyond the stage of all-knowledge. It is not a mark of written characters and is free from the conditions of seeing and hearing. All vehicles arise from...

But tell me, what is it that you shoot? After a long silence, he said: "I let this one point pass."
