“If it is so, then the pure sound is forever inexhaustible; it washes away the dust from the eyes. The Master said, “It is only after frost and snow that one first beholds the form of enduring winter.
The monk said, “The sacred sprout has its place, yet all people neglect it; the iron eye is impartial—do not point to the mysterious.
The Master said, “You must know the path above; it does not permit those who travel at night. The monk said, “If one suddenly encounters a torrential flood that overturns the mountain...”
"How about at the bottom of the mountain? The Master said, "An iron net that covers the sky—who dares to show its head?
A monk asked, "The bottomless bowl transmitted by the thousand sages—on the road to Caoxi, who is permitted to share in it?

What is this bottomless bowl? The Master said, "A thousand men cannot leap out of it. The monk said, "Traveling ten thousand miles across the blue sea, I joyfully encounter waves that overturn the mountains. The Master said, "Not so."
The Tidal Manipulator. A monk asked, "Regarding the Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs, which is like the mechanism of an iron ox—precisely at such a time, is it the seal?
Or is it not the seal? The Master said, "Look at the iron ball in the furnace. The monk said, "If it suddenly breaks, then what?
The Master said, "You must know pain and itch. The monk said, "Today I have met the Master. The Master [nodded].
He said: "The thread of the discourse has shifted.
He ascended the hall and said: "If one's initial practice does not reach the goal, it is like trying to cross a vast river by following the current.

If one's final effort is excessive, it is like a fierce warrior loosing a wild arrow. Sometimes high, sometimes low, there is no fixed standard; thus, what was right becomes wrong, and one is caught being pointed out by others."
Examine this. Tell me, how can one attain accord? After a long silence, he said: "In the midst of the flames of a red furnace, more fire is added;
the blazing, adamantine eye opens of itself. *Du!* (A shout).
Ascending the hall, he said: "The sunbird cries out in spring; the gate of Avalokiteśvara opens. The clear fountain reflects the moon;

the realm of Vairocana is manifest. The crane calls atop the peak—sound after sound is no different. On the pavilion of scattered pearls, every bead is perfectly formed. Now hidden, now revealed; it turns of itself without being pushed.
Is there anyone who can gather it up? Try presenting it to me and see. After a long silence, he said: "How laughable, this monkey!"
Probing for the moon in the water, one does not know whether a real toad truly exists.

"How fierce are those claws that grow? Try letting out a single roar and see! After a long silence, he said:

The Zen Master Fohai of Tōkyū Hōshin Shōtoku Zen-in was named Yūzui. His secular surname was Chen, and he was a native of Xianyou County in Xinghua Commandery.

From his youth, he was extraordinary compared to those of the mundane world; he would sit in silence all day long. His parents marveled at this and immediately granted him permission to leave the household life.
He took the venerable Chongquan of Tōkyū Jingde Temple as his teacher. Having completed the formal ordination through the ritual of comparison, he first visited...

The Master said, "Even the Master must not disturb people. Nan immediately recognized his potential. Later, the Master relied upon Lestan Mountain.
Master Zong had a profound realization of the profound mysteries. After serving him as an attendant for a long time, the assembly recommended him as their leader.

The Great King of the country had not yet entered the Chan school, but having heard of the Master’s reputation for the Way, he dispatched a messenger one day to summon the Master to the palace for a small assembly (*xiao can*).
Addressing the multitude, the Master said: "The true nature of Vairocana is no different from the fundamental nature of you all.
Since beginningless kalpas, you have transmigrated throughout the Dharma-realm; within this process of rebirth, there is neither beginning nor end, neither going nor coming."
The nature is without marks; it is neither ancient nor modern. Not even a speck of dust can be established, and not even a hair’s breadth can remain.

There is no true dharma that can be divided; how could there be an interval between the semblance and the end? Therefore, know that within the dharma-realm, sentient beings neither arise nor perish; the equal source of this nature is the Buddha.
Nevertheless, although it is thus, if one relies on the gate of the patch-robed monks (samneng), heaven and earth are vastly different. Why is this? Since—

There is birth and there is extinction; again, there is going and there is coming. Since there is no distinction between the True Dharma, Semblance Dharma, and Final Dharma ages, nature and form are clearly visible and can be perceived.
Within this interval, there is neither one who attains Buddhahood nor one who does not attain Buddhahood.
Within the treasury of Prajñā, there is nothing whatsoever that can obstruct it—not even the Buddhas of the three periods, the six patriarchs, or the elder monks throughout the world.

today you finally let forth the cry of emerging from the valley. The Master said, "Why trouble yourself to do so specifically? He then said, "If the wise do not know, how can wisdom reach it?"
This abiding place is known only to oneself. When causes and conditions harmonize, it is shared with others. Therefore, when held fast, the trace is cut off at the very moment of engagement;
even the thousand sages find it difficult to peer into. When let go, it manifests its form in response to things; the four modes of birth can then be distinguished. Now tell me:
at this very moment, is it better to hold fast or to let go? After a long silence, he said: "If you wish to know that the ten thousand streams flow without end, it all depends on..."
The lineage of the Holy Source is profound.
Chan Master Zhiming of Yanxi Chan Monastery in Huanglong, Ezhou, was a native of Raoyang. He abandoned Confucianism to follow the Buddhist path.

Having studied the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* through formal examination, he donned the saffron robes and received full ordination. He then traveled to study under Master Daoxin’s quarters, where the incense smoke [wafted].
At the place of his awakening, he attained sudden and profound enlightenment. He refined and clarified the teachings of past and present, penetrating the most secret and profound depths.

Lord Hu Shiwen, the Commissioner for Judicial Review, became his friend outside the monastic circle. Lord Zhang Shangying, the Hanlin Academician, requested that the Master emerge from seclusion to lead a monastery.

Lord Feng Ji, the Minister of Revenue, wrote the preface to his *Yulu* (Recorded Sayings). At the three monasteries of Guankui, Jizhao, and Huanglong, he proclaimed the ancestral wind, becoming renowned throughout the world.
Yang asked, "When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, the realm of Māra was overturned and destroyed. When the Master opens the hall, what auspicious signs are there?
The Master said, "A night of falling flower rain; the city is filled with the fragrance of flowing water. Yang asked, "Why could it not be lifted at the head of Dayu Ridge?
The Master said, "Looking down the cliff with the eyes of a tiger; it causes a sudden outburst of sorrow. The monk said, "If that is so, then I regret not..."

"Be careful at the very beginning. The Master said, "What is this face? When Layman Hu of Huguang was on his circuit inspection tour through Gong'an in Jingnan, he asked a monk from Ersheng Temple, "When Emperor Wu of Liang asked Bodhidharma, 'What is the primary meaning of the holy truth?
Dharma replied, 'Vastly empty, there is no sage. Why is it that today in Gong'an there are, instead, two sages? The monk [remained silent].

[He] had no opponent. Later, he presented this to his teacher. The teacher said, "A single drop of black water forms two dragons. He then ascended the hall and said, "The one path that points upward—monks have no way to grasp it.
To seek the subtle or the profound is like learning to walk from Handan. As the assembly first gathered for the next lecture, the teacher ascended the hall.
The Master said, "One must not continue to open one's eyes and speak of dreams. He then descended from his seat. Entering the hall, he said:
"A single parting word from the South Mountain cuts through nails and severs iron. One must strictly avoid deliberation, lest it turn into a mere track left behind."

Compiled by [Song Ba] Weibai, Dharma-Transmitting Chan Master Foguo, Abbot of Fayun Chan Temple in Dongjing.
The Section on Responding to Capacities:
Chan Master Huairang of Nanyue, the Fourteenth Generation;
Chan Master Yuanyou of Yunju Mountain, the Dharma Heir [of Dongshan Liangjie].
The Zen Master Fuyin of Chikai Zen-in at Daixiangguosi in Tokyo was named Zhiqing. His secular surname was Ye, and he was a native of Tong’an in Quanzhou.

By nature he was intelligent and quick-witted; he was erudite and possessed refined elegance. Before reaching the age of twenty, he followed the Venerable Huiru of Luyuan Temple to leave the household life.
He attended to his master’s needs for five years until his full ordination. At a young age, his innate spiritual capacity was awakened.

He traveled extensively to consult various masters of the Way. Upon first meeting him, Master Yu deeply approved of him. He initially resided at Wuzu, where his fame spread throughout the four quarters and was revered by both the imperial court and the common people.
By imperial decree, he was appointed as abbot. During the hundred-day mourning period for Emperor Zhezong, he was specially granted the Chan title "Foyin.
On the seventeenth day of the second month in the first year of the Jianzhong Jinggu era, the Master passed away.
On the fifty-seventh day of the Empress Dowager’s mourning period, by Imperial Decree, she ascended the throne in the Cide Hall. The Master held up the incense and said:
"This single offering of incense is offered on behalf of the late Empress Dowager; it is burned toward this golden burner to perform great Buddhist rites."
I humbly pray that fragrant clouds, rich and pervasive, shall lead the retinue from Mount Tushita to enter this Dharma hall.
May the refreshing rain of the Dharma moisten the heart of Queen Wenmu, enabling her to ascend instantly to the stage of Buddhahood. Then, adjusting his robes, he ascends the seat and says:

"Before the Hall of the Ancient Buddhas, arrangements are made according to the occasion; atop the Hall of Compassionate Virtue, today we raise it up for proclamation. Tell me, everyone: are these one and the same?"
"This is a distinction. Is there anyone who can express it? Come forward and try to say it. A monk asked, "Myriad streams follow different paths, yet all return to the great ocean;
boundless wondrous virtues all emerge from this school. I wonder, what is this school? The Master said, "The Buddhas of the past have transmitted the Great Canon;
those who awaken realize that mind penetrates the vast void. The monk said, "I rely on the Master’s single flavor of purity..."

"Cool rain. The four seas receive the drenching rain as a repayment for the Emperor’s grace. The Master said, "A single drop of Caoxi water is sufficient to wash away the myriad ages of dust for all living beings.
The monk said, "Under the winds of Yao and the sun of Shun, auspicious omens increase; the woodsmen's songs and fishermen's chants celebrate the Great Peace.
The Master said, "A single word encompasses ultimate transformation; the thousand sages naturally return to the same source. The monk said, "If one does not ascend the tower, how can one..."
"Knowing the sea is vast," he said, and then bowed. The Master said, "You must advance further. A monk asked, "In the Great Ocean of Wisdom, there must surely be a pearl that tames the sea.
Today, on this very stage, I request the Master to bring it forth. The Master extended both hands and said, "Look! Look!
The monk said, "Yangshan of the past, the Master of today. The Master said, "When the *wangxiang* reaches it, its light shines brilliantly."
Where Li Lou walks, the waves surge to the heavens. The monk said, "In that case, atop the head of Śākyamuni there is something naturally distinct;
what the dragon girl brought forth is no different. The Master said, "Perfectly round and penetrating the three thousand worlds; brilliantly clear and containing all phenomena."
The monk said: "The Empress Dowager has received imperial grace and ascended to the Pure Land; may our Emperor’s sacred life endure for ten thousand years of spring.
The Master said: "Only this is most clear; it has never moved. The monk asked: "In the Buddha-land, there are three thousand golden worlds;
in the realm of the immortals, there are twelve jade towers. I wonder, where is Lady Māyā now? The Master said: "Wondrous."
The essence has originally no location; throughout the entire body, how could there be any further traces?
The monk said, "If so, then the purple-gold lotus supports the feet with their thousand wheels, and the white jade hair-tufts welcome the body of ten-thousand virtues.

The Master said, "You must know that the three thousandfold world-system of the Buddha-land exists solely within the single transformation of our Emperor. The monk said, "As for that which is within the Emperor’s transformation, does it still permit..."
The student asked, "Does the practitioner have any news to reveal? The Master said, "The August Heaven does not obstruct the drifting clouds;
how can the bright sun be hindered by the light of a torch? The monk said, "Amidst the smoke of a million people in the nine thoroughfares, one sees only incense being burned to celebrate peace."
The Master said: "The One Qi is impartial; all living beings rely upon it. Question: "The Dharma is inherent within the body; wherever one encounters the occasion, there is Buddhist practice.
Without performing the three prostrations and without uttering a single greeting, can one still pose a question? The Master said: "Rituals may be promoted, but they must not be abolished."
The monk said, “All phenomena are of the nature of quiescent extinction; they cannot be proclaimed through words. Now that the Field for Selecting Buddhas has opened, how do you express this?
The Master said, “Where the flowers of awakening bloom, the thousand forests are exquisite; when the sun of the Buddha is full, the myriad forms merge.
The monk said, “The golden rooster crows at the dead of night; the straw dog barks as day breaks. The Master said, “Whom do you say knows this? The monk joined his palms.
The monk looked at him. The Master said, "It does not hinder one's alertness. The monk said, "With all my strength I support the holy successor to transmit the great enterprise;

I originally hoped for a thousand autumns of peaceful prosperity. Now that the limit has been reached and it is difficult to remain—today being the fifth or seventh day—I beg the Master to preach the Dharma to mourn the immortal spirit.
The Master said, "At first you followed the light of the jade hare; now you follow the shadow of the golden crow. The monk said, "The ultimate principle is one..."
Zi Su-shi asked, "I do not yet know where the chariot of the Immortal is. The Master said, "In the city of Rājagṛha, at the time of the assembly in Jetavana.
The monk said, "The flowing water originally resides in the sea; the setting moon does not depart from the sky. The Master said, "That is already the second moon.
He asked, "The *Avataṃsaka* teaching says that Bodhisattvas manifest themselves as kings within the ranks of worldly positions."
"Most peerless; his merit and majestic radiance surpass all. He universally brings benefit to all sentient beings.

Now tell me, what kind of bodhisattva is the present Emperor? The Master said, "Vast and boundless, beyond naming. The monk said, "With the power of great compassionate vows, he serves as the sovereign.
Daily employing the Buddha-mind, he governs the myriad people. The Master said, "Only by knowing this grace does one understand."
[The Master] spoke of repaying kindness. A monk asked, "I do not ask about the Three Vehicles or the twelve divisions of the teachings;
what is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths? The Master said, "When the clouds have cleared, the sun and moon shine bright; when the wind is gentle, heaven and earth are in spring.

The monk said, "In that case, its merit flows through ten thousand generations and endures forever; the Way penetrates a hundred kalpas and remains ever firm. The Master said, "It encompasses both the vast and the minute; the sky of Yao is wide."
“Illuminating both the high and the low, the sun of Shun shines ever long. The monk said, “If that is so, then all is vast and non-action; the primordial source transforms itself naturally.
The Master said, “His majestic light shakes the great chiliocosm; he is the towering Lord of Lords. The monk said, “This may truly be called the single assembly at the Brahma Heaven.”
Today [the case] is reviewed anew. The Master said, "In the palace of the mani jewel, there is impartial illumination for a thousand ages. The monk said, "A once-in-a-thousand-year moment;
I thank the Master for his reply. The Master said, "I thank you for your question."
The Master said: "Just now, Zen Master Jingyin said: 'He who preaches the Dharma at the beginning does not know the final word;

he who preaches the Dharma at the end does not know the initial word. I, this humble monk, shall now preach the Dharma at the end, yet for the sake of the Great Empress Dowager Xing, I shall expound the initial word.
Do you understand? The spiritual source is profoundly still; things and self are both suchness."
The Buddha-nature is pure and true; it is the same essence for both the holy and the ordinary. Its brilliance and subtlety pervade all things, remaining perfectly clear and limpid through the ages.
It encompasses the ten voids of space, fundamentally transcending coming and going, and has never known birth or extinction.

It is only because those who are deluded regarding it harbor emotions and cling to intellectual understanding, perceiving the existence of self and others, taking the ten realms as their homeland, and grasping at this single body as their own self, that they falsely give rise to hatred and attachment, and forcibly...
Giving rise to greed and anger, they indulge their karmic consciousness to create the causes of suffering; pursuing the conditions of retribution, they rely upon the cycle of transmigration.

Thus entangled from this point forward through accumulated kalpas, they do not know how to contemplate the method for returning to the source. Immersed in various currents, they have not yet awakened to the thought of returning to the origin.

Having already turned their backs on the true limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), they shall surely falter and collapse upon the dark path. Even if they should remember the Radiance, they will be unable to abandon [the world] and depart. All...
O Benevolent One, who could feel such pity for these lost youths? Do you know? It was solely for this cause that our Buddha, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, appeared in the world.
Therefore, he remained for forty-nine years, delivering all sentient beings and turning the fundamental Wheel of Dharma.
At his final resting place beneath the twin śāla trees, he entrusted the secret seal of Vairocana to his foremost disciples. By virtue of this—
This has been transmitted from Buddha to Buddha and from Patriarch to Patriarch, handed down through the ages.

Although various skillful means and gates of transformation have been extensively established, they point only to this single mind, the wondrous Dharma. How great it is! This wondrous Dharma cannot be deliberated upon by wisdom or eloquence;
it cannot be achieved through supernatural powers or meditative realization; it cannot be known by a mind with intent, nor can it be known by a mind without intent.
It can be attained. To awaken to it requires nothing more than a single word to penetrate through to realization; at that very moment, one is liberated from birth and death.

Should one remain deluded, even if you progress through the various stages of cultivation, in the end you will not escape the realm of the false and illusory. Just as on this day, when the human and celestial realms intersect and the visible and invisible worlds are universally present:
the imperial breeze blows gently in harmony with spring, and the sovereign sun lingers long to nourish all things. The Ten-Thousand Chariots [the Emperor] is...
Ascending to the Hall of Shun, the Six Dhyānas look up in unison toward the Heaven of Yao. For the sake of the late Empress Dowager, this Dharma assembly is established;
it must clearly point to the wondrous mind of the ancient Buddhas so that awakening may be attained. Then, lifting the corner of his *kāṣāya*, he said:
Do you see? Here, the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time sit upon jeweled lotus thrones, emitting light and manifesting auspicious omens.
All the great patriarchs are likewise here, occupying the lion throne, entering meditative absorption and practicing tranquil dhyāna.

If Empress Daxing can perceive this, then without leaving her current place, she will suddenly awaken to her own original mind; without moving from the site of enlightenment, she shall sit [in realization].
Ascending to the stage of Buddhahood for oneself, one sees those who arise and those who perish; yet there has never been any perishing or arising.
This very principle applies to the speaker and the listener; there has never been any listening or speaking. Therefore, coming and going are, in their very essence, the complete Reality.
Whether in the past or in the present, there is no separate substance. Even within vermilion towers and jade palaces, the pure Dharma-body manifests in layer upon layer.

In the Golden Gate and the Jasper Pond, the original face is revealed everywhere. Even if one possesses the supernatural powers and samādhis of all dust-motes and lands, they are spontaneously accomplished without effort;
even the subtle and wondrous Dharma-gates as numerous as the sands of the Ganges reach one spontaneously without practice.
If Empress Dowager Daxing can thus attain such thorough realization, she will finally laugh at the daughter of the Dragon King Sāgara, who must wait until she goes to the South to achieve it.
The Buddha has not yet become a master. Lady Vaidehī’s wish to be reborn in the Western Land is merely a vain delusion.
Everyone, tell me: how was it that Empress Daxing attained such fierce and sharp realization?
Do you understand? Only Buddhas and Buddhas realize and know this together; it cannot be fathomed by ordinary sentiments.

I, the monk Zhìqīng, have hereby extolled the merit of Prajñā and its boundless, wondrous benefits, respectfully offering this adornment solely to provide spiritual sustenance for the celestial journey of the Great Empress Dowager.
I reverently contemplate that the Empress Dowager’s internal governance was as harmonious as...
The family’s profound virtue supported all things; their diligence and frugality were renowned both at home and abroad; their wisdom and sagacity surpassed those of past and present.

Now that the sacred governance has been renewed, it was indeed upon the model of the Mother that this rested. Alas, her retribution in Jambudvīpa has ended, and she has perfected the fruit of rebirth in Sukhāvatī.
Having cast off the ancestral palace of compassionate virtue, you have journeyed to the pure land of radiant majesty.

Alas, the two wheels [of life and death] move with such speed that the fiftieth-seventh year has now arrived. Your sacred heart exhausts itself in filial sincerity; for long days you reverently performed Buddhist rites.

You commanded the various Chan masters to ascend the seat and extensively expound the principles of our school, hoping to rely upon the extraordinary merit of the Buddha-dharma to offer supreme dedication.

This is the transformative path of the divine immortals. I humbly pray that Your Majesty, the Great Empress Dowager, will attentively hear the Prajñāpāramitā, thereby liberating yourself from worldly attachments and deeply awakening to your original mind, entering into the Buddha’s wisdom and vision.
Furthermore, I hope that you will bestow upon us these blessings, so as to protect the imperial ancestral altars for all eternity and lead our nation’s people to benevolence and longevity.
As for this servant, Daoxing, I am without merit; both my reputation and my reality are entirely hollow.

On this day, I have encountered the Sage’s grace, being granted this opportunity to propagate the ancestral injunctions. Reflecting upon my own meager and shallow learning, I am filled with even greater trepidation.
This is surely because Your Majesty, the Present Emperor, possesses profound and deep spiritual wisdom and vast, universal compassion.

The successor ascended the precious throne; the harmony of the seasons remained unaltered. He secretly penetrated the wondrous mind of the Triple Gem and subtly exercised the divine administration of myriad affairs.
All insects and plants alike were bathed in the waves of his grace, and even the barbarians of the Man, Mai, Rong, and Yi tribes all returned to his virtuous transformation.
This is truly a flourishing destiny for a thousand years, a singular encounter with a sagely age. I, your servant, from beyond these worldly bounds, bow my head in devotion.

With utmost sincerity, I emulate the benediction of that border-guard: I respectfully pray that Your Majesty, the Emperor, may have a longevity equal to Mount Nanshan, increasing your sacred life without limit;

and may your years be as vast as the Northern Sea, providing for a future more distant than any divination could foretell. May the golden branches flourish and the jade leaves spread their fragrance even further.
May you protect and nourish all living beings and cause the True Dharma to prosper. [This applies to] the Empress Dowager and the Empress.
To the Crown Prince: I humbly pray that your virtue may harmonize with Heaven and Earth, supporting the sagacity of Your Majesty and your father above;

and that your longevity may equal the mountains and rivers, bringing comfort to the hopes of the common people below. I, your servant, reflect that I am originally but a withered tree from the mountain forests, a minor monk of the crags and valleys.

It is an honor for me to lead the assembly of Chan practitioners at Zhihai Temple and to serve as the guardian of the state’s sacred fires. Yet, considering my own rustic nature, I have repeatedly received the imperial grace of Your Majesty.
On this day, we humbly encounter Your Majesty, the Emperor, who, out of compassion for the monastic community, has specially turned His Imperial gaze toward us.
You have commanded that we ascend the seat in the Cide Hall to proclaim the Prajñāpāramitā. From this moment, the Chan school shall shine with glory for ten thousand years.
Reflecting upon this sacred grace, we know not how to repay it. Undaunted by the prospect of death a hundred thousand times over, your servant ventures to set forth the Buddha-Dharma.
I have spoken thus many times, wishing to offer even a fraction of assistance regarding Your Majesty’s myriad affairs of state.

It is said that the waves of the river of craving within the triple world are broad, and the billows of the sea of suffering for the four modes of birth are deep. To attain liberation and transcendence, one must awaken to and clarify the Buddha-dharma.
Yet this Buddha-dharma is not obtained from outside the mind, nor is it transmitted by another; it is entirely Your Majesty’s own pure [mind].
The Sage’s mind—the original Buddha-nature—is perfectly luminous and penetratingly clear, fully manifest in daily life.
Should one’s single thought correspond with it, it is never not present. Formerly, the Venerable Potalaka of Western India constantly instructed a king regarding the Buddha-nature, saying:
"O King, when it functions, it appears in eight locations. What are these eight? When in the womb, it is called the body; when dwelling in the world, it is called..."
When in the eyes, it is called seeing; in the ears, hearing; in the nose, smelling fragrances; in the tongue, discourse; in the hands, grasping; and in the feet, running.
It manifests everywhere, encompassing all within the sands of the world-realms, yet when withdrawn, it is contained within a single minute particle. Those who awaken to this—

This is called True Suchness-Buddha-nature (*tathatā-buddhadhātu*). Those who are deluded call it the essence of delusive thought (*vikalpa-sattva*). When the king heard this, he attained immediate awakening.
Now, Your Majesty the Emperor, need only turn the light back upon yourself, and you will immediately realize that you are identical to the fundamental source.
Thus, while responding to ten thousand affairs daily, everything is none other than the samādhi of Your Majesty’s Buddha-nature. What action could possibly exist outside of this?
These thousand transformations are none other than the radiance of Your Majesty’s Buddha-nature.

Even down to every movement of the countenance and every turn of the body, as well as all seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing—each and every thing is manifest, each is perfectly luminous, and nothing is lacking.

This is just as in the case of the late Emperor Renzong, who for over forty years governed with benevolence and forbearance; he profoundly investigated the principles of Chan and thoroughly realized its source, such that amidst the myriad affairs of state...
Emperor Xia frequently summoned Chan Master Huailian of Dajue and Chan Master Daolong of Yuanming to the Rear Garden to ascend the hall.

There, they engaged in mutual debate, chanted and composed verses in response to one another, and expounded upon the Chan vehicle (zongcheng), the influence of which continues to this day and serves as a model for the Chan monasteries.

Furthermore, at the beginning of the Yuanfeng era, Emperor Shenzong, seeking a dharma-heir for the imperial succession, reformed the Xianglan Vinaya Monastery by dividing it into two Chan establishments:

one named Huilin and the other Zhikai. He summoned the Southern Chan Master Yuanzhao Zongben and the Chan Master Zhengjue Benyi to reside there as abbots with their disciples, where they opened the hall to preach the Dharma. On one occasion, the Emperor summoned them in a relaxed and informal manner.
It is so. When the question was raised regarding the fundamental principles of the Buddha-dharma, Chan was examined; as one probes the sacred mind, realization becomes ever more profound.
Since the arrival of the Patriarchs in this land, there has never been such a flourishing occasion of imperial veneration as that experienced in our dynasty.
Both Emperor Renzong and Emperor Shenzong were willing to turn their sagely minds toward the study of its mechanisms and to inquire with penetrating insight. Thus, they established Chan monasteries.
One knows that the Buddha-dharma is most supreme and most noble, most wondrous and most divine. Therefore, the teaching says:

if one is among Śakra or Brahmā, one is the most honored among Śakra and Brahmā, and for them this Dharma is preached; if one is among kings or great ministers, one is the most honored among kings and great ministers, and for them this Dharma is preached;
if one is among the empress or the palace ladies, one is the most honored among the empress and the palace ladies...
World-Honored One, you preach this Dharma whether among the imperial relatives and crown princes, or as the most honored among the imperial relatives and crown princes;
whether among the inner ministers and high officials, or as the most honored among the inner ministers and high officials;
even among monks and laypeople, among things and among men—you preach this Dharma with complete impartiality. Since the Buddha-Dharma is thus...
This is supreme and wondrous; it possesses such majesty. I pray that Your Majesty, amidst the myriad affairs of state, may deign to set aside your sacred mind for a moment and attain awakening.

When this manifests before you at every turn, you will finally know that it is inherently perfected from the beginning and is not obtained from without—what is called "understanding ten thousand transformations through a single word.
Yao and Shun were truly non-active (*wuwei*). I, your servant, have ventured to compose a mountain verse in one chapter, which I offer to Your Universal [Majesty].
I announce this to the great assembly of devas and humans, so that they may know: Our Emperor, His Majesty, is a Buddha of the present age.
By the power of his great compassionate vows, he accords with Heaven and responds to humanity, nurturing all living beings and upholding the Buddha-dharma.

Your servant is overwhelmed by the boundless longing to gaze upon Heaven and to receive the Sage’s grace; my agitation and trepidation reach their utmost limit. The eulogy says: The Buddha manifests many bodies according to circumstances; Humanity...

Having descended from the heavens to transform the common people, you must know that the Elder of Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa in days of yore has now manifested as the Sage-Sovereign of the Holy Song Dynasty of China.
Your servant has ventured to extol these humble matters, thereby defiling Your Majesty’s celestial hearing. I humbly pray that You will hold me in high regard.

On the day of opening the hall, Emperor Zhezong dispatched an imperial messenger to present incense. After the Master had finished his expressions of gratitude for this favor, he ascended the seat and offered incense.
Having completed the prayers for the Emperor’s long life, he spread his sitting mat. Dharma Cloud Da Tong Chan Master then struck the gavel.
The Master looked left and right and said: "Heaven and earth are vast and open; the sun and moon shine with brilliance. The four classes of people come like children to their parents;
the myriad flowers converge like spokes in a wheel. Everywhere the Dharma-gate is grandly opened. If you wish to look at it, your eyes are diseased and flowers float before you.
The successive heart-seals are brilliantly manifest; if you attempt to grasp them, your form withers and your arms break. When you have reached this point, everyone, how should you observe it?"
Do you understand? Only those superior men who transcend the mundane do not paint eyebrows upon their own brows.

As for those on the later path or beginners, they must first wash water with water. Question: "Incense is bestowed by Heaven and burned in the golden incense burner; as an auspicious omen, it is peerless in all the world.
Thus, Your Majesty’s grace is most profound—what dharma will the Master employ to praise the Imperial Realm? The Master said:
The sun and moon illuminate the celestial virtue; the mountains and rivers fortify the Imperial Abode.

A monk said, "If that is so, then the golden branches will naturally flourish, and the jade leaves will forever spread their fragrance. The Master said, "Since one phrase has been set forth in circulation, all living beings bow their heads. The monk said:
"If this is so, then the wind of Yao and the wind of the Patriarchs shall fan together; the sun of Shun and the sun of the Buddha shall shine equally bright.

The Master said: "Hanshan claps his hands; Shide sings a song. [The disciple] asked: "The former Emperor first reformed the Zen garden, and the present Sovereign has succeeded to the sagehood, once again fanning the ancestral style.
For such incomparable grace, how may one repay it? The Master said: "Sandalwood smoke rises from the incense burner; within the void..."
Auspicious vapors floated about. The monk asked, "If that is so, then you have already repaid the sovereign's grace and your teacher’s kindness; but what of the meaning of the Patriarchs?
The Master said, "I remember well my time at Lotus Peak, gazing for many years at the white clouds. The monk said, "Today I have heard what I had never heard before."
The Master asked, "What did you hear? The monk said, "Auspicious clouds rise by the nine-layered city walls; auspicious vapors arise before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion.
The Master said, "A truly excellent message; you must examine it with great care. The monk said, "From now on, the moon of the sky and the stars is divided equally;
it shines coolly and perfectly round. The Master said, "You have the fortune to gaze upon it. [The monk] asked about the imperial enterprise.
Prosperity! May your sagely depth moisten boundless realms; may the wind of the Dharma spread everywhere. May the *udumbara* flower bloom in the springtime of the Imperial Capital.
To cut directly to the root—please, Master, speak quickly. The Master said: "The clear dream of the stone channel; the cold chanting of frost in the golden hall. The monk said:
"With one word you have already offered prayers for the longevity of the Southern Mountain; throughout the eight directions, all joyfully celebrate the Great Peace. The Master said: [Silence].
"A single word for your birthday congratulations comes from you; how about the phrase for ultimate peace? The monk said, "In the heavens, all stars bow toward the North;
among men, no water does not flow toward the East. The Master said, "Among the worldly people who calculate and deliberate, how many truly recognize such kindness and virtue?
The monk said, "If one does not come forward, how can one know it is thus? The Master said, "Turn your head back and look now!"
The Master held up his whisk and called out, "Does the assembly see it?
This whisk in my hand emits hundreds of kinds of jewel-light for all of you in successive layers. He then struck the meditation seat and asked, "Do you hear it?
On this lion throne beneath me, every word expounds the definitive meaning of the One Vehicle for all of you. If you can awaken here, then throughout kalpas as vast as space..."

The karmic consciousness of self and person shall vanish like smoke and fly away like ashes; the present body, past lives, the faculties, objects, and worldly afflictions shall be utterly melted like ice and thawed like snow.
Then, the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye of Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa will be seen, shining brightly before the eyes in its full manifestation;
the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa from Śrīparvata will be revealed, radiantly manifest throughout the entire body. It is like Yajñadatta awakening to his own face in the mirror—it was there all along.
It is simply one's own head, like a strongman obtaining the round jewel upon his forehead; once attained, it cannot be acquired from another.

In this way, the immeasurable *abhijñās* and *samādhis* are inherently perfected in every particle of dust, and the Dharma-gates of the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are fully present in every thought-moment.
O worthy ones, if you can penetrate it in such a manner, you may say that you have realized the birthlessness of all phenomena (*anutpāda*).
Without waiting for eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*), one immediately attains perfect enlightenment. Do you wish now to see the Unborn? After a long silence, he said:

"A single breath remains silent, yet it contains all forms; where do the myriad spirits go to thank this impartiality? I, the monk Dao-wu, am incapable of universal salvation. My practice has not been heard of far and wide.

With a body and mind like ashes and wood, I have settled myself beneath the crags of the mountains. Deer and elk leave but sparse tracks there; how could I ever endure the hub of the imperial capital?
Regarding this journey: having distantly received the Imperial Edict descending upon us, we would certainly wish to secretly evade it, yet how could we dare?

We merely reflect that, feeding upon the water and milk of the King of the Nation, we find it difficult to bear the weight of his supreme virtue; born from the generative power of Heaven and Earth, how can we ever repay such great kindness?
Thus, like clouds hastening and waves surging, they rush toward the sea to follow the dragon.

This is surely because Your Majesty, the Emperor, having manifested as the sovereign with a mind of Equal and Wondrous Enlightenment, upholds the True Path of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and grandly succeeds to the ancestral foundation.

Therefore, this humble fragrance of a blade of grass has been graced by the profound bounty of the *Liāoxiāo* [Odes]. How could Your Servant not exert himself in the incense and lamps, remaining ever vigilant and solemn?
The assembly of black-robed monks strives to transmit the tradition of True Quiescence and reverently extols the transformation of Non-action.

On this auspicious occasion of opening the hall, we offer our congratulations and pray for His Majesty the Emperor: may his virtue outshine that of Yao and Shun, and his Way surpass that of Fuxi and Huangdi.

May you assist the auspicious destiny for ten thousand years and preserve the jade chart for a hundred generations. May the winds be harmonious and the rains timely, may all things flourish and the people be at ease.

The subject’s sincere prayers are profound, yet words fail to fully express them. Having stood for a long time before the assembly of the Compassionate Ones, I humbly entreat you to take care of yourself.
Lohan Chan Monastery on Mount Lu was founded by Master Nan, a native of Tingzhou. His secular surname was Zhang. In his youth, he left home to become a monk at Jinquan Temple near the city.

His nature was pure and serene, and his aspirations were lofty and far-reaching. After donning the black robes and receiving full ordination, he traveled extensively through various monastic communities.

There, he studied under Chan Master You of Donglin, with whom he attained a profound and secret realization of the mind-ground. Later, he returned to Mount Lu and emerged from seclusion to take up residence there.
He maintained [the Dharma], and his reputation for the Way spread far and wide. Scholars from all quarters all regarded him as a "Little Nanyue.
On the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed? The Master said: "Look after five days. The monk said:

"In that case, you are a descendant of Huanglong and the legitimate son of Luohan. The Master said: "You have misapplied your words. Another asked: "When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, gold sprang up from the earth..."

Lian asked, "Master, now that you have appeared in this world, what auspicious signs are there? The Master said, "The whale swallows the ocean waters until they are exhausted, revealing the coral branches.
The monk said, "In the past it was the World-Honored One; today it is the Master. The Master said, "Its breath charges through the Ox and Dipper constellations.

The monk asked, "If sound and form do not reach [the mind], the illness lies in seeing and hearing; if words and explanations do not suffice, the fault lies in the lips and mouth. Regarding these two principles and two meanings, I pray for [your instruction]."
The Master pointed directly at him. The Master said, "A single character does not bear a stroke. The monk said, "The waters of Ancient Creek reflect the new moon;
the cold pines of Old Ridge meet spring again. The Master said, "Two characters do not form a pair. The monk said, "At midnight, colored clouds enshroud the jade image;
when day breaks, five clouds veil the mountain peak. The Master said, "What a true message! He asked, "O cub of the lion!"
The assembly followed him. After three years, he was able to let out a great roar. [The monk asked: "Before he had left the forest, how would you say it?
The Master said, "His head would split and his forehead crack. The monk asked, "After he has left the forest, how would you say it? The Master said, "The crown of his head touches the ground.
The monk asked, "What about when there is neither entering nor leaving? The Master said, "Advancing forward and retreating backward. The monk said, "But tell me, where does it fall?"
"In what place? The Master said, "The assembly has eyes.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Way is impartial; its power is invincible. It is like the wind passing through grass that bends, or like the arrival of spring when flowers bloom.
Not even a Buddha’s hand can block it; how could the human heart possibly restrain it? To follow it, every single thing shines with brilliance; to oppose it—"
Then every head loses its color; neither opposing nor conforming, square and round as they may be, responding to calls according to their voices, high and low as they naturally are.
Like a reflection appearing before a mirror, self and other forget their sentiments. Manifesting illusory spiritual powers, one achieves illusory perfect enlightenment.
Thus, the ten thousand folds of Mount Lu together turn the Wheel of Dharma, and the thousand fathoms of the Poyang River jointly proclaim the profound meaning. It is simply like this.
The golden rooster pecks through the lapis lazuli shell; the jade hare pushes open the gates of the azure sea. [The Master] struck the meditation seat once and ascended the hall, saying:
"The painted horns announce the spring at the red pavilion; ten thousand households together celebrate as all things are renewed.
Who would have known that the verdant cypress by the courtyard is none other than the one who asked questions back then? There is no body to be had, and no year to be reckoned—only then..."
Ultimately unchanging, it persists through the cycles of coming and going. While the four seasons shift, it does not shift; while the single breath moves, it is not moved.

A hundred years of birth and death are like drifting clouds; ten generations of past and present are like a flash of lightning. When emotion transcends the realm of forms, the Way accords with the midst of the universe.
Without so much as a hair’s breadth of existence, one shares the same longevity as empty space. Simply turn toward seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing to grasp the face of your original nature.
[The Master] looked at them for a long while and said: "The jade hare sinks behind the western ridge; the golden crow emerges from the eastern sea.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The solar disc leaves the sea; the lunar essence sinks into the void. Radiating brilliance through ancient and modern times, it loiters across the west and east.
Unaware, the youth with rosy cheeks suddenly becomes an old man with white hair. Yet this spiritual clarity remains unchanging, ever present within words and speech. Tut!"
"Even if the great void were to decay and crumble, this 'He' would remain forever. If you know where it falls, you may roam freely as you please. Pshaw! Entering the hall, he said:
'Without relying on a single blow, the great treasure is perfected; the Great Sword emerges from its scabbard, its cold light chilling.
For your sake, I have severed the antelope's horn and nailed together a jade-green platter in the void. Well worth grasping, yet you must look further—turning it over and over."
"Departing from the vast darkness. [He] struck the meditation seat once. Entering the hall, he said:
"The mountain hall has opened its furnace today; the dim, cold clouds have not yet spread their snow.
One may poke at the fire to discuss whether it is cold or warm, but who knows who can call out for the Minister? The ancient sages sought people within the hot ashes. All [of you]...

When the Buddha walked through the midst of fierce flames, he saw that every land and every atom was identical to himself, and that every thought and every moment of mind was entirely in accord with the ultimate source.
To understand it in such a way is, in turn, not at all appropriate. Why?
Because "a single phrase that fits the head" is but a tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas.

Ascending the hall, he said: "From darkness, suddenly light breaks through; the radiance of the sun bursts forth over the sea. From severance, it is again continued; celestial music resounds in the void.
Even Kǎng Shìkuàng could not hear it, and Lílóu could not see it.

Only the Bodhisattva Without Supernatural Powers beats them one after another, each surpassing the other. I pray that the eastern wind will exert its full force, blowing them all at once into my gate."
He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Entering the hall, he said: "Heaven and earth serve as the furnace and bellows; the sun and moon act as the tongs and hammers. They smelt the pure wind to produce Buddhas and Patriarchs;
they refine the white clouds so that there is Dharma and ritual. A halo adorns the crown of the head; the ten-thousand-character mark is inscribed upon the chest. A-he-he!"
Knowing the unknowable, he rides backward upon the lion throne; leaping up, he ascends Mount Sumeru. Entering the hall, he said:
"The ninety days of a summer retreat pass day after day without deviation; the twelve hours of a single day pass hour after hour without change.
It is like the yellowness of gold and the azure of the sky—its color and its height remain unchanging and indestructible. How peaceful!
“One name, one character—how can this be similar to my numinous awakening?

Thus, one cultivates the myriad practices of empty flowers, sits in meditation within a moon-in-water dharma-hall, subdues the armies of demons within a mirror, and realizes the fruit of Buddhahood within a dream.

Today, the age of the Dharma has reached its full cycle; let us examine this thoroughly. After a long silence, he said: “Shifting the body, one shakes the Great Flower; cupping sweat, one sprinkles the *amṛta*.”

Ascending the hall, he said: "Object and self are both as they are; right and wrong are of one breath. The clouds have no mind, yet they listen to the dragon’s roar, filling the heavens and obstructing the earth.
The wind leaves no trace, yet it can hear the tiger’s cry, uprooting trees and sounding through the branches.

The Way has no root, yet it skillfully responds to all conditions, distinguishing the black-robed from the white-robed. Suddenly, in a single thought, one merges with the wind and clouds; one does not know who is 'I' as one walks."
There is no place of practice; one abides in the primordial non-abiding. He laughs loudly, "He-he! Rarely encountered, seldom met!
Ascending the hall, he said: "Zen is not Zen; the Way is not the Way. This three-inch tongue sweeps through chaos. Last night, the sun’s orb shed osmanthus blossoms;
this morning, in the moon’s cave, magical fungi have grown. A-he-he! Ten thousand ounces of gold cannot be found anywhere."
"A single phrase cuts off all deliberation; all dharmas do not reach one another. Entering the hall, he said:
"If you wish to propagate the Great Dharma, you must rely on the right person. If you borrow a favorable wind, you may then raise your sails and lift your oars.
Formerly, a monk asked Zhaozhou, "A student has newly entered the monastic community; I beg the Master for instruction. Zhaozhou said, "Eat..."
"Has the gruel finished? The monk replied, "The gruel has been eaten. The Master said, "Go wash your bowl. At these words, the monk attained sudden and great enlightenment.
The Master said, "After the bell rings this morning and before ascending the hall, everyone eats gruel; once full, one simply stops."
If you can chew it through, it will obstruct and block you. If you cannot chew it through, I grant you my approval.
Today, an Arhat rides an iron horse backward up Mount Sumeru, trampling through empty space without leaving a trace.
Do you all see him? Last night the wind arose and filled the courtyard with fragrance; it blew down three or five peach trees. The Master returned to his quarters and sat cross-legged.
He sat down and entered nirvana.
Zen Master Yanlong of Ciyun in Tanzhou ascended the hall and said, citing Xuansha’s address to the assembly:
"The entire earth is, after all, but a single bright pearl. At that time, a monk asked: "Since it is but a single bright pearl, [what is the meaning for] this student?"
"Why do you not recognize it? The monk said, "The whole body is the pearl; who else could be asked to recognize it?
The monk said, "Even though the whole body is it, how can it be that this student does not recognize it? The monk said, "Ask your own eyes.
The Master said, "All you Zen adepts, this koan is called 'feeding a child with chewed rice'—giving a staff even while holding the hand. Do you understand? If you have not yet,"

Yes. You must examine yourself and investigate; you must seek the ultimate truth. Do not speak recklessly or pursue empty verbiage, for that would lead only to a life spent in vain and a death in delusion. Investigate!
At Ziling Mountain in Yingzhou, Zen Master Zi asked: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind does he succeed? The Master said: "Nine in the middle, seven at the bottom.
The monk said: "I beg the Master’s compassion. The Master said: "An old man of a hundred years learning to follow the vermilion [of youth].
The monk said: "I do not understand the meaning of this; what is its intent? The Master said: "It is difficult for the old to act as the young. [Another] asked: "What is the Buddha?"
The general meaning of the Dharma. The Master said: "Better not to have anything at all. A monk asked: "What is the realm of Jingu Peak?
The Master said: "One mountain, one cloud. The monk asked: "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said: "An iron-boned arhat. [The monk] asked: "..."
"What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "Barefoot, treading through mud, cold as ice.
The monk asked, "I do not understand the meaning of this. The Master said, "Do not muddy the waters. A monk asked, "Why did the Great Sage of Sizhou appear in Yangzhou?
The Master said, "He was already within it. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "He humbled his majesty to conform to the lowly."
The monk said, "I thank the Master for his response. The Master said, "The thief is a petty person, yet his cunning surpasses that of a gentleman. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Do you all understand? The pivot of the Patriarchs' gate is not found in words or explanations. If one were to explain it further, it would needlessly separate one from the West."
Chan Master Shouchong of Baiyunshan Haihui in Shuzhou asked: "Everyone understands the single phrase of Yaoshan; what is the matter at Baiyun today?
The Master said: "It fills the void. The monk said: "Who knows that within today, the bright moon locks the city of Shu?
The Master said: "Rubbing the forehead, one gazes toward Fusang. He asked: "A single drop from Caoxi universally moistens the great thousandfold world-system."
“White clouds emerge from the mountains; how do they benefit sentient beings? The Master said, “Spread wide across the mouth of the cave; returning birds lose their nests.
The monk asked, “And what about the single path pointing south? The Master said, “An iron snake blocks the great road; its entire body is black as smoke.”

Ascending the hall, he said: "Pointing to and summoning the four sages, issuing commands to the six realms of ordinary beings, unifying the three worlds as a great monastery, and taking the ten voids as the gates of liberation.
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are the heart-source of the ancient Buddhas; the burning furnaces and cauldrons of boiling oil are the ground of awakening for sentient beings.
Upon a single mote of dust, one manifests the entire bodies of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. At that—
The mind of a single Buddha manifests the worlds of boundless sentient beings. If one can act in this way, then mind after mind is without knowing;
the entire mind is the Buddha, and the entire Buddha is the person. When person and Buddha are without distinction, one has finally entered the Way. Nevertheless, although it is thus:
"How do you speak a single phrase that does not fall into the gate of transformation? After a long silence, he said: "For nine years, I ate vegetable gruel;
few people know this matter.
Chan Master Jingfu Shengyue of Dongshan in Hongzhou ascended the hall and said: "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, one limps along..."

"Pull! Pass it by like this, everyone. Where does the point of benefit or harm lie? After a long silence, he said, "Listen and see how the various quarters judge this," and struck the meditation seat once before descending from the seat.
Chan Master Baoxiang Yuan of Mount Tiantai in Taizhou asked: "What is the realm of Baoxiang? The Master said: "A rootless tree upon a rock. The monk asked:
"Who is the person within the realm? The Master said: "The heart-holding priceless treasure. The monk asked:

The monk did not ask about his arrival, but instead asked, "What is the essential meaning of the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*? The Master said, "In the seven locations where the mind was sought, the mind was not found;

yet Śunyata feels ashamed, for his eyes and eyebrows are too coarse. The monk asked, "And what is the essential meaning of the *Perfect Enlightenment Sūtra*? The Master—

[The Master] said, "The moon in the cassia tree shines solitary and bright against the azure sky. The monk asked, "Since all Buddhas of the three periods of time emerge from this sutra, what is this sutra?
The Master said, "Recited continuously for a long time; it is neither meaning nor sound. The monk asked, "How does one uphold it?

"The moon is full. "Please, Master, speak quickly. The Master said, "The azure lapis lazuli moon. The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it?

Furthermore, you are all merely ordinary folk. When you arrive here, how will you discern the truth?
If you can discern it, I shall allow you to pass through this single thread of the Way. If you cannot discern it, you will all be exposed by this old monk.
Chan Master Yongcheng of Nanfeng in Quanzhou ascended the hall and said: "Beginning at Mount Jiji, the flame was passed on; at Shaoshi, the fragrance flowed forth.
The clouds of compassion were widely spread, and the sun of the Buddha was grandly opened. The teachings were divided into the Three Pitakas, while the One Mind was pointed directly at.

Sometimes the staff and shout were applied together in a total presentation; sometimes, through granting and revoking, host and guest were mutually established. Sometimes the Vajra was held like a drawn sword; sometimes the Master..."
The disciple turns over; sometimes it is like clouds rushing forth as illumination and function are employed, or like lightning flashing in a sudden stroke of the spiritual pivot.

All of this is nothing other than the excision of heterodoxy and delusion, the opening wide of the profound and subtle, and the direct clarification of the fundamental source, arriving at the ground of reality. O worthy ones, only when you have reached this point may I allow you a single thread of the Way with which to deliberate.
If it is otherwise, you are entirely relying on your teachers to form interpretations; such a state is not the way.

When Chan Master Guanghui Guo of Fuzhou was residing at Xiansha Monastery as a successor of Chan Master Minghui Wen of Fuzhou, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The Buddha attained enlightenment through mindlessness."
The mind is deluded because there is a Buddha; the Buddha-mind is the place of purity. Beyond the clouds, a wild monkey cries. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "Eight chi and two cun at the tip of a hair. The monk asked, "What is the mind? The Master said, "Two zhang and three chi at the tail of a needle."
The monk said, "The Buddha-mind leaves no trace in either case. The Master said, "It fills the universe. The monk asked, "Why is it so?
The Master said, "Hold your ears and strike the chime."

Chan Master Chuandeng of Yongan Monastery at Chengtian Temple in Suzhou, whose Dharma lineage was that of Chan Master Baoben Yuan of Huzhou, was named Yuanzheng. He was a native of Pingyin County in Danzhou.

His secular surname was Zheng. He pursued his studies at Taiping Xingguo Temple in his home province, taking Lìzàngzhì as his teacher. He received the tonsure and full ordination through formal examination.

Thereafter, he studied the *Abhidharma* and various treatises, traveling extensively to visit masters throughout the land. In his later years, he arrived at the Dharma seat of Chan Master Yuàn of Wanshòu Monastery in Suzhou.
While contemplating the dialogue concerning the cypress tree in front of the hall, he attained enlightenment regarding the mind-ground. He composed a verse which says: The Cypress Tree of Zhaozhou.
"My son, let no one know where you go. Cast aside the sweet peach tree; seek the mountains to pluck the sour pears. Thus was Master Yuan certified.

A question was asked: "My Master, you have gathered the assembly of humans and devas once more; I pray you will reveal the lightning-fast mechanism of the Westward Coming. The Master said:

[The monk] asked, "When peach blossoms and willow catkins discuss True Suchness (*tathatā*), what is this discussion of the True? The Master said, "The plum blossoms on the ridge are white;

where the incense smoke rises, it is all too clear. The Master said, "This is not that one dharma.
The monk said, "Selling gold, he happens upon a buyer for gold. The Master said, "This is brass."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The multitudes of devas and human beings all receive this power of grace. Great assembly, suppose there were a person who said, 'I do not receive the Buddha’s power of grace;
I do not dwell within the three realms, nor do I belong to the five elements.

The Patriarchs dare not define me, and the Buddhas of the past dare not bestow a name upon me. Now tell me, what kind of person is this? After a long silence, he said: 'Leaning against the stone cliff.'"
He burned an iron bowl and hung a copper gong upon a pine branch. He asked, "Consoler Taiguang has come specifically for this purpose;

The Master said: "When the music ends, the person is no longer seen; on the river, several peaks stand green. The monk said: "When the river moon shines, the reflection of the zither appears;
where the pine wind blows, the sound of the voice is clear. The Master said: "Throughout the night, the cold stream snows until dawn;

"What tune is this? The monk said, "If Bo Ya were here, he would be ashamed to appear before Yong'an. The Master said, "It is difficult to find one who truly understands the music.
The monk said, "If the entire universe and the great earth are but a single zither, how do you, Master, strike the strings?
The Master said, "Every beat is a command. The monk said, "Now that the official banner has graced us with its presence, may I be permitted to reveal a bit of news?"

"No. The Master said, "I allow it. The monk said, "Do not say that there is only the cypress tree in the courtyard; you have also gained the *zhāngtáng* (sweet pear) tree to honor the ancestral lineage.

The Master said, "The same wind blows over a thousand miles. The Master then continued: "If one were to judge right and wrong based on the blow of the staff, Deshan would be a sinner against the teaching.

"O King, Yong'an speaks thus. If there were no person with clear eyes to bear witness, the entire world would fall into pits and ravines.

His poetry is that of the *Zhōu Nán* and *Shào Nán*; his discourse on the Way is that of Zhuangzi and Lǎozǐ. Even speaking in such a manner—"
"You are not yet people of clear vision. Do you recognize a person of clear vision? Yongan pointed this out to everyone. After a long silence, he said:
"The giant turtle must not carry off the Three Mountains; let them remain to sleep upon the summit of Penglai."
Chan Master Deheng of Renwang Monastery on Fenghuang Mountain in Huzhou ascended the hall. A monk came forward from the assembly and said, "Do you understand?

"Buying and selling are no obstacle. The Master said, "I leave it entirely to you to call out and seek. A monk asked, "When the bell tolls and the gong rings, and brocade and embroidery are interwoven, where are Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra?

"Resting, with whom do you discuss it? The Master said, "The bright moon hangs in the void; heaven and earth naturally divide their forms.

A Request for Instruction. When Linji was at Huangbo, he asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma three times and was beaten three times.

Chan Master Yiqing of Mount Touzi in Shuzhou, a successor in the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Jingyan Ming’an of Mount Dayang in Yingzhou, was surnamed Wang and was a native of Qingzhou. When the Master was first born, he...
The father had passed away and the mother was ill; having no means to nourish him, she left him among the thickets by the side of the road.
A strange person passing by heard his voice and, filled with wonder and admiration, exclaimed, "This child shall one day attain the fruit of the Way. He then took him in and raised him.

At the age of eight, he entered the monastic life under the venerable Master Wenshou at Miaoxiang Temple in his native province. Having completed his studies and received full ordination, he first listened to the *Śata-śāstra*.
He studied various treatises on the Dharma and subsequently practiced the Mahāyāna sūtras; without waiting for them to reach their conclusion, he thoroughly understood their essential meanings.

When both monastics and laypeople requested him to lecture, his fellow practitioners gathered like clouds. Later, hearing of the Southern School, he abandoned his seat to seek instruction. He arrived at the Dharma assembly of Chan Master Yuanjian of Fushan.
Zhaojue knew he was a vessel for the Dharma and immediately permitted him to enter his room. He instructed him on the occasion of the outsider’s question to the Buddha.

One day, while sitting among the cliffs, as Zhaojue was recounting that previous dialogue, he suddenly heard the sound of a wooden board and attained sudden, vast enlightenment. He returned to seek confirmation, and Zhaojue gave his seal of approval, saying:
"In the past, I received from Chan Master Ming’an a true portrait of him, along with his monastic robe and leather sandals; I have sent you to seek them."
He was a vessel of the Dharma, commissioned to continue his lineage. Observing that your understanding would not let fall the former fragrance, he presented a prophetic verse, titled at its head:
"To succeed me and perpetuate the style of the Great Sun (Daiyō) School. The verse says: "The grass upon the peaks of Yangguang Mountain, Relies on you to await its true value.
Where the extraordinary sprouts flourish luxuriantly, The profound and secret roots of the spirit remain firm. Because the assembly at Haihui was left vacant, he firmly appointed him as its master.
He went forth to propagate the Great Matter. Next, he moved to Touzi, where he further responded to the prophecy that the Master Ciji would return as a red-robed incarnation.
On the day he opened the hall for formal teaching, he was asked: "Master, you have just offered incense to pray for the Emperor; tell me, how many years old is the Emperor this year?"
The Master said: "The moon enshrouds the distant red cassia; the stars bow toward the high North Star. The monk said: "South Mountain rises straight up to match the longevity of Heaven;

"Where does one go when leaving? Where does one dwell when staying? Whether going or staying, what is there to follow? Transcendent and peerless, at the parting of ways, a single phrase is directed toward..."
Who raised [this case]? The Milky Way is white at night as the solitary moon emerges.
This is the lineage of Chan Master Xing Si of Mount Qingyuan in Luling, the fourteenth generation, and Chan Master Chengyue of Chengtian in Wuzhou, the Dharma heir of [Chan Master] Chengyue.
Chan Master Zhongyan of Chengtian Temple in Wuzhou asked: "The Brahma King invited the Buddha for the sake of all living beings;
today, the Magistrate invites you—what matter does he seek to accomplish? The Master said: "The assembly knows how to acknowledge grace. A monk said: "In that case, humans and devas have met.
The Master said: "It is no hindrance to possess the eye [of wisdom]."
