Compiled by [Song Bao] Weibai, Dharma-Transmitting Chan Master Foguo, Abbot of Fayun Chan Monastery in Dongjing.
From the *Nianggu Men* (Gate of Citing Ancient Cases), twenty cases concerning Chan Master Mingjue Chongxian of Xuefeng Mountain in Mingzhou are presented.
Deshan addressed the assembly, saying: "Tonight I shall not answer questions. Anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows of the staff. A monk stepped forward.
The monk bowed, and Deshan struck him. The monk said, "I have not even asked a question. Deshan said, "Where are you from? The monk replied, "From Silla.
Deshan said, "Before you have even stepped onto the boat's railing, thirty blows are well-deserved for you. Fayan commented:
"Master Deshan of great stature has split his own discourse into two pieces. Yuanming said: "Master Deshan of great stature is a dragon’s head..."

"Snake's tail. The Master said, "Although these two elders were skilled at cutting the long to patch the short and abandoning the heavy for the light, even so, they would not yet have been able to see Deshan.
Why? Deshan was much like one who wields the authority outside the imperial gates;
he possessed the sword that, if it does not decide when it ought to decide, will invite chaos. Do you all wish to recognize the Korean monk? He was simply a head-on collision."
"A blind man clinging to a pillar. It is said:
When Baizhang was attending Mazu for his second visit, as he stood in attendance, Mazu looked with his eyes at the whisk in the corner of the meditation platform.
Baizhang said, "Is it this very function? Is it apart from this function? Mazu said, "After you have opened up your two flaps of skin in the future, what will you use to save people?
Baizhang took up the whisk and held it aloft. Mazu said, "Is it this very function? Is it apart from this function?
Baizhang hung the whisk back in its original place. Mazu then gave a shout; Baizhang was deaf for three whole days. The Master said, "How extraordinary!"

Virtuous practitioners of meditation, those who today enumerate its lineages are very numerous, yet those who investigate its source are extremely few. It is generally said that Baizhang attained great enlightenment under Mazu’s shout;
but is this truly accurate? However, as the characters "刁" (diāo) and "刀" (dāo) are similar, yet "魚" (yú) and "魯" (lǔ) differ, so it is with these matters.
If one is a man of clear eyes, they cannot be deceived by even a single point. Take for instance what Mazu said to you: [text continues]
Later, when he opened his two lips, with what would he have been considered a human? Baizhang raised his whisk;

was it like a worm gnawing through wood, or was it like the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching? If you wish to understand why everyone’s ears were deaf for three days, know that in a great furnace, refined gold remains unchanged in color.
The Case is presented. Xiangyan sat and said: "It is like a person climbing a tree, with a branch held in his mouth, his hands not grasping branches, and his feet not treading on the tree.
If someone below the tree asks about the meaning of the Westward Journey, if he does not answer, he violates the questioner’s intent;
yet if he answers, he loses his body and his life. At such a time, what should one do? There was a monk named Tuhou (Tiger Head).
Xuefeng said, "I do not ask about having already climbed the tree; I ask the Master to speak before climbing it. Yanguan laughed heartily.
Xuefeng said, "It is easy to speak from atop the tree, but difficult to speak beneath it. I, this old monk, have climbed the tree;
bring forth your question!"
Case: A monk asked Xuefeng, "What is it like when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine? Feng said, "Staring with wide eyes, one cannot see the bottom.
The monk asked, "And what of those who drink from it? Feng said, "It does not enter through the mouth. The monk took this up and asked Zhaozhou.
Zhaozhou said, "It cannot enter through the nostrils. The monk then asked Zhaozhou, "What is it like when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine? Zhaozhou—
[The Master] said, "Suffering. The monk asked, "What about one who drinks? Zhaozhou said, "Dead. When Xuefeng heard this being cited, he said, "Zhaozhou was an ancient Buddha;
from this point on, he would no longer answer questions. The Master said, "Everyone in the assembly says that Xuefeng did not bring up this monk’s question."
This is why Zhaozhou refused to consent. To interpret the matter in such a way would be a profound disservice to the ancients. Xuedou, however, was not like this;
he was one who cut through nails and severed iron—a master of the fundamental school. He levels the high by descending to the low, a feat difficult for any other to achieve.
Case: One day, Qingshan ascended the hall, raised his fist, and then opened his hand, saying, "Opened, it becomes a palm;
the five fingers are distinct. He then closed his hand again, saying, "Now it is a fist; there is certainly no high or low. Is there anyone who can deliberate upon this?
A monk stepped forward from the assembly and raised his fist. Qingshan said, "You are merely a fellow who knows neither opening nor closing. The Master said, "Snow."
It is not so with the Jewel. He then raised his fist and said, "When clenched, it becomes a fist; there is high and low. He then opened his hand and said, "When opened, it becomes a palm;
there is no factionalism and no partiality. Now tell me: is it better to benefit others by opening [the hand], or is it better to benefit others by holding it fast?

Opening it is like building a carriage; clenching it is like fitting the wheels together. If you say, "Building the carriage inside the gate, fitting the wheels together outside," you have missed the point.
I also know that you have been making your living inside a ghost cave.
To cite: Dongshan went to Yunmen. Yunmen asked, "Where have you recently departed from? Dongshan said, "Chadu. Yunmen asked, "Where did you spend the summer?
Dongshan said, "Baoci in Hunan. Yunmen asked, "When did you leave there? Dongshan said, "Last year, in the eighth month."

Yunmen said, “I release you from three blows of the staff. On the following day, Xiangshan went up to pay his respects and asked, “Yesterday I received the Master’s release from three blows of the staff;
I do not know where my fault lay. Yunmen said, “You rice-bag! Jiangxi and Hunan proceed just like this.
At these words, Xiangshan attained great enlightenment. The Master said, “The spirit and bearing of Yunmen were like...”

O King! If you had been pressed upon it, it would have melted away like ice and crumbled like a fortress. Had you acted according to the command at that moment, your descendants would not have come to such an end.

It is said: The National Teacher called his attendant three times. When he was pointed out, he did not arrive; when the attendant responded three times, he arrived but was not pointed out. Take this up.
"It is I who have betrayed you; who would have known that you were betraying me? You cannot clear yourself before Xuedou.
Yunmen said, "What is it that the National Teacher betrayed the attendant at? To understand this is also groundless. The Master said:
"Originally, he did not understand. What is it that the attendant betrayed the National Teacher? 'Even if one’s bones were ground to powder and one’s body shattered, it would still not repay him.
The Master said: 'Pointlessly! Pointlessly!'"
Case: Master Zu asked Nanquan, "The mani-jewel, people do not recognize it; it is personally held within the Tathāgatagarbha. What is the Tathāgatagarbha?
Nanquan said, "That which comes and goes with you, Old Teacher Wang, is the garbha. Master [Yunmen] said, "A fellow of the weeds.
Zu said, "That which neither comes nor goes is also the garbha. Master said, "Adding frost to snow."
The Patriarch asked, “What is the pearl? The Master replied, “Dangerous! To perform a feat atop a hundred-foot pole is not the work of a true master.
If one can apply the eye here, such that guest and host are exchanged, one is able to penetrate deeply into the tiger’s den.
If it is not thus, then even if you have attained the realization of a patriarch, you are still a man who has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake.”
Case: Master Mazu ordered Zhizang to deliver a letter to Mount Jing. When the Master of the Mountain (Guishan) opened the letter, he saw a perfect circle with a single dot placed within it.
When National Teacher Huairang heard this being related, he said, "Master Qin was still deluded by Master Ma. The Master (Yunmen) said: [The National Teacher was indeed deluded.]
Jingshan was already deluded; let that be. If he were to present this to the National Teacher, what other stratagem could he have employed to avoid being led astray?
An old master said, "At that time, he should have sat [in silence] and left it at that. Others have also said, "He should simply have drawn a line through it.
If one acts in such a way, it is merely a failure to recognize the distinction. I dare say that all the great teachers of the world possess the golden [eye].
Gangyan’s eyes were wide open as he performed various supernatural transformations; could he have possibly avoided this?
Xuansha’s insight is something I wish everyone to know together: even when Mazu merely drew [the horse] at that time, he was already deluded himself.
Case: There was a hermitage master at the foot of Nanquan Mountain. When a traveling monk passed by, he said to the master, "The Master of Nanquan has recently appeared in the world;
why do you not go to pay him homage? The master replied, "Not only Nanquan—were even a thousand Buddhas to appear in the world, I still could not go.
Nanquan heard of this and ordered Zhaozhou to go see him. Upon arriving, Zhaozhou immediately prostrated himself.
The Master did not intervene. As Zhaozhou went from west to east, the Master still did not intervene. As Zhaozhou again went from east to west, the Master still did not intervene.
Zhaozhou said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated," pulled down the curtain, and departed.
Upon returning, he related this to Nanquan. Nanquan said, "I have always suspected this fellow. The Master said, "How great was Nanquan! How great was Zhaozhou!"
This fellow carrying a wooden board has been thoroughly scrutinized.
It is said: A monk asked Master Zhimen, "What is the essence of prajñā? He replied, "An oyster containing the bright moon. The monk said:
"What is the functioning of Prajñā? He replied, "A rabbit conceiving a fetus. The Master said, "It not only secures the world, but also brings peace to the state.
If you can investigate and examine this well, then please walk alone upon the crimson clouds."
Case: A monk prostrated to Xuefeng. Xuefeng struck him five blows. The monk said, "What fault have I committed? Xuefeng struck him another five blows. The Master said:
"Xuedou never indulges in such entanglements with others. The first five blows were like the sun shining upon the sky;
the latter five blows were like clouds rising to bring rain. If you can discern this, you too deserve five blows."

Case: A monk asked Baling, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the teachings the same or different? Baling said, "When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree; when the duck is cold, it goes down into the water.
A monk asked Muzhou, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the teachings the same or different? Muzhou said, "The green mountains are themselves green mountains;
the white clouds are themselves white clouds. The Master said: "The question is the same in both cases, and the answers are similar. Within them lies the benefit of others."
Self-interest deceives others and deceives oneself. If you examine this clearly, you will surely find that [the masters] were foremost in realizing emptiness.
For example, when Mazu addressed the assembly, saying, "I saw Baizhang not knowing good from evil; as soon as the great assembly had gathered, he struck them all at once with his staff.
He then called out to the assembly, and as they turned their heads, Baizhang asked: 'What is it? There is.
"What is a place for conversation? Huangbo the Master, as the assembly was just gathering, struck them all down at once with his staff.
He then called out to the assembly; the assembly turned their heads. Huangbo said, "The moon is like a drawn bow; there is little rain and much wind. It is still somewhat better than that.
The Master [Xuedou] said, "What do you mean by 'still somewhat better'? It is simply not yet so. According to Xuedou, the assembly...

Assembled! At once, strike it down and let it rest. Perhaps there is someone with an unperforated iron hammer who will exert their utmost strength for the sake of the assembly, being well able to shoulder this burden and capable of encompassing past and present, seizing hold of heaven and earth. [The Master] suddenly picks up his staff and says:
Letting this one move pass. Case:
Nanquan addressed the assembly, saying, "Wang Laozi is selling himself; is there anyone who will buy?
A monk came forward from the assembly and said, "I will buy him. Nanquan asked, "Neither as something expensive nor as something cheap—how do you buy him? The monk...
[Zhaozhou] remained silent. Wulong spoke on his behalf, saying, "The Master belongs to the exclusive category. Heshan spoke on his behalf, saying, "What kind of principle is this?
Zhaozhou said, "Next year I will make a cloth robe for the Master. The Master [Xuedou] said:

"Although these masters compete in their skillful buying, they have not yet understood how to surrender the mechanism. But tell me, would Nanquan have approved? Xuedou also intended to offer a response."
This price leaves Nanquan with no way to advance and no ground to retreat. It is neither expensive nor cheap;
how can it be purchased? No other place can accommodate the Master.
Case: While Jia Shan and Ding Shan were traveling together and conversing, Ding Shan said, "If there is no Buddha within birth and death, then there is no birth and death.
Jia Shan said, "If there is a Buddha within birth and death, then one does not become deluded by birth and death.
They could not agree with one another and went together to visit Da Mei. After they had met, they related their previous discussion in detail. Jia Shan asked, "I wonder which of us is correct?"
"Which one is close? Which one is distant? Meyan said, "One is close; one is distant. Jiashan asked again, "Which one is close?
Meyan said, "Go for now; come back tomorrow. The next day, Jiashan asked again, "I do not yet understand which one is close.
Meyan said, "He who is close does not ask; he who asks is not close. Later, when Jiashan was residing [in his own monastery], he said, "At that time, I was at Dayang..."
Daiman lost one eye. The Master said, "Jiashan did not know that he gained one eye.
If the old fellow Daiman had been struck with a staff all at once when he heard this case cited, it would have cut through the entanglements of both men;
he would have been a patriarch of the school for all time.
Case: Guishan asked Yangshan, "Where have you come from? Yangshan replied, "From the fields. Guishan said, "How many people are there in the fields?
Yangshan thrust down his spade and stood with his hands folded. Guishan said, "There are many people mowing grass on South Mountain."
When Shanshan picked up his spade and walked away, Xuansha said, "If I had seen him then, I would have kicked over the spade.
Jingqing said, "What can you do with the boat? Break the scoop! A monk asked Mingzhao, "The ancients' intent lay in the spade;
where did it lie when they folded their hands? Mingzhao called out, "So-and-so! The monk responded, "Yes? Mingzhao said, "Have you ever..."
"Did you see Yangshan in a dream? The Master said, "The elders of all quarters claim that the 'Plowing in the Furrow' (Inserting the Hoe) dialogue is extraordinary;
this is much like following the heterodox and pursuing evil. According to Xuedou’s own view, as soon as Yangshan was questioned by Guishan..."
He was so thoroughly bound by his own straw ropes that he was ten parts away from death.
[Case] Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying: "I have already met you at Wangzhou Pavilion;
I have already met you at Wushan Ridge; I have already met you before the Sangha Hall. Baofu asked Ehu: "Monk..."
"Let us leave it at that for now in the hall. Where shall we meet at Wanzhou Pavilion or Wushan Ridge?
Guo’u took a sudden step back toward the abbot’s quarters. Baofu immediately entered the monks' hall. The Master said, "These two elders were right, yet they only knew how Xuefeng let go;
they did not see Xuefeng holding fast. Suddenly, a monk stepped forward and asked, "I wonder, regarding Xuefeng..."
Dong asked, "What about it? Is this not a man who discerns different capacities and recognizes fortune and misfortune?
Is there any monk here who has met me at Wangzhou Pavilion or Wushan Ridge? After a long silence, he said, "Board-carrying Zen practitioners are as numerous as hemp and millet."
Case: One day, as the meal was late, Deshan took up his alms bowl and went to the Dharma Hall himself.
Seeing him, Xuefeng said, "Old man, the bell has not yet rung and the drum has not yet sounded; where are you going with your bowl? Deshan then turned back.
Xuefeng reported this to Yantou, who said, "Great as Deshan may be, he does not understand the final word. When Deshan heard this report, he gave the order: [End of Case]
The attendant summoned Yantou to the abbot’s quarters and asked, "Do you not agree with me, old monk? Yantou secretly conveyed his intention.
On the following day, when the Master ascended the hall for the discourse, it was unlike his usual style. Yantou went before the Sangha Hall.
He patted his hand and laughed loudly, saying, "I am glad that this old man understands the final word.
Hereafter, no one in the world will be able to do anything with me. Even so, he said, "It shall last for only three years. Mingzhao spoke on behalf of Deshan, saying, "Tsk! Tsk!"
"Do not dwell in departure. Do not dwell in departure. The Master said, "I have heard it said that there is such a thing as a 'one-eyed dragon,' yet it turns out he possesses only a single eye.
Little do you realize that Deshan is a toothless tiger.
Had it not been for Yantou’s discernment, how could today be different from yesterday? Do you wish to understand the final word?"
"I allow only the old barbarian to know; I do not allow the old barbarian to understand.
It is said: "One must not put sand in the eyes; one must not put water in the ears.

Suddenly, if there were a man who could believe deeply, who could maintain his ground, and who would not be deceived by others—what are the teachings of the patriarchs and buddhas to him? They are nothing but hot bowls.
Upon hearing this sound, he immediately requested that his alms-bag be hung high and his staff broken, vowing to become a man of the Way who has nothing to do.
He further said: "If one can fit Mount Sumeru within one's eyes and the great ocean waters within one's ears, such a person may be discussed by others.
The teachings of the Patriarchs and Buddhas are like a dragon finding water or a tiger relying on a mountain; yet one must still..."
Raising his alms-bag and slinging his staff over his shoulder, he too was a man of the Way with no concerns. He further said:
"It is not to be done this way, nor is it to be done that way; thereafter, do not engage in worldly entanglements.
Among these three men of the Way who were free from concerns, one was to be chosen as a teacher.
Two cases concerning National Teacher Nanyuan of Mount Huanglong in Hongzhou. Case 1:
Linji asked the temple steward, "Where have you been? The steward replied, "I went to the prefectural city to buy yellow rice."
Linji drew a line in front of him with his staff and said, "Can you buy this? The abbot shouted, and Linji struck him.
When the head cook arrived, Linji brought up the previous conversation. The head cook said, "The abbot does not understand the Master's meaning.
Linji asked, "And what about you? The head cook then bowed, and Linji struck him as well. Master [Xuedou].
He said: "When he shouts, I strike; when he prostrates, I also strike. Is there any distinction between near and far?
If there were no such distinction, Linji could not have been subjected to blind shackles and blind blows. If it were Guizong, it would not be so: when the abbot shouted, he could not let him off;
when the steward prostrated, letting him off was impossible. He further said: "Linji was carrying out his command."
Guizong let it pass. Thirty years later, someone will explain it through. Case:
A monk asked Master Da’jue, “What is it like when coming suddenly and going suddenly? Da’jue said, “The wind blows the willow catkins away.
The monk pressed further, “What is it like when neither coming nor going? Da’jue said, “The three peaks of Mount Hua.”
[The Master] points toward the sky. The Teacher says: "Dajue only understands the meeting of arrowheads and the convergence of principle and phenomena;
he does not realize that in chasing after the rat, he has broken the oil jar."
Three Cases from the Record of Chan Master Da Jue Huailian of Jingyin Monastery in Tokyo.
Master Yunmen once heard the sound of the mallet striking the gavel and said: "The World of Wondrous Joy shatters into a hundred fragments."
"You all, take up your bowls and go into the city of Hunan to eat.
The Master said, "Great as Yunmen may be, his affairs are still inverted. Here in my place, it is simply this:
the rector strikes the gavel, the head seat offers the food, I spread out my bowl, and the attendant distributes the benefits. Speak thus, and let the various quarters judge for themselves."
Case: Once Muzhou said, "Suddenly! Suddenly! The mountain monk says, "Not so! Not so! Why?
"The night crow cries at the dawn moon; the jade maiden swings on the swing."
[The Master] raised [the topic]: "Master Zhaor said, 'Only the Sage is one who takes the myriad dharmas as himself.
When Shitou the National Teacher saw this, he struck the desk once with his hand and said, 'The Sage has no self; there is nothing that is not his own self. The Master said:
"Big or small, Shitou was merely washing clods of earth in the mud. I, this mountain monk, am not like that."
After a long silence, he said: "I have always loved secluded and hidden places among the rivers and plains; the flowers and trees fill the garden, swaying in the spring breeze.
This concludes the four cases presented by Chan Master Guangzhao Huijue of Langya in Chuzhou.
Regarding Linji’s instruction to the assembly, he said: "Whenever there is an inquiry, I do not fail him; I recognize his place of origin. And: [The rest of the text follows].
If you come in this way, it is as if you have lost something; if you do not come in this way, you are binding yourself without a rope.

At all times, do not engage in confused deliberation. Whether you understand or do not understand, it is all a mistake. I speak clearly and plainly like this, leaving it entirely up to the people of the world to criticize and strip away.
The Master added: "How would you criticize? How would you strip away? After a long silence, he said: "Lowering the hook."
The four seas serve as the hook for catching the black dragon; this profound discourse beyond the ordinary is intended to seek out those who understand.
(He lets out a shout. He raises [the case]: When Zhaozhou came to visit Baizhang, Baizhang asked, "Where have you come from? Zhaozhou replied, "I have come from Nanquan."
Baizhang asked, "What sayings has Nanquan recently used to instruct his disciples? Baizhou said, "He tells people of this age that they must simply become silent.
Baizhang said, "Setting aside being silent for a moment, how would you express a state of utter bewilderment?
Baizhou stepped forward three paces. Baizhang gave a shout (*tuo*). Baizhou made a gesture of shrinking back his head. Baizhang said, "Excellent silence!"
However, Zhaozhou shook out his sleeves and went out. The Master [Zhaozhou] took it up, saying:
"The old man Zhaozhou gained his fangs and claws within the den of the lion.
He then cited: When Linji was ascending the hall, a monk came forward and bowed. Linji immediately shouted. The monk said, "Old Monk, do not probe too deeply."
"Good," said Linji. The monk asked, "Where do you say it lands? The monk then gave a shout.
Another monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Linji then shouted. The monk bowed. Linji said, "Tell me, was that a good shout or not?"
The monk said, "The grass-thief has been utterly defeated. Linji asked, "Where does the fault lie? The monk said, "A second offense will not be tolerated.
Linji then said, "If you wish to understand the Linji phrase of host and guest, go ask those two Chan guests who were just now questioning me.
The Master commented: "True gold must pass through fire."
Case: Shuilao Can visited Mazu. The Master asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

He was kicked over by Great Master Mazu; rising up, he clapped his hands and laughed heartily. At that moment, he attained great enlightenment and subsequently became a successor to Great Master Mazu.
Later, when a monk asked him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Shuilao said:
"Ever since Master Ma took that single step, it has been until now that people cannot stop laughing. The Master picked up the case and said, "Everyone, tell me:
did Shuilao ever attain awakening or not?"
Three Cases from Master Yunju Shan Xiaoshun’s *Jǔ*:

When Shishuang passed away, the assembly requested the Head Seat to take charge of the monastery. Attendant Qian said, "To succeed one's predecessor as abbot, one must understand the predecessor's intent.
For instance, when our late master said, 'Rest, cease; like cold ashes and withered wood...'"
[The Master] said, "It goes straight like a single white silk ribbon. I do not know how you, Head Seat, understand this.

The Head Seat replied, "The former master’s intent clarifies the matter of the 'one color' (the monochromatic). Qian the Attendant said, "If you understand it in such a way, how could you even dream of the former master’s intent?
The Head Seat then burned incense and said, "If I had understood the former master’s intent, the incense smoke..."
He departed at the moment the incense smoke was exhausted. Had he not realized the meaning of the former master, he would not have been able to depart at the moment the incense smoke was exhausted.
After a long while, when the incense smoke had ended, the Head Seat (Shouzuo) passed away. Attendant Qian said, "The Head Seat’s 'sitting death and standing transformation' is indeed beyond reproach;
yet, he has not even dreamed of the former master’s meaning. The Master said, "As for you all, what do you say?"
At the assembly hall, wherever people gather, they say that when the Head Seat speaks in such a manner, he is speaking according to principle;
this is why Attendant Qian was unwilling to accept him. Dayu said: "Throughout his entire life, Attendant Qian possessed only a single eye."
Case: Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Is it appropriate to meet him when he is in the light? Or is it appropriate to meet him when he is in the dark? Nanquan then returned to his quarters.
Zhaozhou remarked, "This old fellow usually talks incessantly, yet when questioned by me, he shuts his mouth and has no words."
The Head Seat said, "Do not say that the Master has nothing to say; it is simply that you, Senior Seat, do not understand.
Zhaozhou then slapped the Head Seat and said, "This slap ought to have been eaten by the old man at the head of the hall. The Head Seat then desisted. The Master said:
"How do you all understand this? Where you all understand it, you say that the Head Seat fell into Zhaozhou’s trap.
But how could understanding it in such a way be correct? Dayu said: 'Zhaozhou was truly like someone who is indifferent to others.'"
Case: Deng Yinfeng went to visit Danxia. On the way down the mountain, he encountered Danxia, who asked, "Where is Mount Danxia?
Danxia replied, "In that deep, dark expanse. Yinfeng stepped forward and grabbed him, saying, "Is it not just this very thing?
Danxia said, "A true lion cub—pushed once, he turns immediately. Yinfeng then desisted. The Master said, "Great!"
The Way of the Foolish. Danxia only noticed his shirt was torn; he did not realize his shoes were frayed.
Five Cases from Chan Master Chengtian Jian of Wuzhou.
Chan Master Fadeng asked a monk: "When Zen travelers meet, they merely snap their fingers. How many people can truly possess this mind?"
"I know. "How do you understand this? The monk snapped his fingers once. Yunmen said, "Even if you understand it thus, how can you be right?
The monk asked, "I do not yet know what your honorable intention is, Master. Yunmen snapped his fingers once. The Master commented:
"I thought the suffering of sentient beings was extreme; yet there are even more suffering sentient beings."

Case: Master Xuansha went to the abode of the Hermit Sandou. Sandou said, "I have lived on this mountain for many years; do not be surprised that I have no sitting mat. Case: Master Nanquan had a letter for Master Zhunü. In the letter he wrote: "Principle changes according to phenomena;
its vastness is not external. Phenomena arise from principle; their stillness is not internal.
After Zhunü read it, he held it up and asked the assembly, "Who can compose a reply to this mountain monk for me? Then a monk asked, "What is 'vastness'?"
"Vastness is not external. Juyou said, "To ask one and answer a hundred poses no obstacle.
The monk asked, "What is 'solitude is not internal'? Juyou said, "Beholding the countenance, it is not a good hand [at teaching].
The monk again asked Master Changsha, "What is 'broad vastness is not external'? Changsha closed his eyes and remained so for a long while. The monk asked, "What is..."
"Seclusion is not within. Changsha opened his eyes and looked at him. The monk then asked Zhaozhou, "What is 'vastness is not without'?
Zhaozhou made the gesture of eating. The monk said, "What is 'seclusion is not within'?"
The Governor made a gesture of wiping his mouth. The monk then reported this to Nanquan, who said, "These three men are not falsely claiming to be my legitimate sons.
The Master [Xuedou] comments: "Of these three men, one has obtained the skin, one has obtained the flesh, and one is such that Qin cannot claim him and Wei cannot govern him."
Case: A monk asked Master Dadian, "The person who is fundamentally unobscured—please, Master, cast your eyes high.
Dadian lowered his head. The monk said, "Today I have personally realized the Dharma-way of Dadian; I wonder, however, what the matter was at Vulture Peak? Dadian raised his head.
The monk said, "A lute without strings is equal to all others, yet only you, Master, can play it wondrously. Dadian joined his palms. The monk spread out both hands.
Dadian said, "Fortunately you have met an old monk. The monk bowed, and Dadian immediately returned to his quarters. The monk remarked, "Seeking cleverness, one ends up with clumsiness.
The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "Although this monk was capable of engaging in a verbal duel, he did not understand how to deploy his forces.
Dadian was much like lending out uncoined money."
Case: A certain Indian monk came to visit Yangshan. Yangshan drew the shape of a half-moon on the ground;
the monk completed it into a full moon and then wiped it away with his foot. Yangshan then spread out both hands.
The monk said, "A minor Śākyamuni has appeared in this land. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "Yangshan was much like a mute man eating a bitter melon."
A case concerning Chan Master Zhenke of Cuiyan Mountain in Hongzhou.
A monk asked Baling, "What is the Way? Baling said, "A person with clear eyes falls into a well. He then asked Baoying the same question.
"What is the Way? [To this] one should say: "Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion. Again, he asked Shoushan, "What is the Way?
Shoushan said: "Three feet deep underfoot. The Master said: "These three turning words—one phrase stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high;
one phrase is a boat traveling on dry land; one phrase is the mutual interpenetration of guest and host."
Two Cases from the Record of Zen Master Zhizhen of Tōji Kai.
While Yunyan was sweeping the floor, Daowu said, "Why do you trouble yourself so much? Yunyan replied, "You must know that there is one who does not trouble himself.
Daowu said, "If that is so, then there is a second moon. Yunyan held up his broom.
Xuefeng said, "Cloud, which month is this? I shall stop here. Later, Xuansha said, "If I had seen him at that time, I would have told him:
'This is precisely the second moon. Yunmen said, "The master is diligent toward the servant. The Master said: "Using diligence to compensate for clumsiness.
Of these three statements, one sentence can settle the heavens and earth; one sentence can provide verification.
For a patch-robed monk, a single phrase can receive those at the beginning stage of practice. Can you all discern it?
If you can discern it, I grant that you have personally seen Huiguang. If you cannot discern it, do not say that the mountain ranges of Huiguang are steep and perilous.
Gazing across the river from afar, azure clouds part.
[The Master] raised his whisk. Once, while Jia Shan was serving as the head cook at Mount Gui, Mount Gui asked him one day, "What vegetables are we eating today?"
Jiashan said, "Two years share one spring. Guishan said, "Practice the task according to the Dharma. Jiashan said, "The dragon dwells in the phoenix's nest.
The Master [Zhaozhou] said: "Although Jiashan displays his family style, it is beautiful indeed, yet it is not yet skillful."
Huiguang was not like this. His ordinary meals followed the family’s abundance or scarcity. If someone asked, "What vegetables are you eating today?
he would reply, "Either eggplant, or else mustard greens. He prepared his food according to the Dharma, and the five flavors were never lacking.
Now tell me: which is it, Jia Shan or Huiguang?
A Case from Master Changzong Zhaojue of Guanghui Temple on Mount Lu:
The monk asked Zen Master Shanzhao of Fenzhou, "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner? Shanzhao said, "You are a wandering monk.
The monk asked, "What is the phrase for discerning a patch-robed monk? Shanzhao said, "The sun rises in the west at dawn."
"What is the phrase for when the correct command is being carried out? Zhaozhou said, "Traveling a thousand miles, you present your old face.
"What is the phrase for establishing heaven and earth? Zhaozhou said, "In the continent of Uttarakuru, long-grained rice grows; those who eat it have neither greed nor anger.
Fenzhou further remarked, "I shall use these four turning phrases to test the monks of the world. Master [Yunmen]...
[The Master] said: "It is indeed verified. But alas, there is someone who refuses to accept it!
Today, before this great assembly, I dare to offer four alternative turning-words for Fenzhou. What is the phrase for receiving the beginner? The Master said:
'A bottomless alms bowl, its radiance blazing forth. What is the phrase for discerning the monk? The Master said: 'The staff of Tiantai.'"

The *lì* tree has black scales and wrinkled bark. What is the phrase for when the true command is being carried out? The Master said: "Wearing a basin on one's head and a shield on one's belly for three thousand li.
What is the phrase for establishing heaven and earth? The Master said: "When people ask about the heavens, it is the same spring everywhere."
The Master further said: "Fenzhou verifies the patch-robed monks of the world in this manner; Baofeng discerns the Chan practitioners of the seas in this manner.
[Recorded by] Chan Master Wenyue of Nanyue Yunfeng: Five Cases.

Xuansha said, "I knew you would be making your living inside a ghost cave.
Changsheng said, "I am just like this; what about you, Master? Xuansha said, "No one can get out of this."

Case: Master of Fenzhou addressed the assembly: "If you recognize this staff, your journey as a pilgrim is complete.
The Master picked up his staff and said, "Is this not a staff? Which one, then, is your business as a pilgrim?
He further said, "Carrying the knotted staff slung across my shoulder, heedless of others, I go straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks."
Case: Wuye first visited Shitou. As soon as he reached the gate, he said, "If one word accords with you, I shall stay;
if one word does not accord, I shall leave. Shitou sat cross-legged. Wuye brushed his sleeves and walked away.
Shitou then called out, "Dharma Master! Wuye turned his head. Shitou said, "From birth until death, it is only this. Why do you turn your head and look back?"
Thereupon, he had an awakening. The Master said, "The old man Shitou could not sit still and could not hold himself;
he was like a fellow carrying a wooden board. Let him go his way and leave it at that.
Yet I called him back to turn his head, only to have him smeared with tea-soup, saying, 'I have attained enlightenment here. He will dream of this on a donkey-year."
A Case from Master Daopei Huaixiu of Tanzhou:

Yangshan dreamed that he went to the abode of Maitreya, where he was appointed to the second seat. A venerable elder struck the gavel and said, "Now the one on the second seat shall preach the Dharma.
Yangshan rose and struck the gavel, saying: "The vastness of the Dharma transcends the four propositions."
"Severing all hundred-fold negations. Listen attentively! Listen attentively! The Master said: "Yangshan’s interpretation of the meaning according to the text is not without merit;
however, suppose there were a true adept in Maitreya’s assembly who, upon hearing the words 'Mahāyāna Dharma,' immediately said:"
Joining these two pieces of skin together not only puts a stop to Yangshan’s drowsy prattle, but also spares later generations from speaking dreams within dreams.
Three cases concerning Chan Master Tianyi Yihuai of Yuezhou.
Case: Master Xiushan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Cuiyan.
The Master said, "What words or phrases did Cuiyan have for instructing his disciples? The monk said, "The Master usually says, 'When you go out the door, you meet Maitreya;
when you enter the gate, you see Śākyamuni. The Master said, "How can such a statement suffice? The monk then asked, "And what about you, Master?"
The Master said, "When you go out the gate, whom do you meet? When you enter the gate, what do you see? At these words, the monk attained realization.
The Master then said, "Though you have won a moment of glory, you have lopped off a pair of feet. Tell me, where does this lie—in the realm of the guest?
Within the context of a household, if one is destined to emerge from it, one grieves in shared sorrow and rejoices in shared joy. I, this mountain monk, am not like that.
When I go out the door, there are the mountains of Wu and the waters of Chu; when I enter the gate, there are the Buddha halls and the corridors.
Should a patch-robed monk come forth and ask, "What is your Master’s meaning? I would grant him that he possesses the single eye.
Case: Yunmen’s verse says: "Above, one sees no heaven; below, one sees no earth. The throat is blocked;
where can one breathe? Many laugh at me; few smile at me. The Master said: "Yunmen spoke thus, unwittingly turning his cleverness into clumsiness.
I, this mountain monk, am not like that: I look up at the sky and look down at the earth, eating from my own mouth."
Eating rice. Exhaling through the nostrils. The heart bears no grudge against others; the face shows no color of shame.
Case: Zhaozhou sends off a monk. Raising his whisk, he said: "Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell; where there is no Buddha, run past quickly.
When you encounter people three thousand miles away, do not mention this. The monk said, "In that case, I shall not go. Zhaozhou—

[The Master] said, "Plucking willow flowers! Plucking willow flowers! The Teacher said, "Zhaozhou not only wore through the soles of this monk's feet by running away, but he has also silenced this monk's mouth.
If his mouth were not silenced, why would he bring it up whenever he meets someone?"
Two cases concerning Chan Master Shanxian of Kaixian on Mount Lu.
Mingzhao said, "The wind at the peak is quite stiff today; let us go to a warm place to talk. The assembly followed him into the abbot’s quarters.
Mingzhao said, "As soon as we reach this warm place, everyone begins to nod off," and he struck them all at once with his staff.

He drove them away. The Master said, "This would have been to let the prisoners remain incarcerated so they might grow even wiser. At that time, had he waited for him to say, "Today the wind is somewhat stiff;

Case: Jin Shan-zhu asked Chengyuan, "From what do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth arise? Chengyuan said, "They arise from thought.
Jin said, "If a student were to think of a single piece of gold, would he obtain it or not? Chengyuan was speechless. The Master commented:
"Old man Chengyuan thought that by thinking of clarity one could create a land; little did he know that the questioner was like a worm [in the wood]."
Yu Mu replied, "The answerer’s words were merely formed by chance. I, this mountain monk, am not like that. When he says, 'I, a student, have a bar of gold;
have you got it? I simply give him thirty blows of the staff. Why do I act thus? Because when selling gold, one meets a buyer for gold."

Three Cases from Chan Master Fajian Fuhui of Mount Jiangshan in Jiangning Prefecture.
Master Benjing said: "The essence of the Way is fundamentally without cultivation; by not cultivating, one naturally accords with the Way.

Yet people cast aside their single true nature and enter into a world of chaotic clamor. If you encounter a person who cultivates the Way, do not speak of the Way to them first. The Master [Fujian] said: "Mount..."

The Master raised the case, saying: "The wind moves and the heart wavers; the tree stirs and clouds arise, giving rise to dust.
If you understand today's affairs, you darken the person of original nature. The Master said: "Although Master Xiu is most extraordinary, he only knows how to embrace a bridge pillar to wash himself.

Today’s matter: half a catty is eight ounces. [The Master] raised his staff and said:
Xiangyan addressed the assembly, saying, "I have a device: a blink of an eye, a raising of the eyebrows. If there is someone who does not understand this, I will call for the novice. The Master said:
"Although Xiangyan’s compassion is vast and great, did he know that where kindness is excessive, resentment runs deep? Mountain.
The monastic community is not like this. I have a single device; it strikes faster than a flash of lightning. If there is someone who does not understand, there is the golden hammer behind the head.

Case: Nanquan, Guizong, and Magu set out together to pay their respects to the National Teacher.
On the way, Nanquan drew a circle on the ground and said, "If you can speak, then we shall go. Guizong sat down inside the circle; Magu performed a woman’s bow.
Nanquan said, "In that case, we shall not go. Guizong asked, "What was your intention?"
[The monks] depart. The Master picks it up and says: "Guizong and Magu possessed a majestic presence like that of kings, yet they fell into Nanquan’s trap.
At that time, seeing him draw a circle, they simply brushed their sleeves and left. Even if Nanquan had possessed further supernatural powers, they would still have been three thousand li ahead."
Two Cases from the Record of Chan Master Furi Zhicai of Hangzhou.
Linji held his almsbowl and arrived before the gate of an old woman’s house, saying, “A meal for the family. The old woman opened the door and said, “You are truly insatiable!
Linji replied, “I have not yet even received my food; why do you blame me for being insatiable? The old woman then closed the door.
The Master picked up [the case] and said: "Although the old woman’s wit was纵横 (unrestrained and versatile), she still harmed herself.
If Linji had not passed by this person at that moment, she would have been turned outside the threshold. If one wishes to shut Linji’s mouth, one must simply give him food."

Case: Nanquan gave a teaching, saying, "To call it 'Suchness' is already a transformation. People of the present day must walk among the heterodox. Zhaozhou said, "I do not ask about the heterodox; what is the orthodox? Nanquan thrust both hands down to the ground. Zhaozhou then gave him a kick and returned to the Nirvana Hall, saying, "Regret! Regret! The Head Seat asked, "What do you regret? [Zhaozhou replied: "I regret that I did not kick the old fellow over. **Exposition:** Nanquan’s statement, "To call it 'Suchness' is already a transformation," points directly to the fact that as soon as one conceptualizes or names reality, one has already deviated from its true nature.

His instruction for people of the present day to "walk among the heterodox" challenges practitioners to transcend conventional categories and dualistic thinking. When Zhaozhou asks, "I do not ask about the heterodox; what is the orthodox? he seeks the very core of reality beyond all distinctions. Nanquan’s response—thrusting both hands down to the ground—is a direct, non-conceptual demonstration of the Way. Zhaozhou’s subsequent kick is an act of total affirmation and realization; it signifies that he has fully integrated this teaching into his own being. By returning to the Nirvana Hall and crying out "Regret! Regret!", Zhaozhou expresses a profound sense of remorse for having previously failed to recognize this truth.

When the Head Seat asks what he regrets, Zhaozhou clarifies that his regret lies in not having acted with such decisive power against Nanquan earlier. This exchange illustrates the dynamic, non-dual nature of the Zen encounter, where the ultimate is revealed through spontaneous, physical action rather than intellectual discourse.
"What is it? The Governor said, "I regret not having given you another two kicks. The Master commented: "The father is not kind, and the son is not filial;
the deed was done first, and the regret comes later. Even a monk with clear eyes finds it difficult to keep his mouth shut."
Three Cases from the Record of Chan Master Zhengjue of Dongjing Zhikai Benyi.
A monk took his leave of Guizong. Guizong asked, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to study the 'five flavors' of Chan in various quarters.
Guizong said, "I have the 'one flavor' of Chan here; why do you not study it? The monk asked, "What is the Master's one flavor?"
"In this matter, there is only the single flavor of Chan," Mazu said. He then struck him. After a long silence, he asked, "Do you understand?
The monk said, "I understand. Mazu said, "Try to say something then. As the monk prepared to respond, Mazu struck him again.
When Huangbo heard this account related, he said, "Of the eighty-four *kalyāṇamitras* produced by Master Ma, when questioned they all falter and stumble; only Guizong remains."
"The old fellow is still somewhat better. The Master picked up [the case] and said: "Master Huangbo was also fond of forgetting his own ugliness;
he could not restrain his impatience. Old man Guizong’s Chan is of one flavor, yet he unconsciously overdid the salt and vinegar.
This monk met a bare shoulder with a dry stick, simply because all seeking is suffering. There is yet another."
Now, listen as the various quarters pass judgment.
The case is cited: When Master Deshan was unwell, a monk asked him, "Is there anyone who does not exist even in illness? Deshan said:
A monk asked, "What is the one who is not ill? Sanshan said, "Ayé! Ayé! (Ah-ha! The Master [Zhaozhou] commented:
"An adept patriarch does not utter words at random; he is like an archer who hits the mark every time he shoots.
I, however, am not like this. What is the one who is not ill? A runny nose from a cold."
Case: The Monk of Fenzhou held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, "If you recognize this staff, your journey as a wandering monk is complete.
Monk Sanjiao said, "If you recognize this staff, you will enter hell like an arrow shot.
The Master comments: These two elders—one coming out, one going in; half-closing, half-opening—still meet with weapons drawn. As for me, the mountain monk...
Not so. Once you have recognized the staff, the cold light of the painted moon remains; a fragment of autumn cloud shifts as it points toward the sky.
These are two cases cited by Chan Master Chuanzong of Chengtian in Hangzhou.
A monk asked Nanquan, "At the top of a hundred-foot pole, how does one make further progress? Nanquan said, "Take another step forward. The monk...
He asked Salt Official (Yanguan) again. The Official said, "When one is atop a hundred-foot pole, what is the use of taking another step forward?
The monk did not approve; he shook his sleeves and departed. The Official struck him. The Master commented: "If you would study Nanquan, you must take a step forward;
if you would study Yanguan, you must take a step back. Those with clear eyes should discern this."
Case: Yangshan went to Dongsi and asked, "I have come to visit you. The Abbot said, "We have already met; there is no need for you to come up here.
Yangshan said, "If we meet in this way, is that not a mistake? The Abbot then entered his quarters and closed the door.
Later, when Yangshan returned, he related this to Guishan. Guishan asked, "What kind of mental activity was that? Yangshan said, "If it were not..."
"In this way, how can one recognize him? The Master picked up [the case] and said: "Yangshan recognized Dongsi; he was merely expounding principles.
Even if Moshan had gone there in person, he still would not have been able to meet Dongsi."
A Case from the Record of Master Fodeng Dexun of Huilin Monastery in Tokyo:
Baizhang Woshang asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk replied, “From below the mountain.
Baizhang said, “Have you encountered anyone on the way? The monk said, “I have not encountered anyone. Baizhang said, “Why did you not encounter anyone? The monk said, “—”
Whenever he encountered [someone], he would immediately report it to the Abbot. Baizhang said, "Where did you get this news? The Master (Zhaozhou) picked up the point and said:
"Setting aside for a moment the fact that he was not encountered on the mountain below, was he ever encountered on the mountain above?
If he was encountered, then the news from Fenyang has spread throughout all quarters. If he was not encountered, where have you been coming and going?"
Two cases concerning Master Zihong of Ruiyan in Taizhou. Case 1:
Caoshan asked a monk, "The Buddha’s true Dharma-body is like empty space; it manifests forms in response to things, like the moon reflected in water.
Now, how would you describe this 'response'? The monk said, "It is like a donkey looking down a well. Caoshan said, "You have only described the donkey."
[The monk] attained eighty percent. The Master said, "I ask the Teacher to speak the Way in its entirety. Caoshan said, "It is like looking at a donkey from within a well.
The Master said, "This monk has only spoken half; Caoshan has only attained eighty percent. If you wish to attain the Way in its entirety, it is like looking at a well from within a well."
Case: When Minister Chen Cao asked a fellow practitioner-monk, "Is it permissible for me to discuss a certain matter with you, elder brother?
the monk replied, "Shut your dog's mouth! The Minister then slapped his own mouth once and said, "I am at fault. The monk said, [nothing further].
"One who knows their transgressions must surely reform them. As the Book of Documents says: "It is so. [The Master] said, "I beg my elder brother to eat rice from his own mouth.

The Master took up the case and said: "Chen Cao indeed knew how to brandish his sword before the skull and let forth light behind the cranium. Yet this monk, though he entered the tiger's den, did not get the tiger's cub."
Four Cases from the Record of Zen Master Foyun Fashu of Dongting.
Zhuangyan addressed the assembly, saying: "All of you, do not try to drive a stake into empty space.
The Venerable Lingxu stepped forth from the assembly and said, "Is it space? Is it the stake? Zhuangyan struck him. Lingxu said, "Master, do not..."
He struck the monk and said, "Zhu-yu, put down your staff," and then returned to his quarters. The Master commented: "Zhu-yu knew only how to look ahead;
this monk was unable to look behind. If one examines them closely, both would deserve a beating.
But tell me, where does the fault lie? Let those with the eye of discernment distinguish it."
Case: Yushan visited Shitou and asked, "I have a rough understanding of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.

The Master said, "Even if the entire great earth were to be universally exhorted to become Buddhas, they would still not have dreamed of seeing the heels of this mountain monk's feet. Fayan said, "If one sees that all marks are non-marks..."
[The student] replied, "Then I do not see the Tathāgata. The Master said, "Even so, you have not yet avoided being like a leaning post.
The former master said, "If one sees that all marks are non-marks, where are the eyes? These words contain two points of defeat.

The mountain stream. Behind it rises a high mountain ten thousand fathoms tall. If you do not see it, I shall explain it anew for all of you:
The slender bamboo possesses lofty integrity; the idle clouds have no fixed mind.
Two cases concerning Master Qingman of Yuanfeng in Weizhou.
Fayan asked Master Xiu: "A hair's breadth of difference results in worlds apart. How do you understand this?"
The Master said, "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth. Fayan said, "Even if you understand it this way, how can you attain it?
The Master said, "I am just like this; what about you, Elder Brother? Fayan said, "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth."
Heaven and earth were as far apart as could be. The Abbot then prostrated himself. The Master said, "Alas!
Great Master Xuyou has had his eyes replaced by a clay pellet. Do you know this? Furthermore, to prostrate yourself behind me is merely to cultivate causes and increase wisdom."
Case: Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying, "On the southern mountain there is a tortoise-nosed snake; you all must look at it very carefully.
The Master then held his staff crosswise and said, "Let me further add feet to the mountain monk’s snake for you."
A Case from the Record of Zen Master Furi Weiyue of Jingyin Temple in Tokyo:
A Teaching states, "When knowledge and views establish further knowing, this is the root of ignorance; when knowledge and views are devoid of seeing, this is nirvana.
I, this mountain monk, do not agree. Today, I wish to contend with the Old Śākyamuni and provide another interpretation for you all.
This news: when knowledge and views are established, knowledge is precisely ignorance; fundamentally, knowledge and views are non-existent, and seeing this is precisely Nirvana.
If you say that the clouds and moon are the same, I grant that you, Elder Brother, have understood the Tathāgata-dhyāna.
But if you say that the streams and mountains are each distinct, you have not even dreamed of the Patriarchal-dhyāna.

Caoshan said, "You must know that Caoshan is a master craftsman. The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, am not like that.

Three Cases from Chan Master Jia Shan Ziliang of Liuzhou.
At a gathering of the Tathāgata at the Heavenly King’s Palace, there was a woman who entered meditative absorption before the World-Honored One.
The Buddha commanded Mañjuśrī to bring this woman out of her absorption. Mañjuśrī then snapped his fingers once and, with his hand, lifted her up to the Brahma Heaven.
"It is impossible to bring this woman out of this samādhi. The World-Honored One said, "Below there is the Bodhisattva Jālinīprabha who can bring her out of this samādhi;
you must wait for him. When Jālinīprabha arrived, he snapped his fingers once, and the woman emerged from samādhi and departed. The Master said:
There is no *kōan* concerning Zhe that one does not understand thoroughly. Why was Mañjuśrī unable to emerge from it, while Jālinīprabha was able to emerge?
If you all possess eyes that can pass through a rushing torrent or a blade, you will not only see this band of fellows defeated at the barrier;
even if as many patriarchs and Buddhas as there are sands in the Ganges were to appear, they too would be seen through by a master. Otherwise, whether [the world appears] green or yellow...
He did not discern it; he could not distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, but merely went on searching for the woman who had emerged from meditative absorption.

This is the "bottom line" of Xuansha. The case is cited: Nanquan addressed the assembly, saying, "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra—last night at the third watch, I gave each of you twenty blows and have sent you out of the monastery.
Zhaozhou stepped forward from the crowd and asked, "Whom does the Master intend for the blows to fall upon? Nanquan replied, "The King."
"Where does the Master's fault lie? Zhaozhou then prostrated. The Master said, "Nanquan displayed his brilliance for a moment, yet he could not avoid piling up earth on level ground.
Although Zhaozhou met the situation face-to-face, he could not avoid striking his forehead against the earth."
Case: Zhaozhou saw the temple steward delivering cooked rice to the crows. Suddenly, they all flew away. Zhaozhou asked, "Crows, why did you fly away upon seeing me?
The steward replied, "I was afraid of you. Zhaozhou said, "That is quite a statement. The steward said, [nothing further].

A Case from Master Xinyin of Kaixian on Mount Lu:
A monk asked Touzi, "When it is said that 'the lamp of endless transmission has been passed down through successive kalpas, never trimmed and always brightly shining,' what is this?
Touzi replied, "The lamp of endless transmission has been passed down through successive kalpas, never trimmed and always brightly shining."
The Master picked up the topic, saying: "Since the question is thus, the answer is likewise. Why is it that when the eastern neighbor lights his lamp, the western neighbor sits in darkness?
Let those with clear eyes try to discern this."

From the *Jinggu Men*:
Chan Master Chongxian Mingjue of Mount Xuedou in Mingzhou (Twenty Cases). Case One:
Emperor Wu of the Liang Dynasty asked the Great Master Bodhidharma, "What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths? Bodhidharma [replied].
He said, "Vast and empty—there is no sage. The Emperor asked, "Who is it that faces me? Bodhidharma replied, "I do not know.
The Emperor did not attain realization and subsequently crossed the river to go to Wei. Emperor Wu raised the matter with Master Zhi, who asked, "Your Majesty, do you recognize this man?
The Emperor said, "I do not recognize him. Master Zhi said, "This is the Great Being Avalokiteśvara, who transmits the Buddha’s Mind-Seal."
The Emperor repented and subsequently dispatched a messenger to retrieve him. Master Zhi said, "Do not say that Your Majesty has sent a messenger to fetch me;
even if everyone in the entire kingdom were to go, he would still not return."
The Noble Truths are vast and open; when could they ever be defined? "Who is it facing me? he replied, "I do not know.

From this, he crossed the river in darkness; how could he avoid being caught in deep thorns? The entire nation pursued him, but he would not return; for a thousand ages and ten thousand generations, we can only remember him in vain.
"Cease your recollections. When the pure wind pervades the earth, what limit can there be? The Master looked to his left and right and said, "Is there a Patriarch here?
He then said himself, "There is. Call him here to wash the old monk's feet."
Case: Zhaozhou addressed the assembly, saying, "The ultimate Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes discrimination. As soon as there is speech, there is discrimination;
there is clarity. I, the old monk, do not abide within clarity. Do you all, sirs, still cherish and protect it?
At that time, a monk asked, "If you do not abide within clarity, what is it that you cherish and protect? Zhaozhou—
Yun said, "I do not know either. The monk asked, "Since you, Master, do not know, why did you say it is not within clarity?
Yun said, "It is permissible to ask about the matter; after prostrating, withdraw."
The Ultimate Way is not difficult: speak with integrity and act with integrity. One may have many aspects, yet two are never of two kinds. At the edge of heaven, the sun rises;
beneath the moon, the water is deep and cold before the railing. When the consciousness of the skull is exhausted, what joy can there be to establish?
When the dragon roars from the withered tree, the moisture has not yet dried. Difficult! Difficult! Discernment and clarity—you must see for yourself.
Case: Master Yunmen gave this teaching, saying: "I will not question you regarding the period before the fifteenth day;
tell me a phrase for the period after the fifteenth day. [The Master] spoke on his own behalf, saying: "Every day is a good day."
Setting aside one, he grasps seven; above, below, and in the four quarters, there is no equal. Walking slowly, he tramples the sound of flowing water;
gazing afar, he traces the tracks of soaring birds. The grass is lush and thick; smoke mists the air. Wildflowers grow profusely along the crags of the empty mountain.
A snap of the fingers is enough to evoke pity for the *śūnyatā* (void) spirit. Do not touch it; if you touch it, you shall receive thirty blows. [The Master] raised [his staff].
Emperor Suzong asked National Teacher Huizhong, "What do you require after a hundred years?

The National Teacher said, "Have a seamless stupa made for this old monk. The Emperor said, "Please show me the model of the stupa. After a long silence, the National Teacher said, "Do you understand?"
The Emperor said, "I do not understand. The National Teacher said, "I have a Dharma-heir disciple, Tan-yuan, who is well-versed in this matter.
I request that you issue an imperial decree to question him. After the National Teacher passed away, Emperor Suzong issued a decree for Tan-yuan to inquire about the meaning of these words.
Tan-yuan said, "South of Xiang, north of Tan. (The Master said: A single palm does not clap recklessly. Within it lies gold in abundance."
In a single realm (a mountain-shaped staff), beneath the shadowless tree, they board the same boat (the seas are calm and the rivers clear).
Upon the lapis lazuli palace, there is no one with whom to recognize [the truth] (it has already been picked up).
The seamless stupa is difficult to behold once seen. The clear depths do not permit the azure dragon to coil within. Its tiers stand tall and distinct; its reflection is round and full.
For ten thousand ages, through all eternity, it remains for people to gaze upon.
Case: Longya asked Cuibei, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Cuiwei said, "Give me the meditation board.
Longya took the meditation board and gave it to Cuiwei. Cuiwei took it and struck him. Longya said, "I am willing to be struck, but there is still no meaning of the Patriarch.
He then asked Linji, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
Yanguan said, "Hand me the meditation cushion over here. Yanguan took the cushion and gave it to Linji; as soon as Linji received it, he struck him.
Yanguan said, "I am willing enough to be struck, but you still lack the meaning of the Patriarch."
In the mountains of Longya, the dragon has no eyes; how could stagnant water ever stir the ancient wind?
The meditation board and the grass mat can no longer be used; they should surely be entrusted to Master Lu.
Again it was said: "The old fellow has not yet been completely eradicated.

Even if Master Lu has finished his transmission, what reliance can there be? Sitting back and leaning against [the wall], do not attempt to continue the ancestral lamp. Facing the evening clouds, it is not yet time to return;
the distant mountains stretch on endlessly, layer upon layer of azure."

"It is so," [the monk] said. The monk asked, "How about you, Master? Yunmen replied, "What use is Nanshan?

Elephant Bone Rock—high, where men do not go. Those who reach it must be snake-handlers. Masters Leng and Master Bei could do nothing about it;

Suddenly emerging from the head of the staff, he hurls it toward Xuefeng’s wide-open mouth. Wide open his mouth—it is the same as...
A flash of lightning! Even when you raise your eyebrows, it is not yet seen. Now it is hidden before the peaks of the breasts;
let every visitor examine the skillful means. The Master raised his voice and shouted, "Look beneath your feet!"
Case: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall? Yunmen said, "The body is exposed to the golden wind.
Since the question has its principle, the answer likewise shares that same essence; the three phrases can be discerned. One arrowhead pierces the vast void.
Across the great wilds, the cool breezes rustle; beneath the long sky, the sparse rain mists. Do you not see the traveler who has sat for a long time at Shaolin and has yet to return?
Quietly relying on the Bear Ear Mountains, one cluster after another.
[The Master] raised his staff. Nanquan went to visit the Venerable Nianbo of Baizhang. Baizhang asked, "Among all the sages of the past, was there any Dharma that they did not preach for others?
Nanquan said, "There was. Baizhang asked, "What is this Dharma that was not preached for others?"
Dafu asked, "Is it not mind? Is it not Buddha? Is it not an object? Zhaozhou said, "It has already been explained.
Dafu asked, "I am just like this; how about you, Master? Zhaozhou said, "I am no *shanzhishi* (good spiritual friend).
How could I know whether there is something to say or not? Dafu said, "I do not understand. Zhaozhou said, "I have explained it quite thoroughly for you."

You have spoken it. Since ancient times, the Buddhas have never acted for the sake of others; monks of past and present have vied with one another in their frantic running. A bright mirror stands upon its stand, reflecting diverse forms;
each and every one looks south to see the Northern Dipper. The handle of the dipper hangs down—nowhere can it be sought. Having grasped the nostrils, one has lost them.
[The Master] raised his whisk. The Senior Seat-holder Ding asked Linji, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?

Linji descended from his meditation seat, seized him, gave him a slap, and then pushed him away. Ding stood there motionless. A monk standing nearby said, "Senior Seat-holder Ding, why do you not bow?"
Prostrations. While prostrating in a fixed direction, he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
Duanji’s total functioning continues the legacy; why must one wait for leisure to uphold it? When the Great Spirit raises his hand, there is nothing more to it than this:
he splits apart the myriad layers of Mount Hua.
Case: Panshan gave this hanging word: "The three realms have no dharma; where can one seek the mind? The three realms have no dharma;
where can one seek the mind? White clouds serve as a canopy, and flowing springs act as a zither. One tune, two tunes—no one understands them.
After the rain has passed, the autumn waters in the night pond are deep."
Case: A monk asked Yunmen, “What is the pure Dharma-body? Yunmen said, “A flower garden fence.
The monk asked, “What about when one goes directly like this? Yunmen said, “A golden-maned lion.”
Flowers and medicinal herbs in the railing—do not be coarse or vague. When the stars are on the scale, they are not on the pan. To act thus is utterly groundless.
Behold, all of you, the golden-maned lion!
Case: When Grand Master Lu Xun was conversing with Nanquan, he said, "Dharma Master Zhao says that heaven and earth share the same root and all things are one body;
how truly marvelous! Nanquan pointed to a flower in the courtyard and called out to the Grand Master, saying, "When people of this age see this single stalk of flowers, it is like being in a dream."
Hearing, seeing, perceiving, and knowing are not each separate; mountains and rivers do not reside within the mirror.
When the moon sets in the frosty sky and night is half spent, who will share this cold reflection in the clear pool?
Case: A monk asked Master Dongshan, “When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them?
Dongshan said, “Why not go to a place where there is no cold or heat? The monk asked, “What is the place where there is no cold or heat?
Dongshan said, “When it is cold, it kills you with cold; when it is hot, it kills you with heat.”
Hanging down one’s hand is the same as a precipice ten thousand fathoms high; why must the "Correct" and "Deviant" be contrived? In the ancient palace of lapis lazuli, the bright moon shines;
yet the clever hound merely paces up the steps in vain.
Case: Jingqing asked a monk, "What is that sound outside the gate? The monk said, "The sound of raindrops. Jingqing said, "Sentient beings are deluded;
they lose themselves and pursue external objects. The monk asked, "How about you, Master? Jingqing said, "I have not lost myself."
The monk said, "I have not lost my way; what is the meaning of this? Qing said, "To emerge from the body may still be easy, but to shed the very essence of the Way is difficult.
The sound of raindrops in an empty hall—how can a true adept respond to this? If you claim you have entered the stream, you still do not understand as before."
"Will it not? On the southern mountains and northern mountains, the rain falls ever more profusely.
[The Master] raised his staff. Once, while Mazu Daoshi and Baizhang were walking along, they saw wild ducks fly past.
Mazu asked, "What is that? Baizhang said, "Wild ducks. Mazu asked, "Where have they gone? Baizhang said, "They flew past."
"It has flown away! The Master then pinched Baizhang’s nose. Baizhang let out a cry of pain.
Dayue said, "When did it ever fly away?
Wild ducks—where do you think they go? Mazu saw him coming and spoke with him; their conversation exhausted all sentiments regarding mountain clouds and ocean moons.
Relying on his previous failure to understand, he flew away again. As he was about to fly away, [the Master] seized him and said, "Speak! Speak! He then raised the case:
An outsider asked the Buddha, "I do not ask for words; I do not ask for wordlessness. The World-Honored One remained silent for a long while.
The outsider praised him, saying, "The World-Honored One, with great kindness and great compassion, has cleared away my clouds of delusion and enabled me to enter. The outsider...
After he had departed, Ānanda asked the Buddha, "What realization did these outsiders possess that they claimed to have entered [the path]?
The Buddha said, "They were like fine horses that move at the mere sight of the shadow of the whip."
The pivot-wheel has never yet turned; once it turns, it must run in both directions. When the bright mirror suddenly confronts the stand, beauty and ugliness are distinguished in that very moment.
Once beauty and ugliness are distinguished, the clouds of delusion disperse. In the Gate of Compassion, how could there be any dust?

Reflecting on this, I think of the fine horse that, upon catching a glimpse of the whip’s shadow, pursues the wind for a thousand li and is called back. "Called back!"—he snaps his fingers three times.
Case: One day, Master Yanguan called to his attendant, "Bring me the rhinoceros fan.
The attendant said, "The fan is broken. Yanguan said, "Since the fan is broken, bring me back the rhinoceros. The attendant was speechless.
Touzi said, "I would not refuse to bring it out, but I fear its horns and head are incomplete. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "I want one that is not..."
"His entire head and horns [are gone]. Shishuang said, "If it were the Master, there would be none at all.
The Master commented, "The rhinoceros calf is still here. Zifu drew a perfect circle and wrote the character for "ox" inside it.
The Master commented, "Why did you not bring it out just now? Baofu said, "The Master is advanced in years; it would be better to invite someone else. The Master...
The Master held up the whisk and said: "A pity that labor was expended without merit.
The rhinoceros fan has been used for so long; when questioned, it turns out one knows nothing at all.

Infinite cool breezes and its horned head have all vanished with the clouds and rain, difficult to pursue again. The Master spoke further: "If you wish for the cool breeze to cover once more, you must restore the horned head."
Sheng invited a Zen guest to offer a turning word. He asked: "The fan has already been broken; now I ask you to return my rhinoceros calf to me.
At that time, a monk came forward and said: "Great assembly, go to the hall for practice. The Master said: "I cast my hook to catch the giant *kūṇī* and *tīrī* whales;
instead, I have caught a mere frog."
Case: One day the World-Honored One ascended the seat. Mañjuśrī struck the mallet and said, "Contemplate clearly the Dharma of the Dharma-King;
such is the Dharma of the Dharma-King. Thereupon, the World-Honored One descended from the seat.
Among the gathered assembly, only the master knows; the Dharma-king’s teaching does not proceed in such a manner.
If there were a śrāmaṇera among those present, why would it have been necessary for Mañjuśrī to strike but one blow?
Citing three turning phrases from Zhaozhou’s address to the assembly:
"The clay Buddha does not cross the water; the divine light illuminates heaven and earth. If one stands in the snow without ceasing, who would not abandon artifice?"
The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; when people come to visit Zihu, there are several children within the signboard—where is the pure breeze not present?
The wooden Buddha does not pass through the fire; I always think of Paozhuo’s fall. When the staff suddenly strikes, one finally realizes they have betrayed me.
Recorded: Emperor Suzong asked National Teacher Huizhong, "What is the Tamer of the Ten Bodies?
The Master said, "Donor, you are walking upon the crown of Vairocana’s head. The Emperor said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Do not mistake your own self for the Pure Dharma-body."
The teacher of a nation is merely a strong designation; only Nan-yang was permitted to spread his illustrious reputation.
The Great Tang supported the true Son of Heaven, who once trod upon the crown of Vairocana.
The iron hammer shatters the golden bones; what else remains between heaven and earth? The ocean of three thousand lands is serene and clear at night;
who knows who has entered the blue dragon’s cave?
Case 1: Chan Master Chiming Chuyuan of Shishuang in Tanzhou (Three Cases).
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? Yunmen said, "Steamed buns."

Transcending Buddhas and surpassing patriarchs—how can this be proclaimed? At the memorial feast, one eats fill-the-bowl steamed buns to one’s heart’s content. In Hunan they spread out their alms bowls;
in Silla they gnaw on them. The Arabs and Persians seek a ferryboat.
Case: A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? Ming said, "Water flows from a high source.
"Water flowing from a high source—how marvelous! If practitioners do not understand this, their eyes are utterly bewildered.
If you have not yet clarified this phrase of mud and water, the lanterns and pillars will laugh with joyful ease.
Case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou said, “The cypress tree in the courtyard.
Zhaozhou’s cypress in the courtyard has caused Zen travelers to run all over the world. When raising a child, do not let him grow too big; once he is grown, he becomes a master thief.
Three Cases from Master Huanglong Huinan of Hongzhou.
On the road to Mount Tai there was an old woman. Whenever a traveling monk asked, "Where does the road to Mount Tai go?
the woman would point her finger and say, "Go straight ahead. Just as the monk was about to depart, she would say, "What a fine monk!"
Furthermore, when he went away in such a manner, Zhaozhou heard it mentioned and said, "The next day, upon ascending the hall, I have already scrutinized and seen through this old woman.
Outstanding in the monastic community is Zhaozhou; there is a reason why the old woman was scrutinized. Now, the four seas are as clear as—
Mirror. Travelers, do not treat the road as your enemy. Lifting [the case]:
National Teacher Zhong called his attendant three times. The attendant responded three times. The Master said, "I thought it was I who had failed you;
it turns out it was you who failed me."

The National Teacher called his attendant three times; in striking the grass, he sought only to startle the snake. Who would have known that beneath the green pines at the bottom of the ravine lies a thousand-year-old *fuling* fungus?
The National Teacher’s words were never uttered in vain; yet the attendant, though called three times, gave no response. His lifelong heart and gallbladder were thus revealed to others.
Tilting. It is better not to know someone than to know them as they truly are.
Case: Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Have you ever been here before? The monk said, "I have. Zhaozhou said, "Go drink tea."
He asked another monk, "Have you ever been here before? The monk said, "No. Zhaozhou said, "Go have some tea.

This is the point where Zhaozhou scrutinizes people with absolute precision; were it not for his casual opening of the mouth that allows one to know him, and his direct gaze with its clear distinction between the blue and white eyes, how could the wind of the ancestral school have reached the present day?
Meeting and exchanging greetings, they learn each other’s origins; without distinguishing between kin and stranger, tea is served at once.
One cannot help but recall those who come and go in constant bustle—amidst such frantic haste, who can discern the blossoms filling the bowl?
Tokyo Chikai’s *Muzhe Zhenru Chan Shi* (Two Cases).
Case: Master Guishan addressed the assembly, saying: "After I am gone, I shall become a water buffalo on the mountain below.
On its left flank, I will write five characters that say: 'The monk so-and-so of Guishan. At that time, if you call it 'Guishan,'..."
This mountain monk is also a water buffalo. If you call me a water buffalo, I am a water buffalo; yet if you call me a monk of Mount Gui, how can that be right?
With hooves and horns clearly defined, he reaches everywhere; there is no need for supervision and no need for restraint—just know not to tread upon another's sprouts.
*Jia*: Water plants obtain freedom according to the seasons.
*Ju*: Yantou Han was a ferryman at Yangyang. On both sides of the river, north and south of Jiangnan, he had wooden planks suspended.
Those seeking a crossing would knock on a plank once. One day, an old woman carrying a baby knocked on the plank to request passage. Yantou—
From within the thatched hut, he emerged dancing with his oar. The old woman then asked, "I do not ask about your presenting the oar and dancing;
but from where did you get this child in your hand? Yantou struck her with the oar. The old woman said, "I have given birth to seven sons;
